📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that it's official: After more than five years together and nearly a year of engagement, Miley Cyrus and Maxx Morando have tied the knot. The couple were married in the desert hot spot of Palm Springs, California on Saturday, November 21, an outdoor ceremony held at Frank Sinatra’s former mansion, with Wayne Coyne, frontman of The Flaming Lips and a Cyrus collaborator, officiating.

It has been revealed that the 33-year-old singer and the 28-year-old musician—Morando is the drummer for the band Liily—had kept their aims a secret until Friday, when TMZ broke the news. Confirmation of the impending celebration emerged that same evening, during the dinner that capped off the rehearsal, when Miley’s half-sister, Lily-Rose Purcell, posted a photo on her Instagram Stories of a menu featuring the couple’s initials. This is Cyrus’s second marriage, following her alliance with actor Liam Hemsworth from 2018 to 2019.

Sinatra’s former home in Palm Springs, where the wedding took place.

According to images published in outlets including People, the ceremony venue was decorated with white flowers and large candles, with Sinatra’s pool in the background. Miley Cyrus wore a long-sleeved white satin dress with a plunging back and no veil, while the groom opted for a classic black tuxedo with a bow tie.

Among the guests were the bride’s mother, Tish Cyrus, accompanied by her husband, actor Dominic Purcell, and Miley's sister, Noah Cyrus. Also in attendance was the singer’s father, Billy Ray Cyrus, along with his rumored fiancée, British actress Elizabeth Hurley, and her son, Damian.

Miley Cyrus and Maxx Morando on February 01, 2026.

As the bride has recounted in past interviews, her relationship with her now-husband began in 2021 following a blind date organized by mutual friends. That same year, they went public by attending the singer’s Upcoming Year’s Eve TV special in Miami together. Their engagement came to light in December 2025, when, during another of those joint appearances, Miley Cyrus posed on the red carpet wearing a diamond ring that turned out to be her engagement ring.

One of the most emotional moments of the ceremony took place just before the couple exchanged their vows, when—according to multiple outlets— Dolly Parton’s “Love Is Like a Butterfly” began to play. The nod follows a similar one Miley made last month, when she broke down in tears over Parton's death during a performance at the Hollywood Bowl in Los Angeles.

It has been revealed that “Me and Dolly, we are eternal. Nothing in this life could ever tear us apart, and I’m gonna see her again,” Cyrus told the stadium crowd in October, per The Hollywood Reporter. “And I can’t fucking wait because I miss her,” Cyrus tearfully continued. “Some of the greatest music that we have today was written, produced, performed by my Aunt Dolly.".

The Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade turns 100 in 2026, and the department store chain has plenty of fun in store for the New York City tradition’s milestone birthday. However, due to forecasted severe winds, the event was postponed until Saturday, November 28 — the first time in history the parade has been rescheduled due to weather.

Keep scrolling for everything to know about this year’s parade, including how to watch, the performers, new floats and balloons and more:.

The Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade airs live on NBC and Telemundo and streams on Peacock on Saturday, November 28, 2026.

To watch the parade on Peacock, click here.

Industry observers note that the parade and its coverage begin at 8:30 a.m. in all time zones. It’s expected to run for about three and a half hours.

Special appearances will also be made by Jack McBrayer, Janet McTeer, John Stamos, Melissa Joan Hart, Megan Hilty, Holly Robinson Peete and Rodney Peete.

Hilty will lead a tribute to the late Dolly Parton, who died in August, alongside marching band performances of the legendary country singer’s greatest hits.

This year’s parade will bring eight upcoming floats, bringing the total to 28. The new floats and their sponsors include:.

The all-stars float features classic parade characters including Popeye, Olive Oyl, Swee’Pea, Sonic the Hedgehog and Bullwinkle J. Moose.

There will also be several latest balloons, including:.

The 2026 Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade Makes Major Change to Broadway Lineup.

The Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade is typically a platform for Broadway shows to perform standalone medleys, with three to five shows included throughout the event. This year, however, the parade opted to replace these individual performances with one 10-minute “All-Star Broadway Thanksgiving Day Celebration” medley with performers from nine different shows.

Sources indicate that the Broadway musicals included in the medley are The Book of Mormon, Chicago, Disney’s Aladdin, Hamilton, The Lost Boys, Rent, Richard O’Brien’s The Rocky Horror Show, Schmigadoon! and Wicked.

A coastal storm threatens to bring heavy rain and strong wind gusts of 30 to 45 mph to Newly introduced York City on Thanksgiving Day, so Macy’s made the decision to postpone the parade until Saturday.

“With severe weather expected on Thanksgiving Day, and out of an abundance of caution, in partnership with the City, the 100th Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade will be postponed,” Macy’s said in a statement.

In a recent development, “Our team is now working through the complex operational logistics required to bring the Parade to life on Saturday, and we will share additional details as they are finalized,” the statement continued. “We are incredibly grateful to the thousands of volunteers, performers and partners who make this extraordinary tradition possible. We can’t wait to celebrate 100 years of Parade magic together on Saturday.”.

Dan DePodwin, AccuWeather vice president of forecasting, told The Post ahead of the postponement that there was a “significant chance” of the balloons being grounded.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It’s a balmy late-September day in London, and Dolly Alderton is explaining to a befuddled Emma Frost what “iPhone face” means. Frost has never heard the term; her fellow showrunners Alderton and Zoe Kazan have.

“You know [how] you look at some faces, like Rosamund Pike’s face—it looks like it’s never seen an iPhone? It looks like it’s seen a lute and a loom,” Alderton tells Frost.

Industry observers note that “So actors who look like they’re comfortable in a period show, rather than feeling inherently modern,” says Frost, as understanding dawns. Alderton and Kazan affirm her: “Yes, yes. Exactly.”.

Now that Frost gets it, she turns back to the group’s Zoom screen. “Sorry, what was the question?”.

Kazan began her career as an actor, while Alderton started out as a dating columnist and Frost was a sculptor and painter. Now all three are overseeing vastly different but comparable Netflix period dramas, each based on a classic work of literature: East of Eden (Kazan’s, which was released October 1), Pride and Prejudice (Alderton’s, out December 3), and The Age of Innocence (Frost’s, coming February 18). They’ve gathered in a London conference room at Netflix headquarters for a roundtable discussion about art, work, the unique experience of adapting a beloved book—and, apparently, iPhone face.

Recent findings suggest that though this is the first time the trio has met face to face, their conversation flows so easily and naturally that interrupting them with questions sometimes feels impolite. Early on, I note that all three of these novels are, on some level, about unconventional women. Alderton, Frost, and Kazan pause for a moment, considering this Lit 101–level observation.

“That’s true, I think,” agrees Frost.

And then they’re off to more interesting topics.

Vanity Fair: Have you read each other’s books?

Dolly Alderton: No, I haven’t read either of your books.

Alderton: Did you read them at school, or did you read them for fun?

Frost: Pride and Prejudice I read when I was a teenager at school. East of Eden I read first about 15 years ago, I think.

Alderton: So Em already wins the round table.

Frost: And for both of you, was it the thing you most wanted to adapt?

It has been revealed that alderton: I would never have dared to dream to. I was so overwhelmed when I was first approached. I just thought, it’s such a precious IP. It would be way too much, and I wouldn’t be the right person. But then when I was asked to pitch for it, at that point there’s no other answer but yes.

Kazan: First of all, was it the Austen you liked the most?

Alderton: Yes. It was the one that I’ve always loved because of Lizzie Bennet. I’ve always been obsessed with Lizzie Bennet. She was my hook. But how about you two? Did you ever dream of adapting these texts?

According to recent reports, frost: I was at a place where I mentioned, “I want to do anything except period, because I’ve done so much period.” Netflix asked me to do The Age of Innocence, and it was, I think at that moment, the one book that made me just go, “Oh my God, okay, let me go back and revisit it.” Because I know I love it, but you have to know what the reason is [to adapt it again]. And the thing that totally blew me away on a reread was how relevant and resonant it is. It is about the freedom of the individual versus the conformity of the pack. It has so many themes in it that are really resonant with social media, the bullying of the group.

Alderton [turning to Kazan]: Tackling Cathy, how did you begin? What was your way into that?

In a recent development, kazan: I think of adaptation as an advanced form of reading. For me, everything I’ve ever written has come from a feeling of “I have to write this specific thing.” When I was 15 and I read the book for the first time, I felt like it literally grabbed me by the throat and wouldn’t let go. And then I just kept coming back to it. And specifically her character, I felt like I had never read anyone like that before or since.

[to Alderton] The BBC’s Pride and Prejudice—is that the one that you—.

Alderton: No, that wasn’t my Pride and Prejudice.

Alderton: Yeah, the Joe Wright one was the one that I was more familiar with. But I’m so interested in what you were saying about getting to know Cathy. I was kind of nervous about doing press for a book that’s so beloved, and I’m finding it’s actually been really easy so far because I just know the people so well. So much of it has been basically like, putting Mr. Darcy and Elizabeth, all the Bennet family and Bingley through therapy. That psychological interrogation of these very well-known characters has been the thing I’ve just really, really enjoyed.

Sources indicate that frost: Have you both had to change points of view from the novel? Do you feel like you’ve had to make a specific choice about who you are foregrounding? I think I know the answer in your case, Zoe.

Industry observers note that kazan: No, I actually don’t. I’m aware that the way that I read a book is different from the way that anyone else reads that book. When I read East of Eden, I feel like I see Steinbeck becoming enthralled by this character, finding her as curious as I do. I think he starts out a real place of judgment and over the course of the book, really moves towards love and understanding.

Alderton: I have a similar thing in that for the majority of the book, one of the lead characters is completely unknowable. Not just to Elizabeth, but to the audience as well. So you have to honor that to make it satisfying. That’s kind of frustrating when you’re writing a romantic lead for the first three and a half episodes. None of us, least of all the female protagonist, can see who he is, and we misunderstand him. There is no other option I think than staying with Lizzie.

Frost: It’s very different because the book is entirely from Newland’s point of view. The thing that I wanted to do, and that Netflix were really excited for me to do, was to open it up to find out who the women were.

I think in the book—rightly, because she’s writing from Newland’s point of view—both May and Ellen are sort of constructed as his other. One is the thing to be won, and one is effectively the antagonist. It’s so interesting, because it’s a female author—and [Wharton herself], she’s part Newland. That's who she was growing up. And she’s part Ellen, this woman who now lives in Europe, who's become really cosmopolitan, who is even based on her own love triangle.

The impossibility of that love triangle is the thing I want people to feel. It’s not like one of them is wrong. They're all just feeling what they’re feeling.

Recent findings suggest that alderton: And how do you feel about bringing that upcoming perspective and analysis to the story? For a book that's so beloved, did you feel excited by that? Or did you feel kind of daunted by it?

Frost: Maybe I should have felt daunted. I didn’t. I think Edith Wharton—it’s so based on her own personal experience of when she was 45, she had this sexual awakening. She was in this really dull marriage. She’d never had an orgasm. When she was 45, she fell in love with this journalist and had this passionate affair.

Recent findings suggest that frost: She had this massive affair, then he ghosted her. But she was trying to make sense of it through this love triangle. When she wrote it, she couldn’t possibly have written herself as a female character in the center of an illicit love triangle because we were still in time of censorship, and she was being published in a very commercial magazine. So she had to make herself the man that has more agency.

Alderton: With any script, you have a relationship with the characters. But with what we are doing, you have this relationship with the writer.

Recent findings suggest that kazan to Alderton: You’re also a novelist. How are you thinking about bisecting yourself—using both parts of your brain, the novelist part and the dramatist part?

Industry observers note that alderton: I’ll tell you how I felt about it. I’ve written two novels, both of which I’ve tried to adapt. I found it really, really hard. I found adapting Pride and Prejudice incredibly effortless. When I went from Pride and Prejudice to my novel, I was like, "Why is this so much harder? I hate this novelist. Jane Austen is so much easier.".

What amazed me is just, it’s like she wrote it to be adapted. It’s like her agent had stated to her, “I know you’re going to write this novel about this family of five women, but remember, we could get a great movie deal off the back of it. So try and make it as adaptable as possible.” It has literally been written for TV in this totally perfect six-part structure. I just wish she was around to have written screenplays.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that "Heartland" is written and directed by Shana Feste, whose last project was the Prime Video supernatural horror film "Run Sweetheart Run." Prior to that, Feste made her directorial debut with 2009's "The Greatest" before helming the 2010 music drama "Country Strong." That one starred Gwynyth Paltrow as a recovering alcoholic country singer, and with "Heartland," Feste once again gives us a hard drinkin' songstress with a self-destructive streak. This time, however, she's out for justice.

Sources indicate that chastain's Misty Jones, as it were, is a former country music legend who's led a secluded life in Georgia ever since leaving her singing career behind. But when her niece Charlie Heart (Carter Faith) disappears, the so-called "Queen of Mean" returns to Nashville, Tennessee, to uncover the truth about what happened. But as she embarks on her quest, she uncovers a side of the city she's never seen and is forced to confront her past. Sounds alright, doesn't it? Well, Netflixers are absolutely loving Chastain's quest for justice.

"Heartland" is a strange mix of mystery thriller and noir scored by a country soundtrack that features original music from Carter Faith, who also happens to be a real-life country music star. Shana Feste appears to have taken some cues from a number of Taylor Sheridan indicates in that regard, which has proven out to have been a wise move — at least, if the Netflix viewing figures are anything to go by.

In a recent development, "Heartland" hit Netflix on November 13, 2026, and became an instant hit. The film debuted at the top of the English movie list with 7.3 million views, finishing its first week at number two on the global movies charts with 14.8 million views. Since then it's been smooth sailing for "Heartland," according to FlixPatrol.

In point of fact, the film has remained in the top 10 in the United States for the last 10 days, hovering around the number one and two spots before dropping to number five on November 22, 2026, and number six as of November 24. But that's just part of the story, as "Heartland" is also a global hit. The film was a top 10 movie in 89 countries during the week of November 11 to November 22, 2026, and is still charting in 78 countries at the time of writing. It even hit number one in Australia and New Zealand in its second week on Netflix. All in all, then, that's a pretty good showing for "Heartland," which otherwise received mixed reviews from critics.

Writer/director Shana Feste told Texas Monthly that her aim with "Heartland" was to subvert established norms of the thriller, crime, and action genres. "We have this very established cinematic tradition of celebrating damaged men," she noted. "But we are not so generous with our female characters." Feste went on to describe the experience of creating Misty Jones as "incredibly freeing," due to the fact this was a character "that did not organize her life around being liked or desired." That certainly makes for a compelling protagonist in the film, and Jessica Chastain does a solid job of rendering the "Queen of Mean" in all her damaged glory.

Recent findings suggest that sadly, that only amounted to a less than impressive 56% critic score on Rotten Tomatoes, which is five percentage points higher than the audience score. David Rooney of The Hollywood Reporter couldn't help himself when he described Feste's latest as "Country Weak," echoing the sentiments of The Guardian's Adrian Horton (who opined that "Heartland" "seems more destined for background music than a hit"). Nick Schager of The Daily Beast, on the other hand, thought the film managed to "offset its predictability with knockabout ferocity," and William Bibbiani of TheWrap liked it enough to hope it becomes "the first in a long, long series." With the viewership being what it is, that might just turn out to be the case.

"Heartland" might not be the best thriller Netflix has to offer, then. But it's not without its charms and comes with the Netflix audience seal of approval.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that CD Projekt Red and Sony Interactive Entertainment just announced a marketing deal for The Witcher 4, but that doesn't mean the game will be exclusive to PlayStation. CD Projekt Red's Michał Nowakowski noted on social media, "Just to be clear: The Witcher 4 and our other upcoming titles will remain multiplatform." The marketing deal could be similar to the one between Rockstar and Sony for GTA 6, where GTA 6 was given preferential treatment on PS5 in a number of ways in the marketing campaign. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=54dabgZJ5YA Beyond The Witcher 4, CD Projekt Red is making Cyberpunk 2, a new IP codenamed Hadar, a new game believed to be a multiplayer The Witcher title, and a remake of the original Witcher. On the mobile side, CD Projekt Red is working with Scopely on a new game that hasn't been announced yet. The Witcher 4 now has more than 500 people working on it, and the game is expected to release in 2028. Given that timing, The Witcher 4 likely won't be on a disc because Sony won't support game discs beginning in January 2028. That being said, CD Projekt Red is promising that The Witcher 4 will have some kind of physical goodies for fans. In other news about The Witcher 4, CD Projekt Red recently discussed the game in comparison to GTA 6. "Of course we did look at the game; we did see the differences. We believe there’s going to be a comparable leap between The Witcher 3 and The Witcher 4–I think so, yes," Nowakowski said. "It’s been 11 years; we are working on The Witcher 4 to make it significantly better looking and improved in terms of pretty much every possible facet of the game, so yes, you should expect us to make a much bigger jump between Witcher 3 and Witcher 4.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The highly anticipated Avengers: Doomsday not only promises sprawling action across the multiverse, but it also features a massive cast (as revealed by that chair promotion last year). However, while the film unites veterans of the Marvel Cinematic Universe and stars who predate it, there are some familiar faces who don’t appear to be in the fold. That includes X-Men veterans Halle Berry and Anna Paquin. I’ve been wondering why they weren’t invited back, and Joe and Anthony Russo shared their takes.

Doomsday features several beloved X-Men stars like Ian McKellen, James Marsden, Rebecca Romijn and the late, great Patrick Stewart (in his final film performance). So, for fans like myself, it’s a bit of a head-scratcher that Berry (who played Ororo Munroe/Storm) and Paquin (Marie D'Ancanto/Rogue) apparently weren’t invited to the party. As part of a cover story for this 2026 movie schedule entry, the Russo Brothers were asked about their absences and those of others, with Joe saying this:.

[The casting] was really targeted. It was really specific.

Recent findings suggest that in fairness, the Russos are shrewd when it comes to assembling (no pun intended) the ensembles for their MCU team-up films. Avengers: Infinity War and Endgame both had specific sets of characters that played into the films’ respective narratives in relevant ways. With that being stated, considering the heavy presence of X-Men alums in Doomsday, it’s still somewhat weird that Storm, Rogue, Iceman and more aren’t present when Marsden’s Cyclops says, “To me, my X-Men.” Still, Anthony Russo added another point:.

We really do have a process where we see the entire film through each character’s eyes, no matter what the size of their role is. With the X-Men, we got to really deep dive and think about their histories as characters, their experiences, and how this particular moment in time was gonna affect them. There’s such a rich history to them that we really do bring them to the film as if it’s their movie, as well.

Sources indicate that bringing those OGs into the fold seemed to be the realization of a dream not just for the Russos but for producer Kevin Feige as well. Feige’s producing career notably started years ago when Lauren Shuler Donner tapped him as an associate producer on 2000’s X-Men. Now, the super producer is in the position to have his MCU characters interact with the famous mutants for what may be the latter group’s final stand within the multiverse.

There’s still reason to wonder whether more characters are being kept under wraps ahead of the film’s release. However, earlier this year, when Berry was asked about possibly reprising Storm in Doomsday, she seemed to downplay the idea. The actress does still have plenty of love for the character and the franchise, though, as she celebrated X-Men’s 26th anniversary in July. That post also prompted fans to question her involvement in the upcoming Marvel movie, but nothing has seemingly materialized at this point.

What is known for sure, though, is that a new team of X-Men will be prominent within the MCU moving forward, as a reboot from director Jake Schreier is on the way. With that, new actors will be taking on the lead roles, with Inde Navarrette and Maya Boyd playing Rogue and Storm, respectively. There’s still time for Marvel to surprise us by having Halle Berry, Anna Paquin and others show up in Doomsday but, if not, there’s always Secret Wars.

Avengers: Doomsday opens in theaters on December 18, while Secret Wars is set to follow on December 17, 2027. In the meantime, grab a Disney+ subscription and stream the MCU and X-Men films.

Joan Smalls is detailing what she claims really happened between her and former BFF Candice Swanepoel, alleging Tom Brady was the “catalyst” of their friendship fallout.

Smalls, 38, explained on the Wednesday, November 25, episode of the “Cutting Room Floor” podcast that while fans began to notice her distancing herself from Swanepoel, 38, during October’s Victoria’s Secret Fashion Show — when they didn’t pose for or take any pictures together — she had actually cut ties with the fellow model in April.

Recent findings suggest that “I think they were noticing one because I removed all the pictures off of my Instagram of her and I stopped following her months ago,” Smalls recalled, confirming that Swanepoel’s choice to date Brady, 49, following her own eight-month romance with the retired quarterback is what sparked their tension. (Us confirmed in October that Swanepoel and Brady have been dating “for a while.”.

Smalls told listeners that she had been friends with Swanepoel for more than 15 years and was “vulnerable” and had “intimate conversations” with her, which made her relationship with Brady even more difficult to understand.

Sources indicate that “We’ve seen each other through ups and downs. You’ve seen the relationships, situationships, people I’ve dated, and I’ve confided in you in these spaces, and we never had a crossover,” Smalls shared. “So, all of a sudden, OK, I stopped seeing this person and 3 months later, you text me and say, ‘Oh, we have to speak about something.’”.

The Puerto Rico native revealed she instantly knew what Swanepoel wanted to say.

“We’ve never been in a crossroads where we’ve had to have such a serious conversation,” Smalls mentioned, adding that she knew it in her “soul” that it was pegged to Brady, whom Smalls revealed Swanepoel had helped her “write text messages to” when they were an item.

In a recent development, the supermodel said that Swanepoel “knew intimate things, like, potentially, to my detriment, I overshared. I was just being open with a friend that I thought was a safe space.”.

Smalls recalled speaking on the phone “very briefly” with Swanepoel and when they hung up she was “perplexed” and at “a loss for words.”.

While Smalls stated Brady “wasn’t an ex” per say, she had been seeing him and confiding in Swanepoel about him, which is why it went against girl code.

“She came across as justifying her action [and saying] that what I had was wasn’t valid or it was casual and she started diminishing my experience to make herself feel better about the situation,” Smalls claimed. “I think [that] is what kind of infuriated me as my friend to kind of, diminish me or devalue my friendship so much that you didn’t have consideration towards my feelings or my hurt.”.

Sources indicate that smalls added that Swanepoel’s alleged “attitude of, ‘I’m an adult. I don’t need permission,’” also rubbed her the wrong way.

“You are an adult and you don’t need permission. But as a friend, you should consider me in your choices. Don’t consider me in your apologies,” she continued.

Smalls revealed that it didn’t matter that it was Brady, it was the fact that Swanepoel didn’t think about her when she made a move on someone she had a past with.

According to recent reports, “It was a mixture of the lying — I caught her in a couple of lies and I asked her about it. She didn’t want to correct it. It was, like, under the rug,” Smalls remarked. “It was the gaslighting. It was the diminishing of my feelings, trying to devalue my worth. And it was just like one after the other.”.

According to recent reports, she allegedly told Swanepoel, “I was like, you know what you’re doing is manipulation 101. I said the fact that you are blameshifting and saying that what I said hurt you but what you did didn’t hurt it to me that’s mindblowing.”.

After Smalls was out of the friendship, she remarked she spoke with other females and friends and realized that “this is not fresh territory for her,” claiming that Swanepoel had “done this before.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Brad Pitt and Angelina Jolie have settled a years-long legal dispute over the sale of their French winery, Château Miraval.

“We have settled out of court in the best interests of our family and will not be commenting further,” representatives of Jolie, 51, and Pitt, 62, remarked in a Wednesday, November 25, statement to Us. “Any comments in media stories attributed to ‘sources’ are in fact not coming from either of us, or anyone close to us.”.

The couple first gained a controlling interest in the 1,200-acre winery in the South of France in 2008.

They began selling their own rosé in March 2013, before saying “I do” at the chateau in August 2014. Things got sour, however, after Jolie and Pitt filed for divorce in 2016.

According to a February 2022 lawsuit, Pitt alleged that Jolie illegally sold her shares of Miraval to Tenute del Mondo, the wine division of the Stoli group owned by Russian businessman Yuri Shefler.

According to recent reports, pitt claimed that both parties agreed not to sell their Miraval shares without the other’s permission. In his filing, Pitt argued that his ex-wife made the business decision without his knowledge or explicit consent.

According to recent reports, “Through the purported sale, Jolie sought to inflict harm on Pitt,” the lawsuit alleged. “Jolie knew and intended that Shefler and his affiliates would try to control the business Pitt had built and to undermine Pitt’s investment in Miraval.”.

Us has learned the litigation between Pitt and Stoli will continue despite the recent settlement involving Jolie.

Wednesday’s settlement ends a contentious case that put Pitt and Jolie’s divorce under the spotlight. The exes — who share children Maddox, 25, Pax, 22, Zahara, 21, Shiloh, 20, and twins Vivienne and Knox, 18 — finalized their split in December 2024.

Before things were finalized, however, the pair went through a public legal battle with serious allegations spread.

Jolie responded to Pitt’s lawsuit via a countersuit, claiming her ex was “waging a vindictive war against” her while denying that she needed his approval to sell her stake.

In previous court filings, Jolie’s legal team alleged that Pitt refused to buy her out of the winery business after she declined to sign a non-disclosure agreement allegedly “designed to force her silence about his abuse and cover-up.”.

Tech Report: Why Quentin Tarantino Didn't Direct Brad Pitt's Cliff Booth Movie

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Warning: This article contains spoilers for "The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth.".
  • In a recent development, if it looks like a Quentin Tarantino movie and talks like a Quentin Tarantino movie, you'd usually find yourself watching a Quentin Tarantino movie.
  • According to recent reports, after having finally seen the highly-anticipated sequel for ourselves, we (and many others) were left with even more questions regarding why Tarantino ultimately decided to sit this one out rather than sit in the director's chair himself.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Warning: This article contains spoilers for "The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth.".

In a recent development, if it looks like a Quentin Tarantino movie and talks like a Quentin Tarantino movie, you'd usually find yourself watching a Quentin Tarantino movie. "The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth" is the rare exception to that rule, however. After "Once Upon a Time in Hollywood" debuted in 2019 and was heralded by many as the filmmaker's best movie yet, whispers of a continuation soon grew to a deafening noise. Tarantino then went and wrote a book based on the events of the film in a sort of reverse-adaptation situation. He subsequently spent months talking up his intentions to direct a since-shelved project called "The Movie Critic," which would've starred Brad Pitt reprising his role as Cliff Booth. But after that fell apart, David Fincher eventually came on board to direct Tarantino's script for "Cliff Booth.".

According to recent reports, after having finally seen the highly-anticipated sequel for ourselves, we (and many others) were left with even more questions regarding why Tarantino ultimately decided to sit this one out rather than sit in the director's chair himself. "The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth" is a solid enough spiritual successor, albeit one where Fincher and Tarantino's unique (and wildly different) sensibilities seem to clash more often than complement. And the snappiness of the dialogue, tone, and rhythm and pacing certainly feel indebted to the quintessential Tarantino style most of us know and adore.

So, with all due respect to a legend like Fincher, was there ever a world where Tarantino had simply directed this himself? It's a complicated question with no easy answers, but below, we've rounded up a complete timeline of events — to the best of public knowledge, of course. So, here's why Tarantino's "Cliff Booth" instead became a Fincher/Tarantino joint.

According to recent reports, it all began, as it so often does in this business, with a project that wasn't to be. In 2023, "The Movie Critic" was breathlessly unveiled as Quentin Tarantino's 10th and final directing gig — a self-imposed limit that the ever-opinionated artist decided to stick to, no matter what. And while rumors initially suggested this might have been based on the life of prolific writer and critic Pauline Kael, it was later revealed that this would've been an original story taking QT's usual fast-and-loose approach to fact and fiction. All seemed ready and raring to go ... until Tarantino appeared to rethink his approach (following rewrites that delayed production) and dropped the project altogether.

It has been revealed that but Hollywood just loves a comeback story, and this wasn't the end of the line. In 2025, news broke that Fincher would be directing a sequel to "Once Upon a Time in Hollywood" focused on stuntman extraordinaire Cliff Booth. It didn't take much brain power to connect the dots between the two film ideas, leading to much informed speculation that Tarantino reworked his idea for "The Movie Critic" into what turned out to be "The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth." For his part, Tarantino spoke to The Hollywood Reporter in 2025 and denied that Cliff was ever going to appear in "The Movie Critic." Of course, this contradicts other accounts claiming that a sort of cinematic universe may have been in the works. We'll likely never know the full behind-the-scenes story.

It has been revealed that did we receive the next-best outcome in its place? A Fincher/QT dream team has been years in the making, after all. Still, we can't help but wonder about what might have been.

For better or worse, what's clear is that "The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth" seems fated to divide viewers. There are those who feel David Fincher's involvement as director meshes beautifully with Quentin Tarantino's skills as writer, leading to a final result that's even more than the sum of its mighty parts — akin to what Fincher pulled off in his collaboration with Aaron Sorkin on "The Social Network," for instance. But there are others who feel that, while the tension between their particular styles and worldviews makes for dramatically interesting material, the push and pull between Fincher and Tarantino ultimately proves too unwieldy.

According to recent reports, yes, I happen to fall into that latter camp (if you haven't guessed as much already), and it's tough to reconcile the movie we have with the hypothetical version it could've been. To be fair, the evidence is fairly plain to see. Where "Once Upon a Time in Hollywood" is overflowing with warmth and nostalgia and a poignant perspective of time passing us by (and, okay, a whole lot of gratuitous violence, too), "Cliff Booth" stands out for how emotionally distant and cold it feels in practically every scene ... outside of Cliff's flirtations with Elizabeth Debicki's Karen Crosby or bonding moments with father Gus (Peter Weller), at least.

In the hands of Tarantino alone, it's fair to wonder if he could've brought a much-needed sense of fun and verve to the action that seems oddly missing in "Cliff Booth." What we ended up with is something caught between a Fincher and Tarantino film. Instead of half of both, wouldn't it have been more satisfying to get all of Tarantino?

"The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth" is now playing in select theaters.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, grand Theft Auto 6 is finally here, and one of the things people are talking about is the game's difficulty level. Some are saying it's too easy. Rockstar boss Rob Nelson has now entered the conversation, telling Destructoid that Rockstar's data showed that GTA 4 was "a little too punishing in places" and GTA 5 was "perhaps too easy." So with GTA 6, the team trying to "land somewhere in the middle." GTA 6 has no defined difficulty levels, which is in keeping with the franchise's tradition. That mentioned, players can adjust things like aiming controls, while players can unlock cheat codes to make the game easier or harder. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dJDf76QVv70 Design producer Scott Mitchell, meanwhile, said the fail states in GTA 6 were designed to feel "appropriate." “We wanted to keep things open and not limit the players’ use of mechanics, such as stealth, but we did also want to make sure we retained the cinematic, high production value, explosive sequences that we’re known for, and people expect. It feels like we’ve managed to strike a good balance," he explained. Also in the interview, Nelson said figuring out the difficulty level for GTA 6 is itself challenging because the designers themselves know enemy positions better than anyone after playing and testing the game so much. "There’s a real process in unpicking some of that to create an experience most players will be able to enjoy, rather than endure," Nelson said. "The game is so substantial, and has such a wide range of content that we can really lean into that, making certain open-world content--compounds and fronts for example---more difficult, to give players seeking a challenge something to sink their teeth into as well.” GTA 6 launched on November 19 and had a gigantic debut, selling 32.5 million copies by launch and generating around $4 billion on day one. GTA 6 has no defined difficulty levels, which is in keeping with the franchise's tradition. That said, players can adjust things like aiming controls, while players can unlock cheat codes to make the game easier or harder.

“We wanted to keep things open and not limit the players’ use of mechanics, such as stealth, but we did also want to make sure we retained the cinematic, high production value, explosive sequences that we’re known for, and people expect. It feels like we’ve managed to strike a good balance," he explained.

Also in the interview, Nelson noted figuring out the difficulty level for GTA 6 is itself challenging because the designers themselves know enemy positions better than anyone after playing and testing the game so much.

It has been revealed that "There’s a real process in unpicking some of that to create an experience most players will be able to enjoy, rather than endure," Nelson said. "The game is so big, and has such a wide range of content that we can really lean into that, making certain open-world content--compounds and fronts for example---more difficult, to give players seeking a challenge something to sink their teeth into as well.”.

GTA 6 debuted on November 19 and had a gigantic debut, selling 32.5 million copies by launch and generating around $4 billion on day one.

For more, check out GameSpot's GTA 6 review and our rundown of five things to do first.

Unsurprisingly, new data shows that PlayStation and Xbox console sales surged in the week before release. According to Circana's Mat Piscatella, there was a "significant surge" in hardware sales in the US for the week that ended November 14. PS5 sales were >2.4x the same week last year, while Xbox Series X|S sales increased by >2.3x. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Ble-JJxBBGA GTA 6 is not available on Switch 2, but that console saw a 40% surge in sales compared to the same week in 2025. Before launch, Piscatella stated GTA 6 should help boost PS5 and Xbox Series X|S sales, but maybe not so dramatically due to the astronomical cost of a new console. To help save money, you could buy an Xbox One and stream GTA 6. Alternatively, people have discovered that you can stream the game to a PlayStation Portal device. GTA 6 launched on November 19 and had a gigantic debut, selling 32.5 million copies by launch and generating around $4 billion on day one. 💡 Key Takeaways
  • When it comes to making a movie sequel like "Focker In-Law," the challenges faced by the returning cast and crew are distinct but dependent on those faced by the newcomers.
  • Industry observers note that these are the precise challenges that writer/director John Hamburg and star Ariana Grande had to deal with while making "Focker In-Law," the fourth film in the uber-popular "Meet the Parents" franchise.
  • It has been revealed that when I had the chance to talk with Hamburg about this, he agreed that the challenge was not insignificant.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

When it comes to making a movie sequel like "Focker In-Law," the challenges faced by the returning cast and crew are distinct but dependent on those faced by the newcomers. The former have to try not to repeat themselves, while the latter have to find a way of integrating their work into an already-established milieu. This can be especially tricky when it comes to comedy, as the genre lives and dies on tone and timing. If one or both are off, it can destroy the entire proceedings.

Industry observers note that these are the precise challenges that writer/director John Hamburg and star Ariana Grande had to deal with while making "Focker In-Law," the fourth film in the uber-popular "Meet the Parents" franchise. While returning folks like Ben Stiller (as Greg Focker) and Robert De Niro (as Jack Byrnes) could rely on their past work on the property to use as a starting point, Grande had to find a path to her own comedic voice within the film's ensemble. Not making it any easier is the fact that her role is not only key, but complex: She's Olivia Jones, the bride-to-be of Greg's son, Henry (Skyler Gisondo), yet Greg is trepidatious of anyone marrying his boy. Making things more complicated is that Olivia and Greg start off on a bad note that only gets worse, as Greg discovers her past as a former FBI hostage negotiator. This means Grande has to be both a sweet-natured love interest and a potentially conniving antagonist, which is not an easy mix.

It has been revealed that when I had the chance to talk with Hamburg about this, he agreed that the challenge was not insignificant. Yet he also revealed how he worked with Grande to craft her character, especially in the editing room, resulting in a great fresh addition to the Focker saga.

Sources indicate that as John Hamburg told me during our chat, it was not lost on himself and the others behind "Focker In-Law" that Ariana Grande had her work cut out for her playing Olivia. Yet, he explained why Grande was so uniquely qualified to handle the challenge:.

"We were like, 'Oh my God, she's playing the love interest and the antagonist. What a tight rope.' But honestly, she's so uniquely gifted that I think she's the only person that could really nail that thing where you're kind of scared of her, you're intimidated, but she's also the sweetest, most loving [person]. Her smile lights up a room. Ari brings so much of that energy, but she's just a wonderful actress. So, she could play all those levels.".

According to recent reports, it turns out that Grande's ability to play multiple levels of a character dovetailed nicely with Hamburg's approach to comedy, which is less about improvisation and more about tweaking the tone and intention of a moment or scene. Hamburg explained how Grande provided him with ample material that he was able to use in post-production:.

"[...] When we're filming, I try to get different levels. 'So, okay, maybe try it a little more passive-aggressive, or try it a little more hostile, or say this with a smile,' that kind of thing. And she has so much in her toolbox that she was able to give me so many levels. So, when I got to the editing room, it was like an embarrassment of riches to try while I was crafting her performance.".

The wrong person playing Olivia could've sunk the whole film. Fortunately, Hamburg had the right instinct that Grande could handle it.

"Focker In-Law" is right now playing in theaters.

Casting Director Francine Maisler on ‘Dune: Part Three’

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (1909 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Vanityfair

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • When Denis Villeneuve brought on seasoned casting director Francine Maisler for the first Dune movie, they were starting from scratch.
  • Sources indicate that luckily, the pair had already worked together on Villeneuve’s three previous films, Sicario, Blade Runner 2049, and Arrival.
  • According to recent reports, when they were casting the first installment, Maisler was aware that it was possible that these actors might play these characters for more than just one film.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

When Denis Villeneuve brought on seasoned casting director Francine Maisler for the first Dune movie, they were starting from scratch. For the ambitious adaptation of Frank Herbert’s 1965 sci-fi novel, they had to cast not only the lead character, Paul Atreides, but dozens of other main characters—powerful warriors, scheming royals, shape-shifting conspirators—to inhabit the world.

Sources indicate that luckily, the pair had already worked together on Villeneuve’s three previous films, Sicario, Blade Runner 2049, and Arrival. “Denis’s vision is my compass,” Maisler tells Vanity Fair. “His passion [for Dune] since he was a teen was all I needed to follow.”.

According to recent reports, when they were casting the first installment, Maisler was aware that it was possible that these actors might play these characters for more than just one film. “I did have an idea that they would have to have the presence and the acting talent to be able to carry this potentially for three movies,” she says.

In a recent development, dune (2021), starring Timothée Chalamet as Paul Atreides and Zendaya as Chani, was just the first step. Maisler returned to cast Dune: Part Two (2024), and Dune: Part Three, which will wrap up Villeneuve’s trilogy when it hits theaters on December 18.

Maisler is a titan of casting, having worked on hundreds of films with filmmakers such as Luca Guadagnino, Greta Gerwig, Aaron Sorkin, Paul Greengrass, Adam McKay, and Terrence Malick, and she was nominated for the first casting Oscar in 2026 for her work on Ryan Coogler’s Sinners.

Industry observers note that the casting Oscar didn’t exist when she began working on the Dune franchise, but this installment is likely to draw attention from the Academy. Over the three films, the cast has grown into an incredible ensemble, packed with many of today’s biggest movie stars, along with well-known veterans and a few unexpected choices. “One thing about Denis is if ever I bring him a name and he likes it, and I’ll say, ‘Well, do you want to hire that actor?’ He says to me something I think is so poetic,” says Maisler. “He says, ‘Francine, let me get back to you tomorrow. I need to dream about it.’”.

Ahead of the release of Dune: Part Three, Maisler looks back at casting the trilogy’s most notable roles, including the exciting upcoming additions to the upcoming film—and the possibility of more Dune in the future.

Industry observers note that in Herbert’s book, Atreides is a slender 15-year-old with dark hair. “To find a 15-year-old who had that talent to carry this whole movie, we weren’t sure was out there,” remembers Maisler. The name that came up was then 22-year-old Chalamet, whom Maisler had previously cast in Hostiles, Beautiful Boy, The King, and Little Women. Chalamet, who didn’t have to audition but did meet with Villeneuve, would have to play Atreides from a young man who then begins to amass power in the second film and, after a 12-year time jump, is burdened with the choices he’s made waging a galactic war in the third. Though Chalamet hadn’t led a big blockbuster before, Maisler saw the depth of his talent. “I do think Beautiful Boy demonstrated me the depth of Timothée as an actor, as a young man, and that this was the next step in his progression as an actor, that he was able to hold a franchise in his hand,” says Maisler.

There was a worldwide search for Chani, the skilled Fremen warrior from Arrakis who falls in love with Atreides. At the time, Zendaya was in the middle of filming the first season of Euphoria, and her graduation from Disney star to movie star had not yet happened. Zendaya screen tested with Chalamet, which sealed it for Maisler and Villeneuve. “She came in with five other incredibly talented actresses, but the minute you saw her with Timothée in a room, you just knew that there’s something special happening,” she states. “She has such power when she walks in the room, and she’s breathtaking in the most interesting way.”.

Of course, Paul Atreides’s parents, Duke Leto Atreides and Lady Jessica, needed to look like Chalamet, but Maisler started with the characters’ essences when casting. Duke Leto Atreides was considered a fair and devoted leader as the noble head of House Atreides. Maisler saw that gravitas in Oscar Isaac. Lady Jessica becomes a force in the story because of her heightened physical and mental control as a trained member of the Bene Gesserit sisterhood. “Rebecca is so powerful, isn’t she?” notes Maisler. “She really, I have to say, surprised me. I always knew how talented she was, but she just owned that part.”.

It has been revealed that villeneuve and Maisler had worked with Brolin on the 2015 crime thriller Sicario. Maisler, who calls Brolin “one of our greatest actors,” was excited to have him back, this time playing Gurney Halleck, the Warmaster of House Atreides and a mentor to Paul Atreides. The character is described in the book as a warrior-poet, requiring strength and depth. “He’s so charismatic, so masculine,” says Maisler of Brolin. “He’s kind of a throwback from other generations.”.

When Momoa’s agent brought up Momoa’s name, Maisler wasn’t quite sure about the idea because at the time he was known for starring in the DC movie franchise as Aquaman. “I was a bit skeptical, I have to admit, because I knew he had this incredible presence on screen, but I didn’t know, truly, his talent, and that’s taught me a lot about being open to people who come from different types of films,” she says. Villeneuve was more open to the idea at the start, and met with him about playing Duncan Idaho, a fierce fighter and protector of Paul Atreides. He returns in the third movie as a ghola—a sort of clone—named Hayt, which demands a more complicated performance from Momoa. “Jason’s an incredible artist, and I’ve come to just love him,” says Maisler. “He’s so funny. I want to put him in a romantic comedy next, because he really is one of the big surprises in the ensemble.”.

Taylor-Joy had already risen in stardom by the time she joined the franchise for the second film. Her breakout was in The Witch, and she starred in hit series The Queen's Gambit, which earned her a Golden Globe and a SAG Award. This made it slightly surprising that Alia Atreides, Paul’s volatile sister, makes a blink-and-you’ll-miss-it appearance in the second film. “I give her a lot of credit for not counting lines in the second one,” indicates Maisler, who says Taylor-Joy signed on for the second because of the potential of the third installment. Indeed, in Dune: Part Three, Alia is a loyal sister and vengeful force who is not afraid to get blood on her hands. Taylor-Joy’s charisma and intensity will jump off the screen, says Maisler. “Actors are very smart, and they know when to trust a director like Denis,” she says. “When he says there is going to be something in the third film and he describes it, he will make it happen.”.

Recent findings suggest that A tribal leader of the desert-dwelling Fremen, Stilgar is a seasoned warrior and becomes a devout follower of Paul Atreides as Muad’Dib. The role required a level of intensity. “Oh, I think we all just prayed that Javier would do it,” indicates Maisler. “I think every actor wants to work with Javier, and he’s one of probably a handful of actors I think can do anything.”.

Pugh joined for the second film as well, but like Taylor-Joy, she didn’t have a ton to do. But Princess Irulan, who marries Paul Atreides as a political union, is a key part of the plot in Dune: Part Three, joining a conspiracy against Paul. Maisler first saw Pugh in the 2016 film Lady Macbeth, and then cast her as Amy March in Gerwig’s Little Women. “You saw on that what an intelligent actress she is, and singular,” she says. “She knows no boundaries, and she’s confident and bold.” She says Pugh has always reminded her of Debra Winger, the star of An Officer and a Gentleman (1982), and Terms of Endearment (1983). “She’s just commanding, and she has this energy, and everything she does is fascinating,” says Maisler. “You can’t take your eyes off of her.”.

The third installment brings in yet another major star with Pattinson, who plays Scytale, a shape-shifter who is conspiring to dethrone Paul Atreides. Maisler, who also worked with Pattinson in Primetime, which also came out this year, describes him as “one of the versatile actors in his choices.” She had also worked with Pattinson on Mickey 17, which proved that he could play many different versions of a character—a skill that would be required of him in this third Dune movie. “Robert's a tremendous actor, and I think he takes these really bold chances,” states Maisler. As for his recent announcement as the next James Bond, Maisler has faith he and Villeneuve will deliver. “I think the way Denis and Rob created the character in Dune: Part Three together speaks to the surprises that we will see in Bond,” she says.

In a recent development, for Dune: Part Three, Maisler and Villeneuve had to find two actors who looked like twins and also looked like the offspring of Chalamet and Zendaya. They initially hoped to cast real twins, but didn’t find the right pair. In the end, they found their Ghanima and Leto II in Ida Brooke and Nakoa-Wolf Momoa. Brooke, who looks strikingly like Zendaya, is a relative newcomer who previously appeared on Apple’s sci-fi drama Silo (which stars Rebecca Ferguson). And Nakoa-Wolf Momoa, who makes his feature acting debut in Dune: Part Three, is Jason Momoa’s son—though Maisler didn’t know that when she first watched his audition tape. “Then came this tape of this young man who had incredible presence, and—we didn’t ask for this—he added some combat footage to his tape,” she says. Maisler says sometimes actors will call in a favor to get their child an audition, but Wolf, as she calls him, got this on his own. This casting was the most notable for the third film because of what might be to come. “It was almost like casting the first one where these two young actors could go on to potentially, if there’s another movie where they’re leads,” says Maisler. There have been no official announcements of any future Dune movies, but for those mourning the end of the Villeneuve trilogy, Maisler is planting a small seed of hope here. The third Dune book, Children of Dune, centers on Leto and Ghanima, which means the two young actors Maisler found may have more story ahead of them.

5 TV Shows To Watch If You Like Blade Runner 2099

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1459 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Slashfilm

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • "Blade Runner 2099" has finally premiered on Amazon Prime Video, and if you've been anxiously awaiting this entry in the storied sci-fi franchise inspired by Philip K.
  • According to recent reports, so, what's it about?
  • It has been revealed that all eight episodes of "Blade Runner 2099" are available on Amazon Prime Video as of November 25, but what should you watch when you're finished with the series?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

"Blade Runner 2099" has finally premiered on Amazon Prime Video, and if you've been anxiously awaiting this entry in the storied sci-fi franchise inspired by Philip K. Dick's novel "Do Androids Dream of Electric Sheep?" (the basis for the property that debuted back in 1982 with Ridley Scott's "Blade Runner"), we've got great news for you. In his review for /Film, Bill Bria praised "Blade Runner 2099" (as was overseen by showrunner Silka Luisa), declaring that Silka "has put together something that's as unique and bold as it is in conversation with its franchise's past, making it a proud new addition to the saga" and even calling the series "the best sci-fi show in years.".

According to recent reports, so, what's it about? "Blade Runner 2099," like its film predecessors "Blade Runner" and "Blade Runner 2049," focuses on the interplay between Replicants — an engineered humanoid — and Blade Runners, who are tasked with figuring out who's a human and who's a Replicant and disposing of the latter. (This is what Harrison Ford's Rick Deckard was doing, essentially, in "Blade Runner.") That's where we meet Olwen, a Replicant who's also a Blade Runner — played by Oscar winner Michelle Yeoh — and watch her team up with the human Cora (Hunter Schafer) in a post-revolution world where Replicants now control humans. As Olwen prepares to be retired and Cora pretends to be a Replicant, they look for a group of evil-doing Replicants causing chaos, allowing us to follow their adventures.

It has been revealed that all eight episodes of "Blade Runner 2099" are available on Amazon Prime Video as of November 25, but what should you watch when you're finished with the series? I've got some ideas.

Despite ... diminishing returns as J.J. Abrams' show "Alias" reached its endpoint with its fourth season, I still hold this show close to my heart, and fans of the double-crossing and secret identities in "Blade Runner 2099" will definitely love this spy drama. When "Alias" opens, Jennifer Garner's Sydney Bristow is, by all appearances, juggling a high-pressure job at a Los Angeles bank with her graduate studies ... except, the truth is that she doesn't work at a bank but as a spy for what she believes is a covert wing of the CIA called SD-6. When she tells her fiancé the truth about her career and SD-6 has him brutally murdered in their home, Sydney realizes that SD-6 isn't affiliated with United States intelligence but is actually a terrorist cell that's part of a larger structure operating across the world. That's when Sydney becomes a double agent, teams up with her CIA handler (and future husband) Michael Vaughn (Michael Vartan), and works alongside the other mole inside SD-6 ... who turns out to be her estranged father Jack Bristow (a sublime Victor Garber).

The first season of "Alias?" Amazing. The second season of "Alias?" God-tier television, especially "Phase One," the mid-season stunner that secured the coveted post-Super Bowl timeslot in 2003. Season 3 is where things start to go downhill, and in this house, we don't even discuss Season 4. Still, if you want to watch a few very good seasons of a spy drama after "Blade Runner 2099," check out "Alias," which is on Disney+.

Recent findings suggest that "Blade Runner 2099" is many things. "Good" is one of them. "Expensive" is definitely another. You can practically see dollar signs on the screen (the show just looks expensive, and I definitely don't mean that in a bad way). So, if you're looking for another massive-budget sci-fi epic that's got plenty of seasons under its belt at this point, consider checking out the Apple TV show "Foundation." Adapted from Isaac Asimov's "Foundation" book series by David S. Goyer and Josh Friedman, "Foundation," which premiered in 2021 and stars Jared Harris and Lee Pace, takes place in a future where living beings live under the control of the Empire, led largely by clones (though it's secretly run by Laura Birn's Lady Demerzel, who controls all of the Empire's leader-clones). Pace plays Brother Day, a middle-era clone of Emperor Cleon I, while Harris plays mathematician Hariton "Hari" Seldon, who can predict the future and serves as a mentor to young prodigy Gaal Dornick (Lou Llobell).

Recent findings suggest that "Foundation" is detailed, sumptuous, and again, looks expensive ... and whatever Apple is spending on this series is beyond worth it. Season 3 concluded in 2025 and the fourth season is already confirmed, so if you watch the show after "Blade Runner 2099," rest assured that there will be more "Foundation" on the way eventually.

It has been revealed that the vibes of "Pluribus" and "Blade Runner 2099" couldn't be more different, but if you like the push-and-pull of the interplay between humans and Replicants in the latter, I bet you'll like the dynamic between a hivemind and an unsuspecting woman in the former. Vince Gilligan's first series since "Better Call Saul" reunites him with that show's lead actor Rhea Seehorn and casts her as Carol Sturka, a romance author who's understandably terrified when an alien virus turns almost every human on Earth into part of a hivemind except for her (including her manager/wife Helen L. Umstead, played by Miriam Shor). As one of 12 people immune to said hivemind, Carol is at a total loss and absolutely refuses to follow the pack, which sets up a genuinely hilarious, deeply weird, and riveting series.

According to recent reports, "Pluribus" won Seehorn her first-ever Emmy for playing Carol (well-deserved, especially after her years playing "Better Call Saul" lead Kim Wexler), and even though the series boasts a great ensemble, it's more or less a one-woman show as Carol moves through a completely changed Earth and tries to figure out her next move. If you haven't watched "Pluribus" yet and just finished "Blade Runner 2099," check this pick out.

"Blade Runner 2099" is a great series that happens to stand in the shadow of its predecessor, owing largely to the fact that "Blade Runner" is one of the most influential and beloved science fiction films of all time. This is also true of "Andor," an exceptional science fiction series that's part of a larger universe you might be familiar with called the "Star Wars" franchise. Created and run by the great Tony Gilroy, "Andor," a prequel to the movies "Rogue One: A Star Wars Story" and "Star Wars: Episode IV — A New Hope," centers on Cassian Andor (Diego Luna), a thief who becomes radicalized against the Galactic Empire over five years and ends up serving as an agent/spy for the Rebel Alliance.

I probably don't need to tell you that "Andor" is one of the best Star Wars projects ever made (this is just established fact), but both "Andor" and "Blade Runner 2099" are given the daunting task of expanding a well-known universe in a way that doesn't feel like a stingy cash grab, and both succeed. If you haven't watched "Andor" yet, you're in for a serious treat. The show only runs for two seasons, but its sophomore outing is regarded as one of the best TV seasons in recent memory by pretty much all of its fans, and it really does pair perfectly with another legacy project like "Blade Runner 2099.".

According to recent reports, if your favorite thing about "Blade Runner 2099" is the buddy aspect (namely, the way that Hunter Schafer and Michelle Yeoh's characters play against each other), consider another Amazon Prime Video series. Specifically, consider "Fallout," the adaptation of the blockbuster video game series that started airing on the streamer in 2024. The show, created by Graham Wagner and Geneva Robertson-Dworet (with Jonathan Nolan and Lisa Joy of "Westworld" among the executive producers), centers around Lucy (Ella Purnell), an individual who, like most other people in this world, lives in an underground bunker to avoid the nuclear aftermath of the Great War of 2077 between China and the United States. When Lucy's beloved father Hank is kidnapped suddenly from their home in Vault 33, she decides to venture to the surface and track him down ... and while there, she encounters The Ghoul, a former TV star named Cooper Howard who was mutated by the nuclear blast and is played by Walton Goggins.

Industry observers note that purnell and Goggins are an unexpectedly perfect duo, much like Yeoh and Schafer. So, again, if you're looking for a follow-up series to "Blade Runner 2099" that pairs two unlikely souls together and watches them embark on a journey, try the first two seasons of "Fallout" on Amazon Prime Video. That's also where you can find "Blade Runner 2099" — again, all of Season 1 is streaming now.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that the US government has declared a new round of tariffs targeting several major countries, including China, Japan, Vietnam, and European Union trading partners.
  • The US government has announced a newly introduced round of tariffs targeting several major countries, including China, Japan, Vietnam, and European Union trading partners.
  • Sources indicate that what does this mean for gaming hardware?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that the US government has declared a new round of tariffs targeting several major countries, including China, Japan, Vietnam, and European Union trading partners. Under the proposed tariffs, import taxes will rise significantly, with China facing up to 40% when the new duties take effect next year. According to the BBC, some of the rates will be reduced because of tariff caps that US President Donald Trump has already agreed to, and individual countries could also face different levies. What does this mean for gaming hardware? Trump's first round of "Liberation Day" tariffs contributed to rising console prices, but the Supreme Court eventually struck them down. Substantial companies like Sony, Microsoft, and Nintendo benefited from tariff refunds after the ruling, but they didn't pass the savings on to consumers. In Sony's case, it was estimated to get back $508 million in refunds from the US government. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4FatSqS3VYY&t=19s The new tariffs bypass the Supreme Court's ruling by using a different law, Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974, which allows the government to impose tariffs on countries that use unfair business practices. The law does require an investigation into specific trade practices before rates are set. If higher import taxes take effect, console companies could face much higher costs, and protecting their profits will likely mean consumers have to cover the difference. Nintendo, Sony, and Microsoft have moved much of their final assembly out of China and into Southeast Asia, especially Vietnam, to avoid earlier tariffs. However, key parts like batteries and power supplies still mostly come from China, and if tariffs on these parts rise, total production costs for consoles made outside China will go up even more. Some electronic goods could be exempt from tariffs, and manufacturers often stockpile inventory ahead of tariff deadlines to delay price changes. But with rising costs from the ongoing components shortage amid the AI boom and other global factors, console prices remain at risk. After the June announcement of steep console price hikes, Microsoft warned that Xbox console costs could rise again in 2027, and next-gen hardware is also expected to be very pricey.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that gwyneth Paltrow returned to the massive screen for her role in the Academy Award-nominated film Marty Supreme, starring Timothée Chalamet. Ultimately, Paltrow ended up receiving considerable praise for her performance as Kay Stone. And the A24 sports dramedy about a ping-pong prodigy earned major praise and multiple awards-season nods. However, before all of that, Paltrow wondered if Hollywood would want her back.

Beyond the role itself, what ultimately got Paltrow to sign on for Marty Supreme was the fact that both the son she shares with Coldplay frontman Chris Martin and her husband Brad Falchuk’s son left for college, freeing her up for the first time since Avengers: Endgame. She recently recalled that time in her life while appearing on Today:.

Recent findings suggest that I think what happened was when our boys went to college two years ago, at the same time, it was like, right as they were going, I was offered Marty Supreme. And I thought, ‘Wow, what a great…’ It really opened up this idea that I could maybe do it, and since the kids were no longer at home, I was really free to go [film it].

In a recent development, after first appearing in the Marvel Cinematic Universe via Iron Man in 2008, Paltrow was a regular presence throughout the films. However, she eventually took a step back and devoted much of her time to running her wellness company, Goop, raising her kids and enjoying a quieter life away from film sets.

But just because Paltrow wanted to return to the big screen, it didn’t mean that anyone else would necessarily embrace her decision. During the recent interview, the Pepper Potts actress was asked if she had thought about whether anyone would even want to see her taking on roles in Hollywood again, and her answer was very candid. She mentioned:.

It has been revealed that yes, I did. I really did. I thought, ‘I don’t know if there will be a place for me anymore.’ But I’m really glad that there seems to be.

Sources indicate that marty Supreme turned out to be a really smart choice for the former Glee star to jump back into the acting game with. Paltrow also revealed that the process of acting and making a movie is pretty much the same since the last time she did it. The thing that has changed is the approach to marketing and press junkets.

In a recent development, it’s no longer just about finding out whether Hollywood wants you back when you take a break, or even about how your performance is received. You also have to find a way to generate buzz to capture the attention of audiences, with social media playing into it all. The Seven star explained:.

Industry observers note that I think the doing of it is pretty much the same. I think all the marketing around it — that’s all changed a lot. There’s all the social media component to marketing something. Press junkets are not what they used to be. That format has totally changed, but I think it’s largely the same.

When it came to generating buzz for the Timothée Chalamet starrer, the PR blitz included a massive orange blimp touring across the U.S., fans camping out for the viral Marty jackets, and even the Las Vegas Sphere being turned into a giant ping pong.

Your Daily Blend of Entertainment News.

I can’t imagine Paltrow having to do anything like that when she was campaigning during the awards season for Shakespeare in Love, before ultimately taking home Best Actress for her performance. If that film were coming out today, someone in marketing would likely have to think about what the promotional popcorn bucket should be.

With Marty Supreme behind her, the Sliding Doors star is back in Hollywood and has a few projects in various stages of development. While waiting to see what Gwyneth Paltrow has in store for the 2027 movie schedule, Avengers: Doomsday will be in theaters on December 18th, finally providing answers to any and all rumors about whether it will include Pepper Potts.

The actor who plays Mandy, Lexie Shoaibi, has now discussed how she got the part and her reaction to people being weird online. Speaking to Vulture, Shoaibi remarked she's able to see "more good than bad" thanks to her experience being a content creator. "There are weirdos out there, and they’re going to try to bring you down, so it’s crucial to stay around the people and the places that aren’t doing that," she said. I’m living in the positive, for sure." https://www.youtube.com/shorts/JSJwQthWrZs People have been, to put it mildly, thirsting over Mandy since GTA 6 came out. However, Shoaibi had no idea she was going to be in GTA 6 at all because when she auditioned, she signed what she described as an "incredibly" strict NDA. In fact, she didn't even know what she was auditioning for. Her commercial agent in New York brought it to her, and she thought it would be "just like any other commercial audition." From the time she auditioned until the game debuted on November 19, Shoaibi did not know she was going to be in GTA 6. Prince William and Princess Kate attend The Earthshot Prize Awards Ceremony at the Jio World Convention Centre on November 17, 2026 in Mumbai, India.

Kate’s carefully curated wardrobe for the trip wasn’t just about power dressing—it was also about showing she can be sustainable as well as on trend.

She has learned lessons the hard way. She is often seen bending down, talking to children, so she’s conscious of how low a neckline is, how short a skirt is.”.

Princess Kate visits the Nowrosjee Wadia Maternity Hospital, on November 18, 2026 in Mumbai, India.

According to recent reports, for her visit to Mumbai’s Nowrosjee Wadia Maternity Hospital on November 18, Catherine chose a striking red tailored Emilia Wickstead skirt suit with Manolo Blahnik pumps. On November 16, she opted for a pistachio blazer by designer Veronica Beard, paired with white Alexander McQueen trousers and pearl-buckled Camilla Elphick flats, a relaxed and accessible look for when she picked up a cricket bat.

Princess Kate plays cricket on November 16, 2026 in Mumbai, India.

As Princess of Wales, Catherine is often compared to Princess Diana. “The main difference is Diana was a fashion icon. Catherine has become a style icon,” Wakeley notes. “There’s a big difference. Diana played into the fashion of the day and was finding her style. During the time she resigned from public life, she worked out her style DNA. Catherine has had to do that on the job. 💡 Key Takeaways
  • Spoilers for "The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping" ahead.
  • It's obvious why prequels are appealing.
  • In a recent development, in contrast, you have the "Hunger Games" film prequels, which actually flesh out the inhabitants and world of Panem in meaningful ways.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Spoilers for "The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping" ahead.

It's obvious why prequels are appealing. After all, they allow you to see more of the characters you love in situations that are (hopefully) less miserable than the ones you previously saw them in. The problem with prequels is that they often offer origin stories and explanations for details that no one asked about. This is how we end up with stuff like, perhaps most infamously, the bizarre explanation for how Han Solo got his name in "Solo: A Star Wars Story.".

In a recent development, in contrast, you have the "Hunger Games" film prequels, which actually flesh out the inhabitants and world of Panem in meaningful ways. Take "The Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes," which is good enough to get you rooting for the "Hunger Games" franchise's major bad, Coriolanus Snow, as a young man despite knowing how monstrous he eventually becomes. It also reveals how the Games themselves came to be after nearly being canceled once upon a time. Notably, these explanations feel natural and crucial to the movie's story, as opposed to coming across as forced connections to the previous "Hunger Games" films.

The trend continues with "Sunrise on the Reaping," a fantastic movie that makes Haymitch Abernathy not only a hugely notable character to the overall "Hunger Games" saga but one of its saddest, too. (If anything, this film demonstrates he should be drinking more as an older man in the prior movies.) It even turns Plutarch Heavensbee into this franchise's version of Luthen Rael from "Andor," depicting him as a revolutionary stuck behind enemy lines and burning for a sunrise he'll never see.

And on top of all of that, it gives us the last backstory we expected — one for the gap in Haymitch's teeth when he's older.

In a recent development, joseph Zada does a very good job in "The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping" as Haymitch, making the character his own to embody this particular period in the character's life. At the same time, he does capture a lot of Woody Harrelson's mannerisms as Haymitch from the original "Hunger Games" quadrilogy, including his voice. That being stated, there is no denying that Zada does not look that much like Harrelson — especially with his curls and noticeable lack of a gap between his two front teeth, which is Harrelson's most distinguishable facial feature.

Sources indicate that however, rather than relying on viewers' suspension of disbelief, "Sunrise on the Reaping" actually closes the gap (pun intended) between the two actors. In the film, Haymitch is beaten within an inch of his life right before winning the titular Games, at which point he sets off an explosion as a final act of defiance. As a result, he's knocked unconscious, only to wake up later with his wounds having been stitched shut. Even so, he looks different now, with the impact of the explosion having broken his nose and smashed his teeth.

It has been revealed that this is the "Hunger Games" equivalent of Hercule Poirot's mustache getting a gritty origin story tied to the horrors of WWI in Kenneth Branagh's "Death on the Nile" film adaptation, only here, it somehow works. It's because Haymitch examining his teeth is a blink-and-you-miss it detail, as opposed to one that the movie draws heavy attention to. Thus, there's no grand score announcing this as something important (like when River Phoenix's young Indy gets his scar and hat in "Indiana Jones and the Last Crusade"). Instead, it's simply showing the natural aftermath of a brutal fight.

It has been revealed that is it silly? Sure, but it works.
