📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

My elderly mom, who has been deeply unwell for a number of years, has recently started clenching her hands into balls and curling her feet inward like little hooks. Her gerontologist mentioned that, horribly enough, her mind is no longer sending a message to her body that she needs to relax. Medicine can’t help, she explained, but massage might. So one evening, I turned to Google Maps, where I increasingly find everything from authentic Thai restaurants to the best place to buy youth soccer cleats. I guided the map app to the Upper West Side, one of the country’s most expensive neighborhoods, and put one word in the search bar: “massage.”.

Then I squinted. Why was the massage table at “Ashley massage and spa” lit by dark purple light? And why did another listing have photos of the masseuse herself in skin-tight exercise wear, with directions to contact her on Telegram? But it all became clearer when I spotted a description of the type of massage services offered: “I’m available for deep tissue, Swedish, or any kind of massage appointment with a happy ending.”.

Even if nothing should surprise us anymore about our tech overlords, I was still pretty shocked to find that Google Maps appeared to be the new Craigslist, famous for its battle with regulators over sex work classifieds. Somewhere between figuring out the location of the neighborhood CVS and “coffee near me,” it seems like Google branched out. I’d always assumed it adhered to local laws—sex work is illegal in New York state—but perhaps Silicon Valley’s fave “we’re just a platform not a publisher” defense applied here. Otherwise, why on earth was the algorithm retrieving sex work listings when I was just trying to help my 84-year-old mom?

I emailed Google PR to ask what, exactly, was going on, giving them a deadline of the next day to respond.

According to recent reports, the response came from a senior publicist, swiftly. “Hi Vanessa - I'm on the Google Comms team. Would you be able to provide the listings and screenshots?”.

According to recent reports, I did so, then received another response: “I’m reviewing all of this, but wondering if you have wiggle room in your deadline? Want to make sure I can get you the right info in time, and I think that timing tomorrow may be challenging.”.

I responded that I could wait until a couple more days to find out what Google had to say.

In the meantime, I contacted some experts.

Mike Blumenthal has been studying Google Maps almost since it existed. A co-founder of Near Media, he began writing about the product in 2005 and notes he first documented large-scale spam on Maps in New York City in 2009. When I showed him the strange massage listings I’d found scattered across New York, he wasn’t particularly surprised. Google Maps is an extraordinarily valuable way to get in front of customers, which gives gray and black market businesses a powerful incentive to game it. Once they figure out how to convince Google’s algorithm that real people should be directed to those listings, “they can make bank.”.

According to recent reports, google removes an enormous amount of fake listings, reviews and images, and has tightened its verification procedures over the years, mentioned Blumenthal. But when those systems fail, enforcement is largely reactive. Even Blumenthal, who has volunteered in Google’s forums for nineteen years and knows how to escalate a complaint, said getting suspicious listings removed can take upwards of a month or six weeks. When a problem attracts press attention, though, he indicates Google can act within hours. What Google doesn’t do, in his view, is spend enough to prevent the same problems from recurring. “They won’t put in place systemic fixes. They won’t put in place people to deal with this swiftly…They don’t want the cost.”.

After I talked to Blumenthal, I read the reviews of some of the massage businesses that Google Maps was serving up nationwide. Not all were positive. One reviewer of the “Asian Palace Spa” in San Francisco, writing five years ago, gave the business one star and called it a “fraud,” saying he had paid for an hour-long massage but received only 15 minutes before being asked for additional money for “extra services.” The review had received 17 likes. Another one-star reviewer from the same period stated, “they don’t have spa, just pay for room and then pay for lady for whatever you do.”.

Sources indicate that but many more of the illicit massage businesses had positive reviews, about services that were above and beyond, with smiley kissy face icons attached. Were these just independent sex workers trying to make a living? Was it so wrong that they were using Google Maps to find clients? Perhaps it’s needless to say, but when I called several of the phone numbers and introduced myself as a reporter, information was not forthcoming.

I started to feel a little queasy as I reviewed a listing that was clearly written by a woman working for herself, just trying to make a listing. But then, as I looked more closely at others, I realized that the photos were so similar, and the setups of the listings so close to each other, that they must be coordinated by an organized group. Whether that was a lead-generator for escorts who needed extra clients, or a scammer, or a sex trafficker, I couldn’t tell.

I searched for illicit massage listings in different cities, and found them all over neighborhoods in Los Angeles, from Beverly Hills to Koreatown. I also began to notice that most of the massage spots seemed as though they were unlikely to actually be located in the spots they claimed to be. For example, a masseuse who appeared to be nude from breastbone up, with a butterfly tattoo decorating her clavicle, located her business on the Upper East Side’s Museum Mile, home to multimillion dollar apartments and Latest York’s great cultural institutions, but she also included information about a certain corner in Queens, where it seemed like she could’ve also set up shop.

It has been revealed that now that I had more information, I tried to understand whether Google Maps bore any responsibility for these listings, calling Chelsea Binns, a professor at John Jay College of Criminal Justice who studies cybercrime. “It’s interesting from an anti-fraud perspective, because we rely on Google Maps virtually every day now,” she said, taking the call from Japan. “No one takes out a hard map anymore. And there’s a bit of borrowed credibility, because these listings are on Google. It’s Google Maps!”.

Despite this, Binns indicates responsibility rests with each individual user to decipher the legitimacy of a Google Maps business, a caveat emptor situation. “A lot of us don’t read disclaimers, but somewhere deep within the service it says they’re not at fault,” explains Binns. “It’s ‘use at your own risk, research independently, and verify.’”.

According to recent reports, “But why don’t they care if it’s an illegal service?” I ask. “They wouldn’t have guns on there.”.

It has been revealed that “They do care,” says Binns. “They actively review their content. I suspect this slipped through the cracks. But at some point you’re just playing whack-a-mole. You take one down, and another pops up.”.

It has been revealed that this was the perspective of AI-critic Brian Merchant, creator of the Blood in the Machine podcast and newsletter. “As [Google] has moved their resources into moderating, training, and shipping AI, I would not be surprised if resources that were dedicated to moderating are falling off, and things are just staying up longer,” he states. “And maybe criminal organizations have been emboldened, realizing that they can get their links listed higher and longer, and it’ll be weeks before they’re taken down.”.

In a recent development, but the next time I checked out the massage listings near my mom’s apartment, almost all had disappeared. And I heard back from Google with a statement: “Google Maps only displays places that people can visit or interact with in the real world, and we've removed the businesses that do not exist at these locations.”.

Sources indicate that this seemed to indicate that Google had taken action to remove listings in my mom’s neighborhood, and that I was also correct when I noticed that some of the sex workers weren’t actually in the locations they mentioned they were. Google also directed me to their policies against adult-themed content, which explain that no one uploading listings can violate local laws, especially in the areas of “alcohol, gambling, tobacco, guns, health and medical devices, regulated pharmaceuticals, adult services, and financial services.”.

Sources indicate that A Google spokesperson further pushed back against Mike Blumenthal’s contention that the company doesn’t want to incur costs monitoring Google Maps, noting, “we placed posting restrictions on more than 782,000 policy-violating accounts and removed over 13 million fake Business Profiles, further defending genuine businesses on Maps. We blocked or removed over 292 million policy-violating reviews, while publishing more than 1 billion helpful reviews.” Google also added, “we hold bad actors accountable through account suspension and litigation. We display alerts to let you know if we've recently removed suspicious five-star reviews in certain circumstances. These warnings help you understand quickly if a place may be engaging in unfair review practices.”.

They also directed me to their policies against adult-themed content, which explain that no one uploading listings can violate local laws, especially in the areas of “alcohol, gambling, tobacco, guns, health and medical devices, regulated pharmaceuticals, adult services, and financial services.”.

Sources indicate that I contacted Danielle Citron, a professor at the University of Virginia School of Law, to understand more. She said that Google’s statement made sense. “Ordering, filtering, and otherwise structuring the presentation of content” is likely to be shielded as “publishing and speaking” under Section 230, the law that protects tech platforms from liability for user-uploaded content, she said. But there could be a wrinkle. “A different question is getting paid for and designing systems in a particular way, [which] may not be immunized,” she explains, mentioning social media cases like Newly introduced Mexico v. Meta, “where [a lawsuit challenging platform design] was permitted to go to trial because it was about what Meta did in their design of sites, not what owners did to kids.” So a question could potentially be asked by attorneys in the future along these lines: Is the very structure of Google Maps allowing gray and black market businesses to flourish?

In a recent development, within a week, some listings that Google removed when I last checked seemed to have popped up in New York again, but there were far less of them. Still, I found it confounding that in trying to find a massage for my mom, I had uncovered a network of massage spots that a less savvy consumer than myself might have imagined were legitimate. “We really need a better understanding of this landscape, because we need to look out for the consumer,” Binns told me. “Your mom is someone who is vulnerable in society, and that can take many forms. She’s perhaps incapable of doing the due diligence that’s required just to get an ordinary service.”.

At the same time, I was aware that no one wants to change Google’s algorithm to the point that it screws over legitimate small businesses that rely on the visibility of Google Maps. Blumenthal explained the conundrum to me this way: if Google tightens their mapping search controls too much, “businesses’ reality becomes worse, because you can’t get into [Maps]. If they loosen it, consumers’ reality becomes worse, because shit gets in.”.

According to recent reports, after all of this back and forth, I still had to solve my initial problem: securing a massage for my mom. I contacted a few spots in her neighborhood that looked legitimate, but they stated she’d have to raise herself on the massage table, which, since she’s in a wheelchair, wouldn’t work. I decided to reach out to her Medicare-supplied occupational therapist, who got back to me right away.

He mentioned he’d been meaning to call. He needed to send me a form saying that my mom was no longer able to participate in the exercises they were performing together, and she’d likely be kicked off Medicare payment for them in the near future. That was a bummer, and made me regret calling him at all, but I figured while I had him on the line I’d ask another question: Does Medicare (original, parts A & B) cover therapeutic massage? He said no, apologetically.

I’d spent a week investigating a system that made it remarkably easy to sell massages that weren't massages, only to discover how difficult it was to obtain one that was.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • For the last 25 years, nearly every noxious gamer stereotype had a home in Grand Theft Auto.
  • Sources indicate that this, for the most part, suited Grand Theft Auto’s publisher just fine.
  • But with Grand Theft Auto VI, something has changed.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

For the last 25 years, nearly every noxious gamer stereotype had a home in Grand Theft Auto. Juvenile, sexist, crass, embarrassing—people could accuse the games of being these things because the allegations were, in part, true. Beginning with 2001’s Grand Theft Auto III, the series began giving players the freedom to wreak havoc across satirical renditions of US cities. It was an amazing technical feat that only grew more impressive with each subsequent Grand Theft Auto game—and harder to appreciate the more those cities were filled with dick jokes and sex workers.

Sources indicate that this, for the most part, suited Grand Theft Auto’s publisher just fine. What business did the company have calling itself Rockstar Games if it cared what a bunch of prudes thought?

But with Grand Theft Auto VI, something has changed. And the game’s staggering launch-day revenue—$3.79 billion—suggests that this change was a welcome one.

Industry observers note that rockstar has executed an astonishing about-face in Grand Theft Auto VI, choosing to build a game around a couple depicted with aching sincerity—from their car-boosting meet-cute to the desperate stickups they commit, with the player’s help. Jason Duval (played by Dylan Rourke) and Lucia Caminos (Manni L. Perez) are a modern-day Bonnie and Clyde, out of options and on the run, hoping they can land a score big enough to turn things around.

Recent findings suggest that this earnestness is new for Grand Theft Auto, which historically has had a deep love for pushing buttons. (Its sister series, the Western Red Dead Redemption, has less of a problem with heart-on-the-sleeve storytelling.) Lucia, especially, is new. She’s the first woman you can play as in the series, and by the transitive property, she’s also the first woman that Grand Theft Auto has ever had to take seriously. Doing so changes the entire shape of the series.

Until now, Grand Theft Auto has never really thought much of women. True, the games have never thought much of anyone; Rockstar traffics in a nihilistic comedy that lies somewhere between South Park and a Verhoeven film, a dim view of the United States where everyone sucks. But women, usually, have sucked the most. They’ve been the butts of countless jokes; in the Grand Theft Auto universe, they’ve been nags and drags and sex workers secondary to the men that the games were about. Grand Theft Auto III, a game that barely has a plot, begins with main character Clyde’s girlfriend betraying him after a heist, shooting him and calling him “small time” before running off with the take. It doesn’t get much better from there.

In a recent development, so yes: Lucia is a huge pivot for the series, especially because Grand Theft Auto VI doesn’t trust players with her right away. After a brief prologue in which a desperate stickup goes wrong, Lucia is sent to jail and players begin the game as her boyfriend Jason Duval. In addition to doing odd jobs for a small-time crime boss (Stephen Root) and hanging out with your pal (Bobby Moynihan), players have to choose: Are they going to be a good boyfriend? Rockstar Games know they might be making a big ask of their audience, so they slow-roll it. Before Lucia gets out of jail, the game suggests to the player, maybe fix the stairs? Or get a haircut? Buy her a necklace?

In the days since the game came out, many have noted how amusing it is that Grand Theft Auto VI has made caring about your girlfriend one of its first challenges. The game’s “Lucia will appreciate this” notification is its first viral meme, and the source of both incel crashouts (“woke slop … so obvious it was made by women”) and earnest appreciation. (One of the first clips to spread online was of streamer Stable Ronaldo painting Jason and Lucia's bedroom one color before recoiling in horror: What if she hates that shade?).

Recent findings suggest that lucia is a destabilizing event not just for gamers, but for Grand Theft Auto—a damning yet fascinating example of gaming culture’s priorities on its biggest stage. GTA has always been a series of warring ambitions: violent Rube Goldberg machine, Karl Ove Knausgaard–esque obsession with quotidian details, and thrilling Hollywood blockbuster all in one. These disparate aims are often in conflict with one another, and one way to read the series’ heretofore exclusively male focus is as an attempt to thread this needle. By tossing all of its commentary under the carpet of “satire," Rockstar can also use a veneer of meanness to argue that the games’ misogyny is actually an intentional lambasting, much like everything else in GTA.

But taking a woman seriously, and making her colead with a male character, requires an entire rethinking of what Grand Theft Auto is. “It’s a product of the story we’re trying to tell,” Grand Theft Auto VI codirector Rob Nelson said when asked by The Guardian if this is the first Grand Theft Auto to encourage empathy from players. “We’ve tried for the first time in a GTA to provide mechanisms that encourage it, for those who want to.”.

This is an extremely roundabout way of saying that, in this Grand Theft Auto, Rockstar asks gamers to grow up—and punishes them with narrative consequences if they don’t take the game up on the offer.

It has been revealed that the funny thing about Grand Theft Auto VI’s gamified empathy is that, like everything else in a video game, it has to teach the player how to accomplish that goal. The game does this through prompting players to do chores, but also through Jason’s characterization. Throughout the game, Rockstar has to convey what its writers believe a well-adjusted man looks like—or at least what constitutes a man well-adjusted enough to earn the respect of a woman like Lucia, who walks out on him when he tries to exclude her from some of his more dangerous criminal activities.

Sources indicate that to that end, there are an abundance of moments in the game where Jason demonstrates the virtues of being respectful and maintaining boundaries, several of which are a departure from GTA series norms. There are no sex workers in the game anymore (though there are strip clubs). While Jason and Lucia can break up depending on the player’s choices, there are no other options for committed or casual romance.

Industry observers note that the money you steal is ostensibly for Jason and Lucia to use together: so they can get away and start over with their young son, who’s presently entrusted to a relative. Casual conversations between strangers players meet on the road make Jason’s respectful nature both a point and a punchline. There’s one man who’s looking for his missing wife after a night of partying. When he starts to brag about her sexual dexterity, Jason interjects to say, “Hey. Let’s draw a line, bud.”.

Industry observers note that in some ways, this is all rather embarrassing—though in a different way than the weapons-grade sexism of Grand Theft Autos past. One ought to feel a twinge of shame while marveling at any entertainment franchise for including a woman. Yet Grand Theft Auto VI is being graded on a curve. It has a near-perfect Metacritic score in large part for its depiction of Lucia, and for Jason’s relationship to her. The context speaks to a state of arrested development, both in Grand Theft Auto and in major-budget games writ large.

Sources indicate that none of this changes the fact that Lucia really is one of the most well-realized video game characters in a digital city unlike any other. But perhaps her inclusion is less an apology for GTA’s past, and more of a concession to how out of step the series had become with the culture. Because if you’re meant to have empathy for one character, the natural next question is, “Well, what about everyone else?".

It has been revealed that rockstar’s maniacal pursuit of verisimilitude goes a long way here. The game’s animations are so realistic that in GTA VI, shooting unarmed civilians is legitimately unsettling. It’s also disincentivized by a “criminal profile” rating that will mark your character “irredeemable” if you engage in too much wanton violence. (This is not a “game over”—it merely locks players out of achieving a happy ending unless they restart from before their murder spree.) These sorts of limits have become another reliable source of outrage directed at the game, with rage baiters drumming up controversy over Rockstar’s decision to, for example, not permit players to shoot up a nightclub.

According to recent reports, this is the tricky reality of encouraging empathy for “those who want to,” as Nelson put it. Rockstar has certain intentions, but so do players—and managing both is the great challenge of making any video game. Empathy is a shock to GTA’s system and to the audience alike.

In a recent development, replicating humanity with computer software is a daunting and costly task, and one that only Rockstar seems to have the limitless resources to pursue. Those resources—the luxury to work as long as necessary to complete Grand Theft Auto VI, and the obscene amount of money it cost (our only solid figure is “less than $1.5 billion”)—are rapidly dwindling in the video game business, as all available tech funding is vacuumed up by AI companies and private equity loots what’s left. Grand Theft Auto VI may very well be one of one: the most expensive game ever and the last of its kind, the peak of Rockstar’s ambition and also of every big-budget video game. Here, at the end of everything, the biggest of video games has finally decided that it’s time to try empathy. And for a woman, even, should gamers choose (and not all will).

Industry observers note that it’s a bit of an indictment of the billion-dollar video game industry that the most expensive game in history is also the first major game to commit to a realistic heterosexual relationship. Grand Theft Auto VI deserves many of the accolades it instantly garnered upon release, but the nature of its accomplishment is not yet fully understood. It’s possible that what Rockstar has built is less a monument to video games’ potential than a magnificent funeral pyre, a testament to how things might’ve turned out if Rockstar’s priorities—and those of everyone chasing after its vision of what video games could be—were just a little bit different.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Sources indicate that marvel Studios president Kevin Feige and directors Anthony and Joe Russo are planning to include a tribute to Stewart in the upcoming superhero blockbuster, according to a newly introduced interview with Variety.
  • Industry observers note that the actor had already completed filming for Doomsday, in which he reprises his iconic role as Professor Charles Xavier for the ninth and final time.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Patrick Stewart's final on-screen performance will arrive in December's Avengers: Doomsday, and Marvel is making sure the late actor receives a fitting farewell.

Sources indicate that marvel Studios president Kevin Feige and directors Anthony and Joe Russo are planning to include a tribute to Stewart in the upcoming superhero blockbuster, according to a newly introduced interview with Variety. Stewart died on Oct. 29 at age 86 following a brief battle with Alzheimer's disease and Lewy Body Dementia.

Industry observers note that the actor had already completed filming for Doomsday, in which he reprises his iconic role as Professor Charles Xavier for the ninth and final time. Speaking to Variety, Feige revealed that Stewart's last day on set was an emotional occasion, with the actor delivering a speech to the crew.

"He stood up and he gave a speech to the crew," Feige mentioned. "We didn't know necessarily it would be his last day on a set, but he was sort of indicating to us that he thought it was.".

In a recent development, anthony Russo also recalled how difficult filming had become for Stewart as he struggled with his health. Despite the challenges, the actor remained committed to delivering his performance.

"For him to have muscled through and delivered the performance that he did in that movie, and the experience that he delivered for all of us as collaborators, it made it intensely emotional," Russo noted.

Although principal photography has wrapped, Feige stated Marvel is now figuring out how to properly honor its longtime collaborator.

"We're long done filming that movie, and he did an amazing job for us," Feige told Variety. "We're looking now at how we can put something together that honors and respects our friend.".

It has been revealed that the tribute will carry particular significance given Stewart's history with the X-Men franchise. He first played Professor X in 2000's X-Men, becoming one of the defining faces of the superhero series alongside Ian McKellen's Magneto. The two actors will reunite in Doomsday, with Joe Russo revealing that their characters share an emotional scene about forgiveness.

"In a lot of ways, Xavier's the conscience in the movie," Russo remarked. "He has a lovely scene with Ian McKellen, who's his best friend, in the film. It's a very emotional scene about forgiveness, and I think very resonant in the wake of his passing.".

Stewart's death prompted an outpouring of tributes from fans, fellow actors, and gaming communities. Players of No Man's Sky, for example, began naming planets and entire star systems after the actor, with some creating virtual memorials inspired by his portrayal of Captain Jean-Luc Picard in Star Trek: The Next Generation.

Avengers: Doomsday arrives in theaters on Dec. 18.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Early in "Cliff Booth," we're introduced to Charlie Peters, a hot-tempered TV star played by Scott Caan.
  • Fans of "Once Upon a Time in Hollywood" will recall that Tarantino also provided narration in that movie, too.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Quentin Tarantino has returned to the world of "Once Upon a Time in Hollywood" with "The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth" (why not read our review of the upcoming movie here?). But this time, while Tarantino penned the script, he isn't in the director's chair. Instead, he's handed directing duties over to his pal David Fincher (who is ending his exclusive deal with Netflix with the film). Tarantino might not be behind the camera, but he still has a presence in the film, and it echoes something he did in "Hollywood" as well.

Early in "Cliff Booth," we're introduced to Charlie Peters, a hot-tempered TV star played by Scott Caan. To speed-run us through Charlie's successful career, we're given a little montage of his various roles, and that montage is narrated by none other than Tarantino, whose very recognizable voice provides some humorous details about Charlie's work.

Fans of "Once Upon a Time in Hollywood" will recall that Tarantino also provided narration in that movie, too. He actually wasn't the only narrator, either, because during one scene, Kurt Russell, who plays a stuntman named Randy in that film, also provides a little narration. As for Tarantino, he also voiced some crucial narration during a pivotal scene in "The Hateful Eight.".

In a recent development, in fact, the filmmaker has a history of popping up in his movies, either via a voice cameo or a physical appearance. He has a pretty significant role in "Reservoir Dogs," makes a memorable cameo in "Pulp Fiction," gets to use an abysmal Australian accent in "Django Unchained," has his voice heard during a movie playing in "Inglourious Basterds" (and also plays a corpse in the film), plays a bartender in "Death Proof," portrays one of the members of the Crazy 88 gang in "Kill Bill," and lends his voice to an answering machine in "Jackie Brown.".

So while "The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth" may not technically be a Quentin Tarantino movie, it still feels like one, right down to the obligatory cameo.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • What's a worse fate in the world of "Blade Runner," to be human or to be a Replicant?
  • Sources indicate that leave it to "Blade Runner 2099" to flip yet another classic franchise staple on its head.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

I've seen spoilers you people wouldn't believe. This article discusses major plot details from all eight episodes of "Blade Runner 2099.".

What's a worse fate in the world of "Blade Runner," to be human or to be a Replicant? Throughout both films, organics in this post-apocalyptic setting were able to "enjoy" their time at the top of the food chain. That all changes in Prime Video's "Blade Runner 2099," the live-action story taking place after the world order has been upended and our supposed underlings have gained all the power for themselves. While Replicants were built to be "more human than human," the subtle differences between the two kinds are all but impossible to detect — on the surface, at least. But, as we know, looks can be deceiving; what's underneath is another matter entirely.

Sources indicate that leave it to "Blade Runner 2099" to flip yet another classic franchise staple on its head. Traditionally, the purposefully off-putting questionnaire known as the Voight-Kampff test was meant to detect whether an individual is a Replicant or not. In the sci-fi series, the rise of the Replicants and the 50 years that have passed since "Blade Runner 2049" have introduced even more changes. Enter the Index Test, an inverted form of the established quiz. But rather than differentiate between the two beings, this test is meant to detect whether the subject has developed feelings of empathy towards humans.

According to recent reports, in Episode 5, titled "My Lord," we learn far more about this strange newly introduced setup than the show had previously revealed. All we ever saw was the unusually young human girl administering the test, the odd non sequiturs she posed to (supposed) Replicants like Hunter Schafer's Cora, and the results of whether they passed the baseline or not. But that, too, was only scratching the surface.

Industry observers note that of all the differences between humans and Replicants, empathy is the biggest of them all. "Blade Runner 2099" draws fairly stark lines in the sand between the two, with flesh-and-blood people now completely helpless before their bioengineered creations. But despite their physical advantages and killer instincts, Replicants' lack of a childhood means they're deficit in that crucial, compassionate emotion separating humans from all other living things. As we soon learn, however, Replicants can feel these strong feelings ... and actually fear it, too.

This is all summed up in the storyline involving Greta (Katelyn Rose Downey), the young human girl we learn has been sold off into indentured servitude and indoctrinated along with many others into administering Index Tests. Episode 5 peels back all the horrifying layers, showing us Greta's training under awfully unsettling circumstances. First, she's taken through a museum exhibit explaining the purpose and history of the Voight-Kampff test, used by human Blade Runners to hunt Replicants. Now, the new status quo means Replicants use this new Index Test to police their own kind — and, as one instructor explains, prevent any "emotional contagion" crossing over from humans to their Replicant overlords.

It has been revealed that it's a fascinating idea with some pretty serious implications for our two main characters. Michelle Yeoh's Olwen is currently undergoing some serious emotional turmoil herself, as her search for the missing Replicant and her secret lover Marek (Johnny Harris) ends in his tragic death. Meanwhile, Cora's own emotional attachments makes it only a matter of time before her human identity is made known. As a result, every time they sit down for the Index Test makes for must-watch TV.

All eight episodes of "Blade Runner 2099" are streaming on Prime Video.

  • The mastermind behind the mega-medley is none other than Tom Kitt, the Tony-, Emmy-, Grammy-, and Pulitzer Prize–winning composer behind Next to Normal, If/Then, and Almost Famous.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that this year’s Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade is going to look a bit different. First, the threat of severe weather has prompted Macy’s to reschedule the event until Saturday, beginning at 8:30 a.m. ET. But even before the forecast turned, there was a big change: While in the past, viewers would enjoy five or so of the best performances from the current Broadway season, this year, there’s only one big Broadway number. But don’t fret, theater folk. For the milestone occasion of the parade’s 100th anniversary, the powers that be at NBC and Macy’s have put a new spin on their tried-and-true formula, gathering the Broadway community for one supersized performance, featuring more shows and performers than ever before.

The result is an epic 10-minute medley, introduced by Julianne Hough, who will star in Damn Yankees on Broadway this spring, featuring nine beloved Broadway shows: The Book of Mormon, Chicago, Disney’s Aladdin, Hamilton, The Lost Boys, Rent, Richard O’Brien’s The Rocky Horror Show, Schmigadoon!, and—what else?—Wicked.

The mastermind behind the mega-medley is none other than Tom Kitt, the Tony-, Emmy-, Grammy-, and Pulitzer Prize–winning composer behind Next to Normal, If/Then, and Almost Famous. Kitt is no stranger to writing a big production number, having cowritten the Tony Awards opening number “Bigger!,” performed by host Neil Patrick Harris with lyrics by Lin-Manuel Miranda in 2013, among other ambitious musical endeavors. Despite his previous experience, a 10-minute, nine-show medley presented a unique set of challenges the composer had yet to tackle.

Sources indicate that A total of 133 people are performing in the medley—114 Broadway cast members, 17 dancers, a child actor, and Hough. On top of that, more than 125 other Broadway professionals—including stage managers, wardrobe supervisors, and hair and makeup teams—are on site to facilitate the production, bringing the total number of people involved to well over 250.

Recent findings suggest that “Most crucial to me in doing something like this—to celebrate this community, this beautiful community that I’m so lucky to be a part of,” Kitt tells me. “Everyone who’s participating, you want them to feel happy and excited about what they’re doing.”.

A little over a month ago, Kitt and creative producer Sarah O’Gleby got to work figuring out how to make a cohesive musical number out of nine very different shows. He wrote the first draft of the arrangement over the course of a few days. “It was way too long,” he says. That might be because Kitt had to figure out how to connect these disparate shows musically while also finding room for Easter eggs for theater fans: musical nods to shows that might not otherwise be featured in the medley, including Anything Goes, The Music Man, A Chorus Line, and Kitt’s personal favorite, Into the Woods, whose music kicks things off.

It has been revealed that “Into the Woods was one of those highlights that made me want to write for the theater,” he tells me. “The downbeat of the prologue is one of the most beautiful musical gestures; every time I hear it, I get goosebumps. So that was really special and notable for me to get to plug into, and there are so many others.”.

It has been revealed that surprisingly, it will be Kitt’s first time attending the parade in person. “The parade has meant so much to me,” he says. “I’ve watched it for years. I’ve taped it. I’m lucky enough to have shows that have been a part of it. I think that celebrating that relationship and celebrating the history of Broadway and being able to spotlight so many notable shows and artists just feels very exciting and gratifying.”.

According to recent reports, “I’m a tiny little person, but I love to do really massive things,” notes O’Gleby. A former performer on the West End, O’Gleby moved to the States almost two decades ago to pursue a career as a Broadway performer, dancing in revivals of Brigadoon and How to Succeed in Business Without Really Trying. Now she choreographs Broadway productions like Shucked and, most recently, Pink’s widely celebrated Tony Awards opening number. Given her Broadway bona fides, she’s also intimately familiar with the magic of the parade. “I was lucky to perform on the parade as a Broadway girl and the associate choreographer and dance captain on reveals that I was in,” she says. “It was so wonderfully American.”.

The first of two rehearsals took place Friday afternoon at Pier59 Studios at Chelsea Piers. Around 4 p.m., as the sun began to set over the Hudson River, Broadway performers from different reveals practiced the medley. O’Gleby, wearing silver leather pants and clutching a God mic, was charged with organizing the chaos and managing the more than 100 Broadway performers in the room. Standing offstage between a broomstick and a red Les Mis flag, I could still see traces of green makeup on the face of Wicked’s current Elphaba, Keri René Fuller. Most of the performers gathered had a show of their own to perform in just a few hours, but that didn’t stop them from giving it their all in rehearsal, onstage and off, cheering the other productions along as each got its moment in the spotlight.

Industry observers note that case in point: At the end of the rehearsal, the whole room erupted into cheers for the original cast members from Rent—including original Angel, Tony winner Wilson Jermaine Heredia, and original Joanne, Fredi Walker—who are gathering to perform “Seasons of Love” in the parade. (During the rehearsal, Aladdin’s current Genie, Sherri Shepherd, couldn’t help but mouth along to the words of the seminal song.) “It was that moment of why we’re a part of this community,” O’Gleby states, nearly choking up. “Everyone in the room—stage managers, costume, I mean everybody in the room—the way they were applauding these original cast members and what they gave to all of us as a community, really all over the world, it was incredible.”.

It has been revealed that at the second rehearsal, on Monday night outside on 34th Street beneath Macy’s giant turkey, the mood remained high even as the temperatures dropped. By 11 p.m., performers were bundled in winter jackets, sweatshirts, and leg warmers, with their character shoes still on. They hugged one another for warmth and jumped up and down, kicking their feet to stay loose between setups. Margaret Cho, who stars as the Narrator in The Rocky Horror Show, danced “The Time Warp” with her Chihuahua, Lucia, tucked into a pouch in her jacket, the dog’s head peeking out.

Sources indicate that for O’Gleby, a smooth Monday-night rehearsal means setting each show up for success come Saturday morning and making sure all nine shows are “represented in the most powerful and clear storytelling way that we can,” she notes. “This is a huge moment for these shows to sell lots of tickets so everyone gets to keep making their magic every night. And so it’s important to me that each team gets to communicate what they need and what they think would really make their show shine.”.

On Wednesday afternoon, Macy's announced that “after close consultation with our City and agency partners, we have made the decision to move this year’s celebration,” a disappointing piece of news for those who build their holiday around the annual event.

In a recent development, this is only the fourth time in history that the parade hasn't been held on Thanksgiving: In 1942, 1943, and 1944 it was canceled completely as its trademark giant balloons were repurposed as part of the World War II effort. Compared to those years, a move to Saturday seems manageable, O’Gleby says. “The weather will be what it will be, but we will delight in that and deliver the best.".

Tech Report: All Peewees Billboard locations in GTA 6

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (797 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Polygon

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Peewees Billboards are one of the many scannable WAiNK collectibles in Grand Theft Auto 6, but they're also part of the Mr.
  • Sources indicate that all the info you're given is that there is a billboard in the following areas: Vice-Dale, Mariana County, Lummox County, and Leonard County.
  • To save you some time, we've listed where you can find every Peewees Billboard in GTA 6 below.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Peewees Billboards are one of the many scannable WAiNK collectibles in Grand Theft Auto 6, but they're also part of the Mr. Enigma X Peewees scavenger hunt. Mr. Enigma, a play on Dr. Pepper, and the Peewees, a play on Popeyes, have teamed up to create a challenge where you must find four Peewees billboards, and you'll earn a valuable reward.

Sources indicate that all the info you're given is that there is a billboard in the following areas: Vice-Dale, Mariana County, Lummox County, and Leonard County. As these areas are fairly large, it can take a long time to find them.

To save you some time, we've listed where you can find every Peewees Billboard in GTA 6 below.

To start the Mr. Enigma X Peewees scavenger hunt, look out for a Peewees post on Snapmatic, or you can look for one of the four Peewees billboards. After you start, you'll get a text from Chicken Challenge, telling you that you've entered the scavenger hunt. They'll also send you a clue that points you toward another billboard when you start the challenge and every time you find one.

In a recent development, there are four Peewees Billboards in GTA 6, with one in Vice-Dale, Mariana County, Lummox County, and Leonard County. To mark them off the list, head to their location and scan them using WAiNK (hold Up on your D-pad).

Below, we explain where you can find each billboard in detail.

Sources indicate that the Vice-Dale Peewees Billboard is on the west side of Balsero, which is the northwest corner of Vice-Dale County. The billboard itself is between Route US-10 and US-35, which is just northwest of Randy's shop.

The Mariana County Peewees Billboard is technically in Big Pine in Grassrivers, but it's very close to the border between Grassrivers and North Mariana County. Along the border, you'll find three dome-shaped buildings and Route US-82. Head northeast of the dome-shaped buildings, and look in the median strip to find this Peewee Billboard.

The Lummox County Peewees Billboard is located on the border between South West Lummox County and Mount Kalaga National Park. The billboard is just west of Route US-628. Head north from the junction that connects US-628 to SR-73, and you'll find the billboard on your left.

The Leonard County Peewees Billboard is located in the northwest corner of Waning Sands. The billboard is just next to SR-27, which is between Lake Leonida and Mount Hailes Club. Look northeast of Lake Leonida, and you'll find the golf course. Follow along the road until you find the Peewees Billboard.

After you find every Peewees Billboard, you'll receive a text from Chicken Challenge, telling you that you won... almost! You just need to solve one more puzzle, but they don't tell you what the puzzle is.

It has been revealed that if you take a look back at the clues that Chicken Challenge has been sending you, you'll notice that a couple of letters in each photo are covered by the Peewees logo. The following letters are blocked off: V - L - I - L - L - E - B - E. Now, it looks like a bunch of gibberish, but if you scramble the letters, you'll get Belville, which is the southern region of Leonard County.

It just so happens that there's a Peewees in Belville.

Sources indicate that to claim your grand prize, you need to head to the Peewees in Belville, which is just east of the hospital. Alternatively, you can open your map, scroll down to the "Fast Food" section of the "Food & Drink" tab, and select the Peewees in Belville to speed up the process.

Head inside and speak with the manager to claim your reward, which is a Peewees hat, a Peewees shirt, and free Peewees food!

It has been revealed that if you're just getting started in GTA 6, we have plenty of guides to help you live the high life in Leonida. Check out our GTA 6 beginner guide to get a grasp of the basics and our tips for what to do first, recommendations for the best ways to make money fast, and an explainer for how to keep stolen weapons and cars to make the most of your free time.

Our selection of GTA 6 guides includes help for things like how to steal the Phoenix in "Unwanted Attention" and whether you should defuse Mandy, too. There's a set of explainers for GTA 6's more open-ended side activities, like how to rob the Exotic Animal Front and where to find tree effigies for the Skunk Ape mission, and we've got all the GTA 6 cheat codes. You'll have to put in some effort before you can use those, though.

#120112. Blade Runner 2099 Proves The Saga Does One Thing Better Than Any Other Sci-Fi Franchise

📅 25 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (866 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Slashfilm ↗ Open Full Page

Blade Runner 2099 Proves The Saga Does One Thing Better Than Any Other Sci-Fi Franchise

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (866 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Slashfilm

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that continuing the legacy of two of the greatest sci-fi movies ever made is a big enough challenge.
  • It's hard to imagine, but "Blade Runner" had a tiny VFX budget.
  • As such, when Denis Villeneuve managed to both emulate the feel of Scott's classic and push the production design in newly introduced directions with "Blade Runner 2049," it was nothing short of a miracle.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that continuing the legacy of two of the greatest sci-fi movies ever made is a big enough challenge. Doing so on the small screen adds an extra element of difficulty. Incredibly, "Blade Runner 2099" has overcome the odds to deliver yet another intoxicating excursion into the techno-industrial urban decay-scape so magically realized back in 1982's "Blade Runner" and so faithfully recreated in 2017's "Blade Runner 2049." As such, the Blade Runner franchise is now surely the most consistent on-screen sci-fi saga ever made. (Setting aside sci-fi sagas that are directed by the same person the whole time, like James Cameron's "Avatar.").

It's hard to imagine, but "Blade Runner" had a tiny VFX budget. Yet director Ridley Scott and his production team managed to create one of the most believable and immersive worlds in cinema history. The famous "Hades" opening shot immediately plunges you into a future post-ecological collapse, in which technology seems to have almost grown on the wreckage of a fallen world like moss on fallen trees. The debris of society is adorned with neon and machinery, creating an environment in which past and future collide. "Blade Runner" might have been buried at the box office by "E.T. The Extra-Terrestrial," but it was an absolutely enthralling sci-fi adventure that came to define the genre.

As such, when Denis Villeneuve managed to both emulate the feel of Scott's classic and push the production design in newly introduced directions with "Blade Runner 2049," it was nothing short of a miracle. The "Dune" director's take on the world first introduced to audiences in 1982 was immediately familiar as the same one in which Harrison Ford's Rick Deckard did battle with Rutger Hauer's Roy Batty and his band of rogue Replicants. Yet it also felt appropriately evolved for the three-decade time jump. Surely "Blade Runner 2099" couldn't pull off the same trick — especially across eight episodes? Well, it has.

/Film's Bill Bria has hailed "Blade Runner 2099" as the best sci-fi show in years, and it's hard to disagree based solely on the production design. From the moment the show begins, we're immersed in the same world to which Ridley Scott introduced us back in 1982. In fact, "2099" recreates the "Hades" sequence so faithfully you'd think you were watching the original. It's a clever move, too. As the camera slow-zooms on the Tyrell Corporation building and evokes the tone and feel of Scott's film, it establishes "2099" as very much belonging to the "Blade Runner" legacy. But we soon discover that this is not Rick Deckard's future.

In a recent development, 80 years after Harrison Ford's Blade Runner absconded with Rachael (Sean Young), Replicants have now overthrown their human masters to become the dominant race. It's a major change that refreshes the franchise and helps make it more relevant than it's ever been at a time when the looming AI garbage future has prompted widespread talk of machines taking our jobs.

As such, it's more key than ever to maintain a tone and design language that's consistent with what came before, so as to reassure fans of the saga that this isn't some sort of wholesale reinvention of the franchise they love, but an evolution that plays out in the same world. "Blade Runner 2099" impressively pulls that off with its opening scene, and it only gets better from there.

In a recent development, when it comes to the world of "Blade Runner," fans know the deal: Retro futurism and cyberpunk aesthetics meet noirish expressionism in a technological nightmare future. Many franchises have tried to emulate the aesthetic to varying degrees of success, but there is only one "Blade Runner." As Christopher Nolan once told the Directors Guild of America while discussing Ridley Scott's film, it conjures "that feeling that there was this whole world outside the frame of the scene. You really felt there were things going on outside of those rooms where you've seen the film take place.".

"Blade Runner 2099" has somehow managed to make every one of its scenes feel like they belong in that same world. With that in mind, it's truly remarkable how consistent the Blade Runner universe has remained across almost a half-century's worth of projects, each of which has been separated by many years. Even the best sci-fi franchises struggle to pull off what is, admittedly, an almost impossible trick.

The "Terminator" movies have never been able to recapture the intoxicating, doom-laden sci-fi slasher tone that made the first two films so memorable. The "Alien" franchise, meanwhile, has made a point of switching up its style and tone with each successive film — though more recent projects have tried to evoke the feeling of the 1979 original. "Blade Runner" films, however, all feel part of a cohesive whole that gives the entire saga this uncanny sense of existing in a real alternate timeline somewhere — as if we're witnessing an epic, decades-spanning dream play out in the mind of a dying Replicant. Regardless of how you feel about "2099" as a whole, its visual and tonal achievements simply can't be denied.

"Blade Runner 2099" Season 1 is now streaming on Prime Video.

The Cliff Booth Movie Brings Back Two Key Characters From Once Upon A Time In Hollywood

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (842 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Slashfilm

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • This article contains spoilers for "The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth.".
  • "The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth" is not a direct sequel to "Once Upon a Time in Hollywood," as we knew from Quentin Tarantino handing over the director's chair to David Fincher.
  • In a recent development, part of the appeal of returning to the world of "Once Upon a Time in Hollywood" is that the movie ended by changing history.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

This article contains spoilers for "The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth.".

"The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth" is not a direct sequel to "Once Upon a Time in Hollywood," as we knew from Quentin Tarantino handing over the director's chair to David Fincher. But still, you had to wonder if any other familiar faces would pop up in this new mis-adventure.

In a recent development, part of the appeal of returning to the world of "Once Upon a Time in Hollywood" is that the movie ended by changing history. Thanks to the actions of Cliff, actress Sharon Tate (Margot Robbie) is not murdered by the Manson family. How does the entertainment world and Los Angeles change by 1977, when "Cliff Booth" takes place, because of that ripple effect? Tarantino wrote the script for "Cliff Booth," and if any filmmaker is equipped to dig into the nitty-gritty of such a change in Hollywood history, down to the most obscure B-pictures and forgotten TV, it's him.

Now, the major supporting cast of "Cliff Booth" is totally different. Cliff's best friend, actor Rick Dalton (Leonardo DiCaprio) — for whom Cliff worked as a stunt double and driver back in 1969 — does not appear due to DiCaprio declining a cameo appearance. The movie mentions a few times that Rick moved to Australia and is presently starring in a popular TV show there, "Dingo Dan." Tarantino has also devised some stories about what happened to Rick after that fateful August 9, 1969 night.

But a few of the fictionalized Hollywood characters return for brief cameos: Margot Robbie as Sharon Tate, Timothy Olyphant as actor James Stacy, and even Nicholas Hammond as TV director Sam Wanamaker (in a smaller role).

One of the Quentin Tarantino Easter eggs in "The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth" is a commercial for Red Apple Cigarettes, a fictional brand that appears in other Tarantino movies. The actress in the commercial is Sharon Tate, with Cliff smiling at her and likely recalling how he saved her life. "Once Upon A Time In Hollywood" cast Sharon Tate in an angelic light, down to giving her the happy ending that reality didn't. But revisiting her in greater depth, like what became of her marriage to Roman Polanski or how her acting career played out, would risk adding a dash of salt to that sweet ending.

Sources indicate that the alternate history of Sharon Tate in "Once Upon a Time in Hollywood" earned obvious comparisons to Tarantino's "Inglourious Basterds," which also starred Brad Pitt (as Lieutenant Aldo Raine, leader of the Nazi-killing Basterds). In that movie, Adolf Hitler (Martin Wutke) dies at the hands of Jewish soldiers instead of by suicide. That leads into Timothy Olyphant's "Cliff Booth" cameo, which feels self-recursively inspired by "Basterds.".

It has been revealed that "Once Upon a Time in Hollywood" mixes real Hollywood history with pastiche. Much of the first half sees Dalton filming a guest spot on a TV Western, "Lancer," which was a real show back in the late '60s. Olyphant appears as the real-life star of "Lancer," James Stacy, and the episode is directed by Nicholas Hammond's Sam Wanamaker, the real director of the "Lancer" pilot episode. "Cliff Booth" gives us another glimpse of Stacy and Wanamaker working in this alternate timeline's television industry.

Industry observers note that since 1969, Cliff Booth has become a fixer: someone who (violently) solves problems for Hollywood fixtures wrapped up with criminals. Fictional TV star Charlie Winters (Scott Caan) becomes one of his clients. The movie includes a newsreel style montage, narrated by Quentin Tarantino himself, recounting Winters' rise to TV stardom.

According to recent reports, one of Winters' highlights is "Enemy Territory," about a U.S. pilot trapped behind enemy lines in Europe during World War 2. The narrator describes the show as "'The Fugitive' with Nazis, but 'The Fugitive' with Nazis is a fun idea." (I'd watch it!) We see Winters shooting a scene where his character threatens a Gestapo officer into helping him rescue a captured American general. The officer is played by none other than Timothy-Olyphant-as-James-Stacy, doing a broad German accent with a high pitch reminiscent of Christoph Waltz's Colonel Hans Landa from "Inglourious Basterds.".

Sam Wanamaker is directing the scene. Stacy's performance is being criticized as "a smidge cavalier" — so Winters puts a live round in the prop gun with which his character is threatening the Gestapo officer. Stacy, sure enough, begins acting like a man whose life is being balanced on the edge of a trigger.

According to recent reports, casting Olyphant as James Stacy was a nod to how his real most famous roles are on Western TV highlights — namely, Sheriff Seth Bullock in HBO's "Deadwood" and Deputy U.S. Marshal Raylan Givens in the Kentucky-set neo-Western "Justified." But Olyphant has got range beyond playing cowboys, and his comic energy in his "Cliff Booth" cameo is just more evidence of that.

"The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth" is playing in theaters, with a Netflix release date of December 23, 2026.

Latest Update: Capcom Is Officially Killing Its 'Jurassic World Meets Overwatch' Shooter

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (569 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Polygon

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that four years after the game's launch, Capcom is officially shutting down Exoprimal, the company's 5v5 action game about a futuristic dinosaur crisis.
  • While disappointing for stalwart Exoprimal fans, the writing has been on the wall since 2024, when Capcom all but confirmed the sci-fi action game's grim fate.
  • It has been revealed that in an official notice posted to the Exoprimal website, Capcom confirms that players will lose access to the game next year.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that four years after the game's launch, Capcom is officially shutting down Exoprimal, the company's 5v5 action game about a futuristic dinosaur crisis. Capcom announced Tuesday that service for Exoprimal will be discontinued in September 2027 — meaning that Exoprimal will no longer be playable — and that the game will no longer be sold starting in March 2027.

While disappointing for stalwart Exoprimal fans, the writing has been on the wall since 2024, when Capcom all but confirmed the sci-fi action game's grim fate.

It has been revealed that in an official notice posted to the Exoprimal website, Capcom confirms that players will lose access to the game next year. "We regret to announce that service for Exoprimal will be discontinued as of 8:00 PM (PDT) on Wednesday, September 29, 2027," the shutdown announcement reads. "We cannot thank you enough for the love and support you have shown over the years, and we sincerely apologize for the gravity of this announcement.".

Industry observers note that capcom has already pulled the game's four seasonal Survival Passes from stores, and warns that Exoprimal, its DLC, and all related products will no longer be sold on digital stores as of March 30, 2027. The game will shut down completely on Sept. 29, 2027, as Exoprimal is first and foremost a team-based competitive multiplayer game. Capcom notes that it will still be possible to download the game after Exoprimal is removed from stores.

Exoprimal was released in July 2023 on PlayStation 4, PlayStation 5, Windows PC, Xbox One, and Xbox Series X. The game is a multiplayer third-person shooter in which players control an Exofighter — an exosuit-clad soldier — who is tasked with completing objectives while also fighting hordes of dinosaurs in an attempt to defeat the evil artificial intelligence Leviathan. Players are grouped into two teams of five and compete against each other while battling ancient life and futuristic AI.

Capcom announced in July 2024 that, after four seasons of content, Exoprimal players would subsist on recycled, rotating seasons — all but confirming that the publisher was ready to put the newly introduced IP behind it.

In a recent development, exoprimal was released to mixed reviews in 2023. In Polygon's review of the game, which drew comparisons to Overwatch, Dino Crisis, and the Earth Defense Force games, we criticized the game's opening hours, which make "a terrible first impression." But, as reviewer Jordan Oloman wrote, Exoprimal has some surprises in store several hours into the experience.

"This paradigm shift changes Exoprimal considerably, introducing newly introduced maps, a healthy difficulty spike, raid bosses, and, at long last, some genuine narrative intrigue," Oloman wrote. "It is a profoundly confusing pacing decision where you’re abruptly playing a very different, arguably much better game several hours in, one that actually sets a fascinating precedent for future multiplayer storytelling shenanigans. 'Wifi Motion Sensing' Can Track Everything You Do Through Your Router

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (824 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, A simple wifi feature could let ISPs track your location and movement patterns within your home.
  • While the technology isn’t universally implemented just yet and is typically opt-in only (smart home customers might want the movement tracking feature for lights and heating), it presents quite a few privacy risks.
  • Wifi routers rely on radio signals to connect wirelessly to your devices and appliances.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, A simple wifi feature could let ISPs track your location and movement patterns within your home. "Wifi motion sensing" turns your ISP’s router into a motion detector, letting providers know exactly how many people are in the house, where they are situated, individual movement patterns, and, in some cases, even body shapes that could approximate a person’s identity.

While the technology isn’t universally implemented just yet and is typically opt-in only (smart home customers might want the movement tracking feature for lights and heating), it presents quite a few privacy risks. So here’s how wifi routers sense motion, what they can do with it, who has access to the data, and how you can disable it.

Wifi routers rely on radio signals to connect wirelessly to your devices and appliances. Those same radio signals are also absorbed and reflected by the human body as they travel in all directions from the router. With the right software, ISPs can track how those wifi signals travel around your room, which can be studied to detect presence and sense motion patterns.

Sources indicate that as long as your ISP’s router model supports this feature natively, it doesn’t require any additional hardware to be installed in your home. For example, Xfinity’s version of the feature pairs your router with five other connected appliances in your room to create oval-shaped sensing zones that can track your presence and movement within those spaces.

According to recent reports, it isn’t a new feature, either—companies like Cognitive Systems and Origin Wireless that supply networking hardware to ISPs have been offering wifi motion sensing for years now, while early research prototypes from the MIT date back at least as far as 2015. In 2025, IEEE updated its Wi-Fi 802.11 standard to include motion sensing and lay out the architectural guidelines for it, which makes it likely that even more routers will now ship with the feature.

It has been revealed that in its current consumer form, wifi motion sensing can help you control smart home apparatus like lights or thermostats, get pet safety notifications on your phone, set up a fall alert system for elderly consumers, and trigger appliances remotely based on human presence. But enabling it carries risks.

Most providers, including Cognitive Systems, claim that the technology isn’t sensitive to identity and can’t be used to track specific individuals. But even if true, that’s more likely to be a product decision rather than a technical limitation. Karlsruhe Institute researchers have shown that even ordinary wifi signals can identify individuals with a 99.5% accuracy.

Also worth noting: ISPs’ legal wording suggests that they may disclose the collected and stored motion data at any time to law enforcement, government agencies, regulators, and courts in response to subpoenas or during an emergency. ISPs may also retain your motion data in the cloud long-term in case they are required to facilitate a subpoena in the future.

As far as major ISPs are concerned, Xfinity (Comcast) is the only broadband provider that currently offers this feature across its commercial routers on the XB7, XB8, XB9, XB10, MXB1, and XER10 gateways. It’s opted out by default, but in case you or a family member already switched it on, you can disable it again by navigating to Home > WiFi Motion on the Xfinity app, click on the gear icon on the live view page, and tap Remove WiFi Motion.

Industry observers note that verizon Fios customers also had access to a Home Awareness feature on their routers that could be toggled on or off using the MyFios app, but that’s since been discontinued. In an official disclosure published shortly after the discontinuation, Verizon notified customers that it has deleted all associated movement logs from this service and no longer retains any motion data from owners.

But there are other regional ISPs that offer it, too. For example, Breezeline (Atlantic Broadband) offers a feature called Motion within its Plume-powered application that alerts customers when movement is detected in their homes, among its other features. MidCo, a telecom organization in the Upper Midwest, has a feature called Sense which can be toggled on or off using the MidCo Wi-Fi app. Plume, ADT-owned Origin Wireless, and Airties—all of whom supply technology to ISPs—have also been marketing motion sensing to customers for the last few years.

Sources indicate that if you’re unsure if your wifi router or ISP has motion sensing features or opts you in by default, look for a feature called “Sense,” “Motion,” or equivalent in your broadband’s mobile app. Exact steps differ greatly from one ISP to another, so it’s best not to assume that they will all opt you out by default, or that they collect the same types of data. With the 802.11bf revision to IEEE standards in 2025, this technology will be accessible to even more router manufacturers, so expect adoption to grow among internet providers as well.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • HomeKit Weekly is a series focused on smart home accessories, automation tips and tricks, and everything to do with Apple’s smart home framework.
  • A standard motion sensor uses PIR, which only detects movement, and that works fine in many situations.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that motion-based automations are generally straightforward in Apple Home. The only carve-out is lighting, because some rooms are hard to judge by time of day alone. Depending on the windows and placement against the sun, some rooms might need light-based automations earlier in the day than others. The Lafaer 5-in-1 presence sensor fixes that with a light sensor most motion sensors lack, along with mmWave radar.

HomeKit Weekly is a series focused on smart home accessories, automation tips and tricks, and everything to do with Apple’s smart home framework.

A standard motion sensor uses PIR, which only detects movement, and that works fine in many situations. If you’re still for long periods, you’re invisible, and the automation assumes the room is empty. The Lafaer LWR02 pairs PIR with 2.4 GHz mmWave radar. The PIR-based motion sees you walking in, and the radar sees the minor stuff, like breathing and shifting on the couch, so the room stays “occupied” for as long as you are in it. The two together also reduce false positives from ceiling fans, curtains, and the dog, because the radar and PIR both must agree before the sensor reports motion.

In Apple Home, that shows up as an occupancy sensor and a motion sensor from the same device.

Recent findings suggest that “Turn on the lights when someone enters” is a common automation I use, but it can be tricky. What if you only want it when it’s not light outside? Doing it based on time of day sometimes works, but what about depending on where the windows are facing, etc.? You might have a room that gets darker an hour earlier than another room. “Turn on the lights when someone enters, and it’s dark in the room” is what the light sensor can handle for you.

In the Home app, that means triggering a sensor for occupancy, then converting the automation into a Shortcut and adding a condition for the light level. It’s a few extra steps, but it does really give you more fine control over how it works.

Presence, motion, light, temperature, and humidity all come from the same device, and each one appears in Apple Home as its own sensor, so you can build automations around whichever ones fit the room.

It’s IPX3-rated, so bathrooms, kitchens, and laundry rooms are fine to use in. Coverage is about 13 feet for presence and 26 for motion across about 120 degrees, which works in a bedroom, office, or bathroom. It’s not going to cover a great room from one corner. The base is a magnetic half sphere, so you can aim it, and it mounts with adhesive or sits on a shelf. I generally like to use the shelf for these types of sensors.

Sources indicate that the Lafaer LWR02 is Matter over Thread, so it pairs directly with a HomePod, HomePod mini, or Apple TV 4K with no Lafaer hub or account needed. It runs on two included AAA batteries, is rated for up to two years, and rechargeable AAAs work with it as well. Thread is why a sensor doing this much can last that long on batteries. All sensor data is processed locally, so it only uses a trickle on the batteries.

Recent findings suggest that lights that turn off while you’re sitting still in the room are the reason a lot of people stop using motion automations in smart homes. The Lafaer LWR02 fixes that with mmWave radar and then lets you have more granular control of light-based automations based on what’s actually in the environment in the room, not just the time of day.

The Lafaer 5-in-1 presence sensor is available on Amazon.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Adrenaline acts as an emergency boost to all your stats in Grand Theft Auto 6, as it temporarily negates health, stamina, and focus loss. It's meant to get you out of an emergency situation safely or help you burst into a tense situation and mop it up fast. Unlike Zombix and other restoratives, though, you can't buy adrenaline — not from anywhere we've found so far, at least — nor can you expect to find it in abundance throughout Leonida. There is, however, a small set of locations you can reliably get adrenaline from.

Below, we explain how to get adrenaline in GTA 6.

You'll normally find at least one shot of adrenaline where you need it most — illegal operations, which have yellow marked on the map. That's true for the big ones, like the bowling alley the Kolt group operates out of, and the small ones, like the meth labs and grow houses operating out the back of gas stations. Basically, any convenience stores, gas stations, bars, and so on that lets you explore more than just the customer area nearly always has a trauma kit or first-aid kid in a staff area, bathroom, or kitchen. These will always have Zombix, but there's also a chance that they'll contain one shot of adrenaline. The kits might be lying around on a countertop, or they may be little cabinets nailed to the wall. If they're on the wall, you'll have to break them open, which takes a few seconds. Bear that in mind if you've got enemies close behind.

It has been revealed that this is not to be confused with the other robbery opportunities that have green markers or stick ups that have gray markers. These areas can have adrenaline, but they're a bit rarer.

Sources indicate that there's also a chance to find adrenaline in the back of ambulances, either loose or in a trauma kit. Getting it this way is pretty tough until you reach Chapter 3 and can explore Vice City more freely, though. The city hospital always has a few ambulances around back in the parking lot. They aren't very well attended, so you can break in with comparative ease. They are alarmed, so make sure to slim jim the door first, and then open the back to avoid setting off the alarm.

Recent findings suggest that you might see ambulances driving along the roads of Leonida or the streets of Vice City. If you're really desperate for adrenaline, you can stop them and break into the back. This is a pretty substantial and unnecessary risk to take if you're trying to keep a low profile, though.

Lucia and Jason can only hold three adrenaline apiece, so you can't stock up on them and let loose in a particularly tough mission. If you want to have it on-hand before taking on a dangerous job, instead of scrambling to find the location's bathroom when the bullets start flying, your best bet is to swipe it from an ambulance before setting out to work.

Industry observers note that just make sure to keep an eye on the stat bars in the upper left corner of the screen. They turn yellow when you use adrenaline, and the yellow gradually fades back to the stats' normal colors as it wears off. Consider it your action timer. By the time it's almost completely run out, you should be finding cover or fleeing for safety.
