  • There’s a hidden feature in the Find Hub app that helps you keep track of things without actually using a Bluetooth tracker.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, google's Find Hub app isn't just for tracking your lost smartphone. Over the past year, Google has consistently added features to manage your belongings, share your location with loved ones, and locate lost devices. Find Hub can now notify you when you've left your device or your tracker behind. Plus, you can use Gemini to remember where you left items, even without a tracker attached. Behind the scenes, there are even more hidden settings and features to help track your devices and make it easier to retrieve them in case they are stolen or misplaced. If you use Find Hub, you need to know about these 10 hacks.

According to recent reports, this month, Google finally added Left Behind notifications to Android trackers—but you have to enable the feature manually. AirTags customers should be familiar with this feature already. When you leave your tracker or device behind, and exit the location range, you’ll receive a notification that you left without your item. You need to enable this feature on a per-device basis. Go to Find Hub and select a device. Tap the settings gear icon next to the device's name, and enable Notify when left behind. While you’re here, go to Add location to add familiar locations where you don’t want to get a notification (like your home or workspace). Otherwise, Find Hub may spam you with left behind alerts.

There’s a hidden feature in the Find Hub app that helps you keep track of things without actually using a Bluetooth tracker. You can simply ask Gemini to remember where you put things, and it will show up in the Find Hub app. To use it, pull up Gemini and say something like, “Remember in Find Hub that the passport is in the downstairs wardrobe,” or “I’ve kept the spare car keys behind the garage door.”.

You can then ask Gemini, “Where did I keep my passport?” and it will tell you. If you change the location of an item, just ask Gemini to update it for you. When you go to the Remembered tab, you’ll see the location of all remembered items. You can also add items manually here using the Add button.

Industry observers note that some Android smartphones can remain findable for several hours after they've been switched off or their batteries have run out. If you’re using a supported device (like the latest Pixel series smartphone), you can use a hardware feature to track the location using Google’s mesh network, relying on nearby devices (similar to how Android tags work).

According to recent reports, to make sure this feature is enabled, go to Find Hub, and tap Find your offline devices. Here, make sure that either With network in busy places only or With network everywhere is selected.

If you’re using a tracker in your car, luggage, or on your keys, you might want to share location access with your spouse or family members. Find Hub has a feature called "Share Ownership" that lets you share the tracker details with up to 10 people. Only the location of your tracker is shared, not your personal device.

Recent findings suggest that to set it up, go to Find Hub, and choose the tracker or accessory that you want to share. Tap the Share Ownership button and follow the on-screen instructions to share the invite link via a messaging app or using Quick Share. Once the recipient taps Accept, you’ll get a notification. Go to the device settings in Find Hub and tap the Confirm button to enable location sharing.

In a recent development, you can swiftly share your live location with your friends or loved ones using Google Messages. Open a conversation, tap the Attachment icon, and choose Real-time location. Set the duration and tap Send.

In a recent development, if you don’t like using the Messages app, you can do so directly from Find Hub. Go to the People tab at the bottom of the screen, and tap the Plus icon. Choose the duration and select a contact to share the location with, then tap the Get Link button to copy the link. You can then share it via any messaging app of your choice.

According to recent reports, you might have a Find Hub tracker in your luggage to help keep tabs on your bags. But you don't have to be the only one privy to its location. If your airline loses that luggage, you can temporarily share its location with your airline to help you retrieve it. This is an official feature, too: Google partnered with multiple airlines to make this data sharing easier. From the Find Hub, choose your tracker. Tap the Share Item Location button, and then tap Share Item Location again. Copy the generated web link and share it with your airline using the app or support page. The link will automatically expire in seven days, so you don't have to worry about your airline continuing to monitor your luggage's location long after your flight.

According to recent reports, find Hub uses a mesh network of supported Android devices to securely locate your lost device or tag. But by default, it waits until multiple Android devices detect the location of the lost device. This works well if you've lost the device in crowded areas, but it can increase your wait time if you lose it somewhere remote. Luckily, there is a hidden setting that triggers location sharing even if a single device reports its location. Go to Settings > Google > All services > Find Hub > Find your offline devices and select With network everywhere instead of With network in busy places only.

It has been revealed that if you’ve lost your smartphone, you don’t need to rush to a computer or a website to track it. Borrow someone’s Android smartphone and head into their Find Hub. Tap Sign in as guest and sign in with your Google account associated with your device, then find and select your device in the account. If requested, enter the PIN that you’ve previously set up. You can now track the device’s location, get directions to the device, or play a sound to help track the device if it’s nearby. If the device is truly lost, you can use the Mark as Lost feature to remotely lock your device.

Map-based tracking is helpful in getting to the general vicinity of your lost device. But your smartphone or tracker is hidden; finding it may require precision tracking. Many newer trackers like the Pixel Tag come with an ultra-wideband chip that helps you find the exact location of the tracker, given you are nearby. This also works on Pixel smartphones (Pixel 8 Pro series and above) and Samsung Galaxy devices (S21 and above, Plus and Ultra models only).

Recent findings suggest that when using this feature, make sure you have Bluetooth enabled on your smartphone, then open Find Hub. Choose your tracker, and tap Find Nearby. Follow the on-screen instructions to locate the nearby device. You can also tap Play Sound to make the location process easier.

If you think your Android smartphone is lost or stolen, don’t rush to erase all data. While a remote factory reset is great for protecting your data, it also removes the device from your account. It’s best to try to get the device back. Two-factor authentication (or a passkey) on your Google account, along with a biometric lock on your smartphone, will protect the data itself.

Go to the Find Hub website, or use Find Hub on someone else’s phone in guest mode. Choose your device, and instead of Factory Reset, choose Mark as Lost. Here, you’ll see an option to enter a message. Type an alternative contact number, and a message to help recover the device.

Prime Video's TV show catalog features quite a few notable sci-fi series. The genre is well represented through comedies like Upload, the intense The Expanse, and other exciting genre indicates.

Sources indicate that for instance, Prime Video just released one of the most ambitious sci-fi TV shows in the age of streaming. After all, the streamer has tapped into one of the most iconic franchises of all time, Ridley Scott's Blade Runner, for the sequel series Blade Runner 2099, which is set 50 years after the last film in the cyberpunk franchise, Ryan Gosling's Blade Runner 2049.

Speaking of cyberpunk TV shows, William Gibson is often referred to as the creator of that notable sci-fi subgenre. After all, his hit book, Neuromancer, is highly regarded as foundational to all cyberpunk stories that have come after it. Gibson fans can look forward to that franchise being adapted into a live-action series on Apple TV, as Neuromancer, starring former James Bond candidate Callum Turner, debuts on January 22, 2027.

Industry observers note that those looking for a genre show to watch while waiting for Apple TV's Neuromancer next year can find not only what stands as one of the most intricate sci-fi TV shows in recent years, but another project based on Gibson's work. The TV show in question is The Peripheral, and I still can't believe it was robbed of the chance of becoming a 10/10 show.

Industry observers note that the Peripheral debuted on Prime Video on October 21, 2022, with eight episodes being released on the streaming service until the finale on December 2, 2022. The cyberpunk series went through one of the most disappointing arcs in the streaming age, as The Peripheral holds a strong 79% critics' score on Rotten Tomatoes and an even better 85% audience score, with the show having originally been renewed for season 2 only a couple of months after its season 1 finale. By all accounts, it laid a solid foundation for what could be years of complex sci-fi storytelling.

Recent findings suggest that however, due to the effects of the 2023 SAG-AFTRA and Writers Guild of America strikes, Prime Video walked back on the renewal, canceling The Peripheral in August 2023. To say that was disappointing is not enough. Gibson is known for being one of the most skilled authors in the sci-fi genre, and The Peripheral showed a lot of promise in its first eight episodes. The series had to deal with complicated elements, as its story consists of two interconnected timelines separated by 70 years, headsets that can send people's consciousness across timelines, and a fast approaching apocalypse known as the Jackpot.

There was a lot of worldbuilding to unpack in The Peripheral season 1, but the show did a mostly fantastic job at making all these complex ideas feel interesting and urgent. With impressive VFX, kinetic action sequences, sharp writing, magnetic performances, and plenty of mysteries left to unfold, The Peripheral's eight episodes looked like a clear case of a TV show that was preparing itself to get even bigger and better in its next season. This is why the show's cancellation still stings three years later, as the lasting feeling is that it was robbed of becoming a true sci-fi masterpiece.

Industry observers note that making matters worse is the fact that The Peripheral was packed full of talent both in front and behind the camera. Chloë Grace Moretz as Flynne Fisher and Jack Reynor as her brother, Burton, commanded the screen and were easy to connect with. T'Nia Miller's Cherise Nuland was an intense and cunning villain, and her recent showstopping performance as Jocasta in Marvel's sci-fi series VisionQuest was a reminder of what we lost. Then there is the fact that Jonathan Nolan and Lisa Joy, who were behind HBO's Westworld and Prime Video's own Fallout, were executive producers. The Peripheral simply deserved better.

“We are very happy to be back on the road with IFC. In a recent development, “The Trip” franchise began all the way back in 2011, and since then the films have spanned trips in England, Italy, Spain, and Greece. As has been the case with all of the installments, they’ve been miniseries airing on TV in England but then edited into films for the U.S. release. The first movie made $3.9 million worldwide across several re-releases, “The Trip to Italy” in 2014 made $6.1 million, 2017’s “The Trip to Spain” made $1.9 million, and “The Trip to Greece” in the COVID-addled summer 2020 still managed to make $259K worldwide.

All four of the “Trip” movies are currently available for streaming on Sun Now, which is the streamer owned by Independent Film Company parent AMC Global Media.

In a recent development, “The Independent Film Manufacturer is thrilled to continue our longstanding relationship with this world-class group of filmmakers on the latest installment of this beloved franchise. Few comedic partnerships have the enduring appeal of Steve Coogan and Rob Brydon, and under Michael Winterbottom’s inspired direction, each newly introduced trip remains the comedic gift that keeps on giving. This time around, we can’t wait for audiences to join us on the road to the Northern Lights,” said Ayo Kepher-Maat, Independent Film Company’s Vice President of Acquisitions and Production.

Industry observers note that “Michael Winterbottom, Steve Coogan, and Rob Brydon have created a franchise filled with taste, wit and belly laughs. Independent Film Firm has brought each one to audiences with characteristic care and capability. ‘The Trip to the Northern Lights’ advances the history with the delight of something completely fresh and tasty,” said Josh Sapan of Sapan Studio.

The film is produced by Melissa Parmenter and Josh Hyams for Revolution Films. The deal was negotiated by Ayo Kepher-Maat on behalf of Independent Film Organization and Tristan Whalley MD of Goalpost Films on behalf of the filmmakers.

Industry observers note that executive producers are Winterbottom, Coogan, Brydon, Alex Moody, Josh Sapan, Tristan Whalley, Paul Wiegard. “The Trip to the Northern Lights” is a Revolution Films, Baby Cow, and Small Man Production in association with Sky Studios.

AirPods 5 were introduced in September and come in two different versions. Unlike their predecessors, both versions of AirPods 5 offer Active Noise Cancellation. They differ in the charging case, battery life, and volume control. The base model AirPods 5 ($129) come with a case that can only charge via USB-C.

The case for the higher-end AirPods 5 ($149) supports wireless charging and Find My. You also get one extra hour of battery life. The higher-end model also adds on-stem volume control, so you can adjust the volume just by swiping up or down on one of the earbud stems.

Here’s a full comparison between both AirPods 5 models:.

Recent findings suggest that the key thing about AirPods 5 is their open-ear design, unlike the in-ear design of the AirPods Pro 3 (more on those later). Even with that open-ear design, AirPods 5 offer incredible Active Noise Cancellation capabilities.

Recent findings suggest that if you are shopping for AirPods 5, I do recommend spending the extra $20 to get the higher-end model. The better charging case alone is worth the extra money. With Find My integration and a built-in speaker, you can track your AirPods and play a sound from the case if you lose them.

If the person you’re shopping for doesn’t like in-ear earbuds, AirPods 5 are an excellent choice.

For most people, though, AirPods Pro 3 are probably the better choice ….

Recent findings suggest that airPods Pro 3 are Apple’s most capable earbuds, even with the introduction of AirPods 5 this year. They offer an in-ear fit and come with five foam-infused silicone ear tip sizes. With that in-ear design, AirPods Pro 3 can offer up to 3x stronger noise cancellation than AirPods 5. In my testing, this difference is notable.

AirPods Pro 3 also offer several other features you won’t find on AirPods 5, including a heart rate sensor for workouts, plus Hearing Test, Hearing Aid, and Hearing Protection features.

Sources indicate that I still think AirPods Pro 3 are one of the best products in Apple’s lineup today. I wear mine for multiple hours every single day and can’t imagine life without them. I love the in-ear fit, and the ANC still impresses me, whether I’m at home or somewhere like a coffee shop.

It has been revealed that if you know the person you’re shopping for (whether it’s yourself or someone else) likes the in-ear earbud design, I think AirPods Pro 3 are the best option. This is especially true when AirPods Pro 3 are on sale, like they are right now at $149. The price difference between AirPods 5 and AirPods Pro 3 is very small, and you’re getting a much better product.

Finally, we have AirPods Max. These are Apple’s only option for people who want AirPods in an over-ear headphone form factor. Last year, they were pretty hard to recommend since they’d gone five years without a real upgrade.

Recent findings suggest that this year, however, Apple officially introduced AirPods Max 2, bringing modern features to Apple’s high-end headphones. This includes features like Adaptive Audio, Conversation Awareness, Personalized Volume, and more.

Sources indicate that airPods Max 2 are a far more compelling option than AirPods Max were at this time last year. They’re still pricey, but I love the aesthetics and find them very comfortable. There’s something about the premium aluminum design with an elegant Digital Crown that really stands out.

In a recent development, if you’re looking to splurge this holiday season, AirPods Max 2 are a great choice. For more realistic budgets, I think AirPods Pro 3 are the best option.

It has been revealed that right now, the Xteink X4 Pro, the best tiny e-reader I've tried so far—and Lifehacker's pick for the 2026 E-Reader Gift of the Year—is on its best sale yet for Black Friday: When ordered directly from Xteink, you'll save 15% off the usual $99 price, bringing it down to $84. The X4 Pro is the newest and best e-reader from Xteink, the Chinese tech startup that turned the e-reading world upside down last year with the launch of the original X4 pocket e-reader. While the X4 Pro is the same size as the basic X4 Classic, it adds two big upgrades—a temperature-adjustable front light and a touchscreen—plus a faster processor and more memory. As a result, it costs a bit more, but you can pick one at a $15 discount right now. (Even at full retail, the X4 Pro is $50 cheaper than the entry-level Kindle after its recent price increase—and even considering the Kindle's current Black Friday discount).

Meanwhile, if you're a reader who prioritizes the crispest text over conveniences like a front light, the 4.3-inch Xteink X4 Classic and the smaller 3.7-inch Xteink X3 are about $30 less during Amazon's own Black Friday sale.

As much as I love them, these minuscule e-readers aren't for everyone. Some may indeed find the screen too small (though if you've ever read a book on a phone, the experience is similar). Then there's the fact that they can't load your existing libraries of Kindle books; you'll need to source copies of e-books lacking Digital Rights Management (DRM) software. But if you can jump those hurdles, you might just discover it's the weirdest, most lovable piece of tech you've used in years.

Based on the bestselling 2017 novel of the same name by bestselling author Karin Slaughter, The Good Daughter follows two estranged sisters named Charlotte “Charlie” Quinn (Fahy) and Samantha “Sam” Quinn (Byrne). Set in a small Georgia town named Pikeville, the series follows Charlie and Sam twenty years after a brutal home invasion changed their lives and fractured their family forever. The incident resulted in their mother's murder, devastated their defense attorney father, Rusty (Brendan Gleeson), and led to a series of unspoken secrets between them.

Industry observers note that two decades after the invasion, another act of violence suddenly hits Pikeville, and Charlie, now a lawyer like her father, is the first witness on the scene. In Episode 1 of the series, the event drags both sisters back together and resurfaces the horrifying truths of the night that once tore their family apart. "As the case unfolds and twists through painful memories and buried secrets, what emerges is not just a story of survival, but of enduring ties between a father and his daughters, and the complex bond between sisters," the official synopsis reads. The sisters still live with the effects of a traumatic event that happened two decades prior, and when another violent attack takes place in their hometown, their demons come flooding back.

Since its release, The Good Daughter has received a mixed bag of reviews from critics. On Rotten Tomatoes, the series earned 79% from critics, and a higher 87% from the audience. From some of the reviews, it's clear that while the series has an impressive cast led by Byrne, Fahy and Gleeson, the performances aren't alone in making it gripping and engaging. "This dizzying thriller coasts on vibes alone, and, assisted by its powerhouse stars, that is just about enough," wrote one review. "It deals with some heavy themes, but always in a pulpy, airport-novel kind of way, making it an easy binge despite the dark subject matter," wrote another review.

For Collider's Jessica Toomer, the series earned an impressive 9/10, with her review saying the series "might just be the best thing Peacock has put out in years." Among the highlights, of course, is the stacked cast, as well as the way it integrates two timeframes parallel to each other. "Fahy is doing some of her best work as Charlie, Byrne gives her someone worth fighting with, and the show takes the sisters as seriously as it takes the murder mystery," Toomer wrote. "The childhood timeline isn’t filler, either; it just keeps shifting what the present-day story means. Add Gleeson, who is a pleasure in every scene, and a version of small-town Georgia that’s green and sunlit instead of grim, and you’ve got an addictive binge.".

According to recent reports, ultimately, while the show's reception has been varied, the cast alone makes The Good Daughter a must-watch. With Fahy, Byrne and Gleeson playing a fractured and divided family, the series sets up these actors to show off their vulnerabilities, mend broken relationships, and heal from two traumatizing events. It's a gripping series, with stellar performances and storylines that will keep viewers engaged until the very end.

Sisters Charlie and Sam Quinn have spent two decades living with the aftermath of a violent home invasion that killed their mother. Years later, Charlie witnesses a deadly school shooting in their Georgia hometown, with Sam reluctantly returning to help her investigate the attack.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that ridley Scott is one of those staple filmmakers.
  • One of his most famous films, however, is also one of his sparsest.
  • Set in an unspecified future, Alien follows the Nostromo, a towing ship hauling resources back to Earth.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that ridley Scott is one of those staple filmmakers. The 88-year-old English director has made countless noteworthy films, TV demonstrates, and commercials over the course of his prolific career, dabbling in so many genres that it’s difficult to narrow down the parameters of his work. With the release of this year’s The Dog Stars, Scott has directed 31 feature films. They don’t all share the same characteristics, but broadly, his films are known for huge and immersive sets, battles on an epic scale, and significant and heady concepts.

One of his most famous films, however, is also one of his sparsest. After making his feature debut with the small but well-received The Duelists, Scott delivered his follow-up: Alien, one of the great sci-fi horror films of all time. The 1979 classic gave the space-horror subgenre the Scott treatment, resulting in a modest-budget film that looks gorgeous and frightening, balancing evocative monsters and sets with a quiet restraint no entries in the franchise have matched since. With Alien Netflix on Dec. 1, there's never been a better time to rewatch it.

Set in an unspecified future, Alien follows the Nostromo, a towing ship hauling resources back to Earth. The ship’s crew is made up of workers struggling to make ends meet, hoping to wrap up the job and return home to cash in their paychecks. They awaken from hypersleep after the ship’s computer, Mother, receives a signal from a nearby moon, tasking them with exploring it. Three members of the crew set out to investigate, arriving in an environment that’s hostile from the get-go and quickly get caught in a storm that damages the ship.

The explorers find an alien ship on the moon, filled with strange sights, among them a giant fossilized alien and a nest of large eggs. While walking among them, one of the eggs bursts, with a creature latching onto Kane (John Hurt), the ship’s second-in-command. He’s hauled back to the ship, foreign attachment and all, with the crew deliberating over what to do before ultimately bringing a predatory alien creature on board. The rest is history. Before too long, the remaining survivors are being tormented by the Xenomorph, one of the greatest cinematic creations in movie history.

Recent findings suggest that alien highlights the creature, designed by the Swiss artist H.R. Giger, in its various stages. We first see it as an egg, then a facehugger, a chestburster, and finally as an adult. Despite the painstaking design, Scott treated his monster like the shark in Jaws, knowing that the less the creature is seen and the more it stalks its prey, the scarier it becomes. Throughout Alien, the Xenomorph is filmed in snippets, showing its tail, its dripping jaw, and its terrifying human-like teeth. The monster’s success has inspired four direct sequels, two prequels, two crossovers, and a really good TV show.

But before finding all of this success, Alien was simply a very efficient movie, keeping the audience engaged with its patient approach to storytelling and the slow unveiling of the horror at its core. While it’s a story about an unbeatable monster stalking a terrified group of people, Scott and screenwriter Dan O’Bannon establish the world through details. The crew of the Nostromo is not on a mission to meet new species and explore planets; it’s not a crew full of optimistic heroes out to save the world. We never see Earth or any sort of civilization, but two of the crew’s engineers spend much of their story discussing each other’s bonuses.

Sources indicate that the film also takes its time in revealing who the lead character is. Two of the crew’s central figures are Dallas (Tom Skerritt), the ship’s captain, and Kane, an executive officer on the ship, introduced as one of the film’s protagonists. Kane is also the first to die. By the time Ripley (Sigourney Weaver) comes into the picture, she’s simply one of the survivors, and in command because there’s no one else to take the job. Her first major scene shows her following the rules, refusing to let Kane back on the ship since he’s a hazard to the rest of the crew. (She loses that debate.) Ripley doesn’t see herself as a hero; just a worker, sticking to protocol.

In a recent development, “I feel that one of the reasons Ripley endures as someone who even can inspire me if I need a little encouragement is that she is an ‘everyperson.’ She’s a human character,” Weaver told Empire last year. Ripley barely survives the Xenomorph, yet she establishes herself as a key figure in the Alien universe, as significant to the franchise as the monster itself.

According to recent reports, everyone has a favorite Alien movie, whether it's James Cameron’s bombastic action extravaganza Aliens, David Fincher’s contemplative and maligned Aliens 3, or even Ridley Scott's divisive prequel Prometheus. Still, there’s something about the claustrophobic horror of the original that no follow-up has ever managed to replicate. Scott’s restraint and attention to detail planted the seeds that the franchise is still reaping to this day.

Sources indicate that "I did the best one by far, full stop. End of fucking story,” Scott told Brut this year.

It has been revealed that alien is streaming on Netflix until Dec. 1.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • The opening hook can make or break a sci-fi series.
  • In a recent development, created by Dan Erickson, Apple TV's Severance, too, introduces a fascinating concept in its opening chapters.
  • It has been revealed that this early hook not only feels high-concept but also serves as the perfect allegory for exploitative corporate jobs in the real world.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The opening hook can make or break a sci-fi series. If a sci-fi show does not introduce a compelling concept in its opening episodes, it is almost destined to fail. However, a gripping opening hook is not enough to keep viewers invested in the long run. Even the most promising concepts can lose their appeal if they are not executed as brilliantly as the ones in an Apple TV sci-fi masterpiece.

In a recent development, created by Dan Erickson, Apple TV's Severance, too, introduces a fascinating concept in its opening chapters. Humanity invents a chip that, once installed in the brain, can split one's consciousness into two. A giant conglomerate, Lumon, uses this technology to create a workforce whose employees have no recollection of their lives outside the office.

It has been revealed that this early hook not only feels high-concept but also serves as the perfect allegory for exploitative corporate jobs in the real world. The Apple TV sci-fi show's appeal also lies in its liminal imagery that makes incredible use of space to instill unease in viewers. However, what begins as a retrofuturistic critique of corporate culture gradually turns into a masterful exploration of power and identity.

The consciousness of the severed Lumon employee is split into two different personalities in Severance. While the ones working inside Lumon are referred to as "Innies," the ones outside are called "Outies." The show clearly establishes that the Innies and Outies are separate people in themselves. No overlaps can exist between their memories unless someone finds loopholes.

To keep viewers immersed in both the Innie and Outie worlds, Severance gives immersive and relatable arcs to both counterparts of the same characters. Even the cinematography in both worlds has its own appeal. While the Innie world is cold, liminal, confined, and clinical, the outside world is intentionally covered in shades of grey and shot with handheld cameras.

In a recent development, from the very beginning, a clear point and process of transition is also established between the Innies and Outies in Severance. Using everything from sound cues to facial transitions, the Apple TV series keeps establishing how one character switches between their two alternate states. Once these rules are out of the way, the show gives personal stakes to every main character's Innie and Outie versions.

Severance's biggest strength is that its entire sci-fi lore is not confined to the main titular concept. As it progresses, it introduces more ingenious ways in which its characters can hack into their own brains and break the rules of the overarching technology through re-integration and "Overtime Contingency" protocols.

With these brilliantly set-up rules and concepts, Severance gradually paves the way for mind-bending payoffs that stay with you long after the credits stop rolling.

The core concept that drives Severance's drama is genius in itself. However, the show's true appeal lies in how it treats its characters. As a viewer, you initially find yourself rooting for the Innies because the show gradually develops them while revealing little about the Outies. However, just when a viewer starts seeing the Innies as heroes, the Outies' struggles and vulnerabilities are put on full display.

In a recent development, while ensuring that it keeps dropping newly introduced revelations about its central technology, Severance never rushes through its character beats. Owing to this, some of its biggest mind-bending end-season payoffs feel even more hard-hitting. In its 19-episode runtime, so far, Severance has had no dull moments or filler story arcs.

Every development in the Apple TV sci-fi series so far has added more heft to the overarching story. Its drama is further elevated by its award-winning performances, high production value, and Ben Stiller's direction. Hopefully, Severance will maintain the same momentum in season 3 as well.

A psychological thriller series featuring Adam Scott as Mark Scout, an employee at Lumon Industries who undergoes a "severance" procedure to separate work from his personal memories. However, as his work and life personas mysteriously begin to collide, it promptly becomes clear that not all is as it seems.

It has been revealed that it should come as little surprise that David Fincher’s “The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth” focuses on, well, Cliff Booth. The Quentin Tarantino-penned sequel to the filmmaker’s own 2019 Oscar-winning hit “Once Upon a Time in Hollywood” has always been billed as a spinoff following the continuing adventures of his fictitious (yet still iconic) stuntman Cliff Booth (Brad Pitt). But Tarantino has always loved building out his own shared and connected universe(s), and fans sure love exploring its outer limits.

“Once Upon a Time in Hollywood” and, by extension, “The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth” occupy a unique place in Tarantino’s cinematic world, as they’re both part of his so-called “Realer Than Real World Universe” and his “Movie Movie Universe.” Tarantino didn’t just keep crafting his movies-within-movies world with the hit film — he also introduced real-world (realer than real world?) elements and people (the Manson Family, of course, and all that entails). Related Stories ‘Bad Lieutenant: Tokyo’ Will Come to the U.S. Next March ‘The Trip’ Returns for Fifth Installment, Next Sending Steve Coogan and Rob Brydon to Frigid Arctic Circle.

In a recent development, that bent continues in “Cliff Booth,” which is rife with both out-there elements and very real references (time for that “Hee Haw” resurgence, we guess). But the film also has to follow its own series logic, which means, yes, it’s the Cliff Booth show, but hey, where are our “Hollywood” co-stars Rick Dalton (Leonardo DiCaprio) and Sharon Tate (Margot Robbie)?

[Once again: This article contains small spoilers for “The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth.”].

When we first meet Cliff and Rick, the duo are long-time colleagues and best pals. As his stunt double, Cliff is tasked with doing some serious heavy lifting for Hollywood star Rick, which inevitably (?) leads them to off four members of the Manson Family. The raucous and wild violence the duo inflicts on the foursome isn’t just a fun bonding exercise for the pair. It also ensures that the nefarious group can’t go next door to enact the infamous (and very real) Tate murders. Win-win!

The film ends with an invitation for Rick to slide on over to the Tate house for a thank-you drink, presumably putting him in the path of Roman Polanski, Sharon, and all the star power they carry. “Cliff Booth” is set eight years after those events, and while Rick may have enjoyed a career upswing in the interim, his current professional endeavors have taken him far from Hollywood.

In a recent development, while we never see Rick in the film (despite ongoing rumors that DiCaprio might appear for a quick cameo), Cliff mentions him frequently and fondly, including telling potential paramour Karen Crosby (Elizabeth Debicki) that their professional entanglements ended when Rick got, ahem, “too fat” for Cliff to believably double him and then moved to Australia to star in the TV series “Dingo Dan.” Further details on the show are slim, but we do know it’s a Western TV show that’s proven quite popular and durable (Aussie Karen seems to like it), and Cliff makes it sound like Rick is enjoying himself. Not too bad.

Sources indicate that by blending his two movie universes with “Once Upon a Time in Hollywood,” Tarantino got to both delight in late-’60s Hollywood magic and “save” Sharon Tate, her unborn son, Abigail Folger, Wojciech Frykowski, Steven Parent, and Jay Sebring. That sort of revisionist history was the film’s buzziest twist and, as I argued at the time, the most emotional choice Tarantino has ever made in his filmography.

Sources indicate that and while we don’t get treated to much more Sharon in “Cliff Booth,” we are granted some, in the form of a Red Apple Cigarettes commercial led by a beaming Margot Robbie, returning to her original role as the doomed actress. (The fake cigarettes are another Tarantino-verse staple, and Rick even appears in his own commercial for them during the end credits of “Hollywood.”).

Industry observers note that in the short cameo, Sharon looks healthy and happy, and she’s clearly still enough of a star to warrant her own advertising campaign, built on her smile and her zippy shimmy. As Cliff watches the commercial at the Marina del Rey condo he shares with his dad (Peter Weller), he takes the time to stop, observe, and notably smile at the star. It’s a small grace note, and a very effective one.

One other star of “Once Upon a Time in Hollywood” is missing from “Cliff Booth,” though. Just where the heck is Brandy?

Industry observers note that netflix will release “The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth” in IMAX theaters on Wednesday, November 25. It will be available to stream on Netflix starting Wednesday, December 23.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that there's no denying that Harry Potter continues to be a phenomenon. After seven bestsellers translated into multiple languages, years of extravagant midnight release parties, eight significant-budget films, a stage play, and theme parks, there's still enormous hype for both the upcoming HBO television show and an all-star re-recording of the audiobooks. Clearly, there is something about the boy who lived and his world that draws people in and keeps them captivated. All of this begs one very important question, however: how good are the Harry Potter books, really?

The answer to that question is, ultimately, a matter of personal taste, but the books do have their faults, from skimming mythology and using, at best, insensitive naming conventions to treating serious issues as fodder for gags and jokes. There's also the perennial question of whether the artist can be separated from their art. The good news is that there's a lot of fantasy in the world waiting to be read. Here are six fantasy books better than Harry Potter:.

Set in the same world as Percy Jackson and the Kane Chronicles (Magnus is Annabeth Chase's cousin), this book follows Magnus, an unhoused teen on the streets of Boston who discovers he's the son of Frey. After dying in battle, he becomes an einherjar and a resident of Hotel Valhalla. A Valkyrie named Samirah Al-Abbas convinces Magnus to help her stop Ragnarök.

According to recent reports, while a fantastic adventure full of Riordan's signature charm and wit, Magnus Chase also touches on the ways so many people, including children and teens, are othered because of their gender identity, disability, housing instability, poverty, or religion​​​​​​​. This book, however, never once uses any of these topics as the subject of a joke or a reason for the characters to be cruel to one another​​​​​​​. That's not to say everyone who populates the world is perfect; they have quirks and foibles and they make mistakes. There are, of course, true villains. But the lack of casual cruelty allows Riordan to bring together a found family built on choice, mutual respect, and determination—a believable family that allows each character to explore openly and honestly what's been difficult and traumatic for them.​​​​​​​ Riordan uses impeccable research with care to create a story that pays tribute to it.​​​​​​​.

The Sword of Summer is the first book in a trilogy.

According to recent reports, six of Crows is set in the same world as Bardugo's Shadow and Bone series. It follows a group of thieves hired to break into a heavily guarded prison to rescue​​​​​​​ a scientist experimenting with a drug that amplifies Grisha magic to potentially deadly levels​​​​​​​. The crew is, of course, a motley bunch, all of whom have dark pasts they promise won't cause complications. In the tradition of every great heist story, those pasts do, indeed, make everything a thousand times more difficult.

Industry observers note that these are also the stories that Bardugo does best: the smaller, more intimate ones. The stories with twists and turns and complications that leave characters trapped in the prisons of their own minds. The ones that mislead and distract until, suddenly, the scales fall away and the true double-cross is staring right at the intrepid almost-heroes, ready to crush them. No Harry Potter book ever made readers hold their breath the way the conclusion of Six of Crows will.​​​​​​​ It's probably a good idea to have Crooked Kingdom, the conclusion of the duology, standing by.​​​​​​​.

Blue, a girl from a family of psychics, has grown up being constantly reminded​​​​​​​ that she'll kill her true love with a kiss. That doesn't stop her, however, from befriending a group of boys from the local private school and joining them on their quest to seek out a legend: the Welsh king​​​​​​​ sleeping in the hills that surround them. Gansey, the group's leader, tells her that the first person to wake the king will get a wish.​​​​​​​ Blue accompanies the boys as they search, despite the danger and all the strange things​​​​​​​ that seem to happen when they go looking.

The Raven Boys is a marvel of atmosphere and mood. It gathers the reader in and holds them there, keeps them enmeshed in the world Stiefvater has created. Rather than bouncing around from setting to setting, it unfurls like the landscape it describes, presenting a magnificent vista that spreads wide before the reader and makes magic of what's right in front of them, accessible through their own senses​​​​​​​. It also makes magic a horror-tinged phenomenon, something to be wary of, something beautiful but dangerous. Something with a price.​.​ Like Magnus Chase, The Raven Boys blends fantasy and reality by also exploring income inequality and difficult home situations honestly but without ever shaming or humiliating the characters trapped in those experiences.​​​​​​​.

There are four books in The Raven Cycle, which is currently being adapted into a series of graphic novels​​​​​​​.​​​​​​​.

Christopher is not supposed to go near the water. Like many fantasy heroes, he disobeys​​​​​​​ and finds a drowning baby griffin. He saves it​​​​​​​ and is tasked with taking it back to the Archipelago, a hidden place where magical creatures are supposed to be safe. Once there, he meets Mal, a girl with a miraculous flying coat, and learns that magic is slowly dying, as are the inhabitants of the Archipelago​​​​​​​. Mal convinces Christopher to go with her on a quest to discover what's happening and to save their impossible friends.

Recent findings suggest that A middle-grade book, it will be a quick read​​​​​​​ for adults and a great book to read with kids of a certain age​​​​​​​. This is also a great book for kids because, while the adults keep secrets from Christopher, his grandfather breaks the cycle and becomes a trusted adult—something that doesn't happen in many fantasy novels.​​​​​​​​​​​​​​ Katherine Rundell is fantastic at setting scenes, and each one comes together beautifully​​​​​​​, painting the Archipelago in bright swaths of color and incredible detail. There is a cliffhanger at the end of book one that may be a little upsetting; the good news is that books two of this planned five-book series​​​​​​​ is already out.

In a recent development, bree Matthews hopes going to UNC early for a residential program will help her escape the grief of her mother's death. Her first night on campus, however, she stumbles into a demon attack and discovers a secret society whose members​​​​​​​ are descended from King Arthur's knights. When Sel, their mage, or Merlin, tries to wipe Bree's memory, he fails but unlocks abilities that suggest Bree too is a Legendborn.Initially turning down an invitation to join the group, Bree changes her mind when she discovers that a Merlin had something to do with her mother's death​​​​​​​. What she ultimately finds out is unimaginable.

Sources indicate that fantasy is rife with Arthurian retellings, but Legendborn is something special. The modern college setting gives the story room to breathe and allows Deonn to make some fascinating innovations with the material.​​​​​​​ The story's exploration of different magic systems keeps Bree grounded in the world​​​​​​​ even as she's discovering her powers, which is essential for her growth both as a person and within the Arthurian framework. Each of the characters in Legendborn has a role that's been assigned to them, but they also have their own desires​​​​​​​, and the conflicts and real-life stakes this interplay creates make the story that much more interesting.​​​​​​​ The exploration of grief is also important; it holds the narrative together and carries it forward, much as real grief shapes a life, especially after the loss of a parent.​​​​​​​ It influences everything that Bree does and every choice that she makes. It takes skill to pair fiction and reality so deftly.​​​​​​​.

Industry observers note that the second and third books of the series, Bloodmarked and Oathbound, are out. An as-yet-untitled fourth volume​​​​​​​ is planned.

Rui is an exorcist determined to avenge her mother's death. But one day, in the middle of a battle, her powers disappear. They reappear in Yiran, a boy from a wealthy family who would have had a perfect life if he had been born with abilities; now, suddenly, he does and as far as he's concerned, his new magic will fix everything. Nikai is a reaper whose boss, the Fourth King of Hell, has disappeared.​​​​​​​ Without the ten kings tending to their respective realms​​​​​​​, the underworld starts to crumble, and the human realm won't last much longer. So when Rui thinks she's discovered a lead on the missing fourth king and a way to get her powers back, she makes a dangerous deal.

Industry observers note that darker by Four builds on mythology instead of sprinkling it in where it's convenient or where it sounds good. The story reflects a deep understanding of the source material, which is truly integrated into the narrative; the legends here are load-bearing.​​​​​​​ That doesn't mean they're cited word for word, but it does mean there's a fundamental respect.​​​​​​​ The story itself is also a lot of fun while dealing with some serious topics: grief, othering, and identity. There's also the matter of the magic itself: characters who can use magic swiftly discover that it doesn't save them from their responsibilities and that, sometimes, it's a greater burden than a gift. When things are broken, they can't simply buy a upcoming wand.​​​​​​​​​Brighter than Nine completes the duology.

It shifts between murder mysteries, romantic entanglements, heavy gore, and self-aware humor without treating its melodrama as a distraction. True Blood leans into unapologetic sensuality, where desire is central to the plot. Vampire blood acts as both sustenance and an intoxicating, sensory trigger that blurs pain, pleasure, and power. It's the rush of intimate ecstasy that turns romance into a thrill ride. The story uses its setting's heat, humidity, and secrets to heighten the tension. At the same time, the concept of the "vampires out of the coffin" premise serves as a sharp debate on social and queer themes. From Sookie and Eric Northman's (Alexander Skarsgård) rival-to-romance tension-filled chemistry to Jason Stackhouse (Ryan Kwanten) and Jessica Hamby's (Deborah Ann Woll) chaotic, impulsive hookups, True Blood is never short of sex and intimacy. Even supernatural dream sequences are sexy spectacles! True Blood is not a show to watch with your parents around, no matter your age!

💡 Key Takeaways

  • I'm not going to share any spoilers here, but you should know that the side quests in Chapter 1 are important.
  • Recent findings suggest that if you're used to playing racing games, you'll find the driving experience in GTA VI to be quite different.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that I've been playing Grand Theft Auto VI since launch, and I'm having a blast so far. The world feels even more detailed and immersive than previous GTA games, which means there's a lot to learn beyond the basic tutorials and prompts the game shares at the beginning. These are the 10 GTA 6 hacks I used to improve the game's quality of life. If you do the same, you'll spend more time immersed in the world, and less time fighting the game's default settings.

I'm not going to share any spoilers here, but you should know that the side quests in Chapter 1 are important. If you ignore all the optional quests or small asks by other characters, you won't be able to return to those later. These are small things like fixing up the house for Lucia, meditating with her, and buying her a necklace when she asks you to. All of these have an impact on your progress. Take your time in this chapter, and remember to save before starting the mission called "Recalibration." That mission leads to Tourist Trap, which is the point of no return for Chapter 1.

Recent findings suggest that if you're used to playing racing games, you'll find the driving experience in GTA VI to be quite different. It's hard to keep an eye on minimap directions while you're also getting used to vehicles in the game, and I used voice navigation to ensure that I don't keep getting lost, particularly for time-sensitive missions. You can enable this by going to GTA VI settings > Audio > GPS Voice > Voice. If you're playing the game on PS5, your DualSense controller's speaker plays GPS voice prompts. This is great as those alerts can be hard to hear over all other in-game sounds from your TV's speaker.

Using GTA 6's default controls, making Jason and Lucia run is quite annoying. The game makes you hold L3 to run, which hurts my thumbs. If you alter movement speed in settings, you can make the characters run just by using the left stick. You can walk by easing off the left stick, or switch to a fast walk, jog, or run when you push the stick all the way. Tweak this by going to GTA VI settings > Gameplay > Movement Speed > Jog. This lets you move faster without draining your stamina. You can also change from Jog to Run if you want the fastest possible movement speed with the left stick. Having remarked that, my pro tip is to go to Control Scheme in settings, and switch to Classic. This lets you run by holding the X button, as opposed to L3 with default controls.

Sources indicate that haptic strength is one area where GTA 6 takes the immersion a bit too far, as it's dialed up to the maximum level by default. This makes the controller's vibration strength a bit too intense for my liking, and also has a negative impact on battery life. You can fix that by reducing haptic strength a little. It's under GTA VI settings > Controller > Vibration & Haptics Strength.

In a recent development, many modern controllers develop "stick drift," an matter where small movements of the analog sticks register as large inputs. This causes a significant problem in games that require precise inputs, such as GTA 6. To counter this potential problem, the game allows you to adjust the deadzone for each analog stick in your controller. That mentioned, this setting can be used to your advantage, even if you don't have stick drift complications in your controller. I recommend dialing up the deadzone to 7 to improve the driving experience. I find most cars in GTA 6 to be a bit floaty to drive, and adjusting the deadzone fixes this issue to a large extent.

Committing a heist attracts heat in GTA 6, and there are many different ways to escape the attention of in-game cops. The usual tricks include stocking up on outfits to change into, parking your vehicle a block or two away, and being so stealthy that you leave no witnesses to your crimes. However, an underrated trick involves using the pickup truck you get at the start of the game. Get a bike in the game, and stash it in your pickup truck. Then, use the truck to drive to the crime scene, and hide the truck a short distance away. Unload the bike, and use it to get to the crime scene. Once the heist is complete, ditch the bike, and run to your truck. Witnesses won't have seen you using the truck, which allows you to escape the area promptly.

If you are using a car as a getaway vehicle, you can use two tricks to make a smooth escape. First, double-tap the Triangle button to exit your vehicle without switching off its engine. When you return to the vehicle in a hurry, you can escape a lot faster. If you have quick fingers, you can double-tap Triangle first, and just as your character is about to exit the vehicle, press L3 (or X, if you use classic controls). This leaves the car's door open, and saves you a little more time when you're fleeing.

Recent findings suggest that I suffer from chronic migraines, and I am sensitive to bright lights. Fortunately, GTA 6 has a bunch of accessibility settings that help me play the game for longer. Even if you don't face the same complications, these settings will help reduce eye strain in longer play sessions. Go to GTA VI settings > Display > Flashbang, and switch to Dark. This stops flashbangs from showing a bright white light when they go off. On the same settings page, you can tweak Player Status Effects Intensity to reduce screen effects when your character is low on health or stamina. You can also enable Brightness Reduction to reduce the intensity of bright lights in the game, and try Focus Trail Colorblind Mode if you find it hard to distinguish between different colors.

It has been revealed that I haven't been able to play first-person shooters for decades because the camera movement makes me nauseous and gives me a headache. Of late, I've noticed that it's getting harder to play third-person games too. My first two hours in GTA 6 had me quite worried because I was feeling quite sick, and I had to turn off my PS5. Luckily for me, I found a few tweaks to mitigate this problem. You can do that in GTA VI settings > UI > Persistent Center Dot. This permanently highlights a white dot in the center of the screen, and it reduced my motion sickness enough to help me play the game. You can also go to GTA VI settings > Camera, reduce Camera Bob, and turn off Camera Shake, and Weapon Sway. I also recommend going to the Controller tab in settings, and tweaking all the options under Aim & Look Sensitivity until you find a comfortable level.

In a recent development, GTA 6 includes realistic ringing sounds that linger after explosions in the game. This may be fine for some people, but it can negatively affect some players' gaming sessions. Those who suffer from tinnitus or chronic migraines may not enjoy those ringing sounds, and, luckily, the game allows you to disable them. Open GTA 6's in-game settings, and enable the feature from Audio > Tinnitus Reduction.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

“The Right Stuff” was released 43 years ago, but its spectacular aerial and outer space sequences have lost none of their power. Director Philip Kaufman’s adaptation of Tom Wolfe’s book, which traced the history of the test pilots who became the first astronauts, features immersive set pieces that are still as convincing as ever, in spite of decades of technological advancements since it was made. To revisit it via Criterion‘s new 4K UHD physical media release is to experience one of the most groundbreaking and enduring films of all time.

Sources indicate that the latest Criterion transfer was supervised by cinematographer Caleb Deschanel, who was still relatively early in his career when Kaufman tapped him to shoot “The Right Stuff.” Deschanel didn’t have many feature credits, but the ones he did have were impressive: his early work included the stunning imagery of “The Black Stallion” and two Hal Ashby movies, “Being There” and the Rolling Stones concert film “Let’s Spend the Night Together.” He would earn the first of his six Academy Award nominations for “The Right Stuff.” Related Stories Where Are Rick Dalton and Sharon Tate in ‘The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth’? ‘Bad Lieutenant: Tokyo’ Will Come to the U.S. Next March.

Recent findings suggest that deschanel had met Kaufman years earlier when Deschanel was a film student at USC, and Kaufman was a young director working on the Western “The Great Northfield Minnesota Raid.” “A couple friends and I put on these rock shows at Shrine Auditorium, and he came to a couple of those,” Deschanel told IndieWire. Deschanel visited the set of “Minnesota” and stayed in touch with Kaufman, who called him around 10 years later with the offer to shoot “The Right Stuff.”.

Sources indicate that “It was a dream come true,” Deschanel remarked, noting that he had always been an aviation buff who loved going to air shows with his father. He also remembered that Kaufman wasn’t the only person on “The Right Stuff” who he had met years earlier. “Years before we had moved into our first house and needed some painting done, and we had a friend who was teaching in the Cal Arts theater department. He said, ‘I have this actor who’s really great who paints houses in the summer.'”.

Deschanel hired the young actor and got to know him a little bit, and five years later was having lunch with his wife Mary Jo and Kaufman when Kaufman indicated them a picture of the actor he had chosen to play John Glenn. “I said, ‘We know him. That’s Ed Harris. He painted our house,'” Deschanel said. “Then, coincidentally, the woman who was supposed to play Annie Glenn dropped out of and Phil cast my wife, so they ended up playing husband and wife in the movie.”.

Recent findings suggest that one of the great technical challenges of “The Right Stuff” was integrating archival footage of the space race with the upcoming material being shot — one of the reasons the movie was shot in a 1.85:1 aspect ratio instead of a wider Panavision format as one might have expected for such an epic film. “We were using actual footage of NASA’s rocket launches and things like that, and they were filming in the old-fashioned 4:3 format using the full frame of a 35mm camera,” Deschanel stated. “Converting that to widescreen was really impossible.”.

Sources indicate that working in close collaboration with visual effects supervisor Gary Gutierrez (who provides a fascinating look at the film’s miniature and rear-projection work on the Criterion disc), Deschanel solved the numerous logistical problems that came with trying to make it look as though the actors were hurtling through the air at the speed of sound and beyond. Even when Gutierrez thought he had solutions that would work, they often had to be tweaked to accommodate Kaufman’s desire to make everything feel as realistic and immersive as possible.

Early attempts to use a motion-control system for the effects, for example, were discarded because the camera movement was too smooth for Kaufman’s purposes. “Phil wanted it to have some energy to it,” Deschanel stated. “That changed the whole methodology.” Whenever rockets were taking off or various crafts were flying, Deschanel made sure to add some shake to the camera. “I actually gave my camera operator, Craig Denault, a black eye at one point because I was hitting the camera so hard.”.

In addition to the expected challenges, there were plenty of unexpected ones as well — like the fact that Sam Shepard, who played ace pilot Chuck Yeager, wouldn’t fly. “The only time he ever went up in an airplane was when Yeager took him for a flight,” Deschanel remarked. “Other than that, whenever we had a mockup of an X-1 or the F-104 or anything like that, he’d make me get in and show him how it was going to twist and turn before he would get into it.” For Yeager’s scenes and many of the others, rear projection was used — meaning Deschanel had to photograph what was seen outside the pilots’ and astronauts’ windows long before the actors’ material was actually shot.

According to recent reports, “There was a lot of complexity to all those things,” Deschanel stated. “But it gave it a real energy and sense of being there. And that’s what you try to discover as you’re filming any film: what is that visual metaphor that really makes you believe you’re having the same experience the characters are having?” Creating that sense of authenticity required some unorthodox approaches, as when Deschanel had a Learjet pilot take the nose cone off of his plane and replace it with a clear dome.

“We put a camera in there with a 15mm lens, and then we were able to go up above 50,000 feet,” Deschanel said. “At that level, it’s so dark, it’s almost like you’re in outer space. Anything you could think of to find the reality of the movie, we employed.” Deschanel’s perfectionism became the stuff of legend over the years, with some people who worked on “The Right Stuff” claiming he insisted on shooting only at sunrise or sunset to get the most beautiful possible images — a myth Deschanel is quick to dispel.

In a recent development, “The fact is we shot all day long and had really long days,” Deschanel said. “There was one point where, just to finish up at Edwards Air Force Base, I was on for 24 hours and changed the crew in the middle. So I had a whole upcoming crew for the second half of that long day.” That said, Deschanel acknowledges that the film’s justly famous exteriors were important to him, in part for what they represented.

It has been revealed that “The iconic moment is when Yeager is on horseback, and he rides up and sees the X-1,” Deschanel remarked. “It’s like ‘The Professionals’ or ‘The Wild Bunch,’ these movies about the end of the West as new technology takes over. To me, there’s this wonderful representation of the end of an era when Yeager comes across this fighter jet. Then, of course, he flies it and breaks the sound barrier. So it’s this wonderful juxtaposition of important moments in human history, where one person does something that further advances flight to the point that makes it possible for the next generation to go into outer space. I always miss that I never got to make a Western, but in a way, ‘The Right Stuff’ is a Western.”.

“The Right Stuff” special edition 4K UHD release is now available from Criterion.

Among iOS 27’s many latest features is a great change for anyone with multiple iPhones: you can now keep the same phone number on two iPhones via iPhone Handoff.

With iOS 27, Apple introduces big AI upgrades like Siri AI, plus exciting new features for apps like Wallet, Messages, Notes, and also CarPlay and AirPods.

But the revision also has a lot of smaller, more niche improvements.

One such addition is iPhone Handoff, which enables switching seamlessly between two iPhones using the same phone number.

Here’s how it works, per Apple:.

After iPhone Handoff is set up, one iPhone becomes the main iPhone and the other iPhone becomes the secondary iPhone that shares the number. Your main iPhone should be the one you use most often. Some carrier services, like Call Forwarding and Caller ID, and carrier account management can only be managed on your main iPhone. Contact your carrier for more details.

Sources indicate that to move between your main iPhone and secondary iPhone, simply unlock the device that you want to start using — your phone number will automatically become active on that device. The message “Switched to this iPhone” will display at the top of your screen to confirm it’s now active. Your phone number will only be active on one iPhone at a time when using iPhone Handoff.

Most consumers will never need this feature. But if you’re someone who, for whatever reason, has separate devices that you want on the same number, iOS 27 has the solution.

I feel like I’m exactly who this feature was made for. After years of running dual SIM, I now have a personal line on my Duo and work line on an 18 Pro. Going out with friends, family, etc, I’d love to bring one phone again while bringing both numbers with me, but keeping work system access to a specific, separate device. Only current problem is waiting for Verizon to activate the feature and then see if it actually works well.

If you’re trying to decide between an iPhone Duo and iPhone 18 Pro, perhaps iPhone Handoff is Apple’s subtle way of saying: “Why choose?”.

So far carrier support is limited (here’s the latest list), but Apple plans to expand iPhone Handoff to more carriers soon.

10 Classic Books Worth Reading Over and Over

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Most of us treat classic literature like a checklist to conquer in high school or college and then never touch those books again.
  • When you reread classic literature, everything changes: you stop rushing toward the finale and focus instead on how the author pulled it all off.
  • Industry observers note that following an impoverished former student who believes extraordinary individuals can commit terrible acts in service of a greater purpose, Fyodor Dostoevsky’s Crime and Punishment is a descent into the mind of a murderer slowly unraveling under the weight of his own conscience.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Most of us treat classic literature like a checklist to conquer in high school or college and then never touch those books again. You power through the plot, underline a few quotes for a term paper, and move on to whatever else is fresh. The catch is that great books rarely reveal their most fascinating tricks on the first pass. When you already know the ending, your brain stops racing for answers and begins to notice the machinery holding all those mysteries and themes together. Suddenly, an unreliable narrator's sleight of hand becomes obvious, or a throwaway line in chapter two hits like a freight train in light of later developments.

When you reread classic literature, everything changes: you stop rushing toward the finale and focus instead on how the author pulled it all off. Whether they reshape your perspective as you age or hide their best clues in plain sight, these 10 books reward you on every return trip.

Industry observers note that following an impoverished former student who believes extraordinary individuals can commit terrible acts in service of a greater purpose, Fyodor Dostoevsky’s Crime and Punishment is a descent into the mind of a murderer slowly unraveling under the weight of his own conscience. At the story’s center is Rodion Raskolnikov, a desperate and isolated young man living in the squalid slums of St. Petersburg who sets out to prove his own moral superiority. After murdering a pawnbroker, he is consumed by paranoia and the unbearable weight of his own guilt.​​​​​​​.

According to recent reports, dostoevsky borrows the mechanics of a detective novel as he weaves Raskolnikov’s psychological fallout into the overriding mystery, setting aside the familiar detective-versus-killer plot to peer into the killer’s mind​​​​​​​. When you aren't racing through its pages to see whether Raskolnikov gets caught by the investigator Porfiry Petrovich, you savor the cat-and-mouse mind games between them. Every feverish rationalization and defensive outburst reads like a man slowly building his own prison cell.

In a recent development, franz Kafka's The Trial is one of those rare books that becomes more unsettling the older you get. Josef K. is a bank employee who is suddenly arrested by an inexplicable authority for a crime that is never identified, though he is not confined to a conventional prison. Instead, Josef has to navigate a secretive court system whose offices occupy cramped attics in a residential neighborhood while trying to defend himself against charges nobody will explain.​​​​​​​ He appears before an unruly crowd of onlookers at a hearing and consults a bedridden lawyer named Herr Huld, who never seems to make any progress on his case.​​​​​​​.

In a recent development, kafka's masterpiece is a nightmare about institutional powerlessness, highlighting the absurdity of bureaucracy. It’s a compelling read​​​​​​​, a piece of fiction that proves the systems governing our lives can be profoundly irrational​​​​​​​. Its themes have only become more relevant with time, rewarding a second read once you stop looking for a logical explanation to the plot and start noticing Josef as he slowly pieces together the irrational system at play.

According to recent reports, few narrators divide readers quite like Holden Caulfield, a grieving teenager wandering through Manhattan in a red hunting hat after getting kicked out of yet another prep school. Across three wandering days in The Catcher in the Rye, J.D. Salinger lets Holden complain endlessly about the “phoniness” around him while quietly exposing the trauma and loneliness driving his cynicism.

Recent findings suggest that reading the novel in high school usually feels like an act of rebellion, as readers side with a misunderstood kid​​​​​​​, but coming back to it as an adult transforms the entire experience. Holden's defensive anger turns into a heartbreaking portrait of a boy terrified of growing up in the wake of losing his younger brother. Even the adults in the story land differently on a second pass, shifting from out-of-touch villains to exhausted people​​​​​​​ trying to keep a spiraling teenager from falling off a cliff.

Joseph Conrad's Heart of Darkness turns a riverboat expedition into a suffocating descent into human cruelty. The novella follows Charles Marlow, a British sailor hired to pilot a steamer up the Congo River to retrieve Kurtz, a highly successful ivory trader who has cut off contact and turned a remote outpost into his personal kingdom.

Sources indicate that as Marlow pushes deeper into the stark jungle, the supposed civility of his European employers slowly gives way, revealing​​​​​​​ unchecked greed and violence. On first pass, it’s easy to get swept up in the atmospheric writing and mystery surrounding Kurtz, which is why rereading it feels like stepping into a completely different story. Knowing how the journey ends makes every return trip that much more fascinating, turning Conrad's fog-choked prose into a trail of clues about Marlow's own complicity.

In a recent development, there are plenty of novels that explore the pursuit of the American Dream, but few understand its inherent contradictions quite like F. Scott Fitzgerald's The Great Gatsby. Set during the Roaring Twenties, the plot mostly centers on Jay Gatsby, the mysterious and wealthy neighbor of Nick Carraway, the story’s narrator. Gatsby’s lavish parties conceal an obsessive desire to reunite with his former love, Daisy Buchanan, but hiding beneath all the champagne, extravagant cars, and glittering excess is a deeply tragic story about the impossibility of recapturing the past.

Fitzgerald's writing is top-notch, while the characters remain endlessly fascinating. It’s no surprise The Great Gatsby has remained recommended reading for years, offering a sharp critique of the American Dream whose subtle clues hit much harder once you already know how Gatsby's story ends​​​​​​​.

The Sun Also Rises is Ernest Hemingway's portrait of a generation struggling to find meaning in the aftermath of World War I. The protagonist, Jake Barnes, is an American journalist part of a circle of expatriate friends​​​​​​​ who drift through Paris and Spain in a haze of heavy drinking and late-night parties as they attempt to escape hidden emotional wounds.

At the center of the story is Jake's complicated relationship with Lady Brett Ashley, a woman he loves but cannot fully be with because of a war injury that has left him impotent. Hemingway's famously restrained prose gives the book much of its power on a second read, letting you catch the quiet heartbreak and disillusionment buried beneath seemingly ordinary conversations, a hallmark of Hemingway’s craft​​​​​​​.

Sources indicate that jane Austen's Pride and Prejudice is one of the most enduring romantic novels ever written, and there's a reason readers keep returning to it more than two centuries after its publication. Set in rural Regency-era England, the story follows a sharp-witted young woman named Elizabeth Bennet navigating the expectations of English society while attempting to find a suitable marriage without sacrificing her independence. Her complicated relationship with the wealthy and aloof Mr. Darcy provides the foundation for an entertaining social satire that skewers class obsession and the assumptions we make about other people.

In a recent development, much like The Sun Also Rises, the dialogue in Pride and Prejudice is razor-sharp, while Austen’s characters are wonderfully realized. Her observations about human behavior prove remarkably timeless, with every reread revealing how subtly she signals Darcy's early affection despite his stiff manners​​​​​​​. It's a delightful book that never seems to lose its charm, and only gets better the more times you experience Elizabeth's stubbornness.

A Tale of Two Cities is an enormous historical drama set against the backdrop of the French Revolution, following characters caught between the political upheaval of Paris and the relative stability of London. At its center is Charles Darnay, a French aristocrat attempting to escape his family's violent legacy, and Sydney Carton, a disillusioned English lawyer whose love for Darnay's wife, Lucie, places him​​​​​​​ on a path toward an extraordinary act of sacrifice.

Industry observers note that charles Dickens brings the chaos and brutality of revolutionary France to life while weaving together a deeply moving story about the possibility of personal transformation. It's a sweeping, emotionally powerful novel that builds toward one of literature's most unforgettable conclusions. Knowing the finale changes how every preceding chapter reads​​​​​​​, making Sydney Carton's early apathy and reckless drinking feel like quiet clues to the man he would inevitably become​​​​​​​.

Set in ancient India, Siddhartha tracks a young man who abandons his privileged upbringing to pursue spiritual enlightenment. Along the way, he tests himself through asceticism, material wealth, and romantic love, while seeking guidance from seasoned teachers​​​​​​​, gradually discovering that no outside philosophy can provide him with the answers he seeks​​​​​​​.

What makes Siddhartha so unforgettable on a reread is how it frames personal growth as something messy rather than linear. Real change often requires stumbling into failure or temptation first, forcing you to deal with immediate consequences before you can recognize what actually matters. It is a brisk read built for repeated visits, yet its lessons hold up across a lifetime.

According to recent reports, on the surface, Jonas lives in a peaceful utopia where hunger, suffering, and social conflict have largely been eradicated, yet that stability depends on stripping away emotional depth, collective memory, and individual choice. At the Ceremony of Twelve in Lois Lowry's The Giver, Jonas is chosen as the next Receiver of Memory rather than receiving a standard community assignment​​​​​​​. His training with the old Receiver introduces him to sensations the rest of the community never experiences, from sled rides in deep snow to the warmth of sunshine and the shock of physical agony.

As Jonas absorbs such memories, he begins seeing cracks in his orderly world, especially as he notices flashes of color and questions​​​​​​​ the community's treatment of Gabriel, a young child who has been marked for release. Rereading The Giver makes the quiet dread much sharper because you already know what "release" actually means long before Jonas pieces it together. The polite rituals of the “evening telling of feelings” and the community’s calm routines seem less like signs of peace than evidence of a society sedated into forgetting what it gave up.​​​​​​​ Lowry trusts younger readers with heavy moral questions without ever talking down to them. Returning to the book years later hits differently because the horror shifts away from the shocking twists toward the quiet complicity of the adults who willingly traded away their humanity just to feel safe.

💡 Key Takeaways
