  • In a recent development, technically, “Hundreds of Beavers” has never left theaters.
  • According to recent reports, the re-releases have become a holiday tradition for “Hundreds of Beavers,” which for all its wintery setting and its main character dressed like Santa, is being positioned as a upcoming Christmas movie.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, it’s been four years since the cult hit “Hundreds of Beavers” first debuted and still two years since it started really gaining traction with wider audiences in 2024. But if it feels like the black and white, silent, slapstick indie comedy still hasn’t left the cultural conversation, that’s because in all that time it has continued to quietly play in theaters and attract audiences both loyal and newly introduced alike.

In a recent development, technically, “Hundreds of Beavers” has never left theaters. It continues to play individual screenings in a city or two every weekend. Now, though, “Hundreds of Beavers” is set to return to theaters for what is its biggest theatrical expansions to date. The film will kick off its third annual Northwoods Christmas, which will feature 130 screenings across 85 cities, with more to likely be added in the coming weeks. It came about after another fan campaign pushed for the film to come to some markets it hadn’t previously thought about or targeted such as Indianapolis and Charlottesville, and it will now play in everything from concert venues to microcinemas. Related Stories Cinematographer Caleb Deschanel on Finding the Right Techniques For ‘The Right Stuff’ Where Are Rick Dalton and Sharon Tate in ‘The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth’?

According to recent reports, the re-releases have become a holiday tradition for “Hundreds of Beavers,” which for all its wintery setting and its main character dressed like Santa, is being positioned as a upcoming Christmas movie. The first time “Hundreds of Beavers” was re-released at Christmas 2024, which was shortly after the Blu-ray for the film became available, it brought in $118K at the box office in a month, and the producers continued the tradition in 2025.

Recent findings suggest that “There’s room for a Christmas tradition with the energy of a ‘Rocky Horror’ screening,” noted producer Kurt Ravenwood. “You can watch ‘It’s a Wonderful Life’ and ‘White Christmas’ all you want, but for getting together with friends and family to laugh about the miserable winter ahead, ‘Hundreds of Beavers’ has them all beat.”.

Recent findings suggest that each of the screenings will be preceded by a short film featuring “Bing Crosbeaver,” which they did last year, but this will be a latest short with a new twist in which another character named “Conspirabeaver” will be joined by a “sinister foe,” per the release. Some of the in-person beavers in costume will be present at the screenings, and fans will also get a promotional poster for the movie. The “Beavers” team recently released a few parody posters ripping off the recent releases of “You Can See Everything,” “Digger,” and “The Devils.”.

To date, “Hundreds of Beavers” has made $940,092 at the domestic box office, including another $618,014 internationally to bring its worldwide total to above $1.5 million. It’s done all this via first producing the film for just $150,000 and spending little more than $70,000 on ads, publicity, and its many roadshow screenings. It’s also been released entirely independently, starting with a run in the Midwest where the film is set before it started expanding to the coasts.

It has been revealed that incredibly, more than 70 percent of the film’s U.S. box office has come after “Hundreds of Beavers” began streaming way back on April 15, 2024, and it has even sold more than 20,000 Blu-Rays worldwide. It’s a rare, truly indie success story even in a day and age when many movies have pursued self-distribution strategies.

According to recent reports, for those who haven’t had the pleasure of seeing “Hundreds of Beavers” in theaters yet, the film is about a drunken applejack salesman who loses everything and has to survive the winter by becoming North America’s greatest fur trapper. It sees the trapper wrestling and fighting with dozens of beavers and other forest animals all wearing mascot suits, with the stark black and white cinematography and creative physical stunts embracing a zany video game logic and absurd silent comedy slapstick gags.

The film is directed by Mike Cheslik and was written by Cheslik and star Ryland Tews, with the film also starring Olivia Graves, Wes Tank, Doug Mancheski, and Luis Rico.

For fans eager to see more of the Hightowers outside HBO's acclaimed fantasy series, one of the family's most iconic characters has officially returned to the franchise with Devoted Light.

Alicent Hightower has officially returned to the Game of Thrones franchise as a new Commander in Dragonfire, the free-to-play mobile strategy game inspired by HBO's House of the Dragon. Officially detailed on November 24, Alicent Hightower: Devoted Light depicts the character in her younger years, when her friendship with Rhaenyra had yet to give way to one of the most consequential rivalries in Westerosi history.

As the official Dragonfire character description reads:.

Gentle in manner but keenly observant, Alicent understands how little freedom is granted to daughters of great houses. Her affection for Rhaenyra is true, yet it is tested by a father’s ambitions and a court where obedience may carry a heavier price than defiance.

Alicent's three unique Talents are particularly fitting given her characterization in House of the Dragon:.

According to recent reports, the recently introduced Commander system is a game-changer for Dragonfire, giving players way more freedom when assembling their armies. With eight distinct Dragon Traits and Commanders who specialize in different combat strategies, dragons that players previously overlooked are suddenly indispensable.

In a recent development, perhaps most importantly, Commanders and their upgrades carry over between reigns, giving players another meaningful avenue for permanent progression. With Rhaenyra, Daemon, Criston Cole, and Corlys Velaryon also among the initial wave of Commanders, the possibilities for future additions from the extended Game of Thrones universe are particularly exciting.

The same two incredible cases come in iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max versions, and they also fit the iPhone 17 Pro and Pro Max. The ESR Classic Hybrid Magnetic Case with Camera Control and Flex Stand has a clear back, a TPU frame, and a PU anti-yellowing coating. In simple terms, TPU is the flexible, shock-absorbing plastic used in most case frames, and it’s also what usually turns clear cases slightly yellow the longer you use them, so ESR adds a polyurethane (PU) coating to shield it. ESR upgraded the case’s UV protection for longer-lasting resistance to yellowing, and it’s SGS-certified for anti-yellowing. A clear case is supposed to show off your iPhone’s color, so staying clear longer is the whole point. The ESR Atelier Vegan Leather Magnetic Case with Flex Stand retains the same soft silicone leather and stain-resistant finish as the iPhone Duo version.

Recent findings suggest that on these models, the Flex Stand adjusts from 15 to 69 degrees for portrait and landscape viewing. That has you covered for StandBy mode on your nightstand and a show over your lunch break, with no separate stand to carry around.

It has been revealed that protection is where the two cases differ. ESR rates the Classic Hybrid for 4x military-grade protection with 16-foot drop protection, plus a full-coverage camera bar. The Atelier is rated for 3x military-grade protection, including 12-foot drop protection, and features a soft microfiber lining. Military-grade refers to the MIL-STD-810 drop test, which uses a 4-foot drop, so 4x and 3x mean ESR rates the cases for four and three times that height. Both include a built-in Camera Control cover and raised edges, and both use a precise magnetic ring layout that automatically aligns with MagSafe chargers, car mounts, wallets, and batteries.

Black Friday deal: The ESR Classic Hybrid Magnetic Case is up to 28% off, and the ESR Atelier Vegan Leather Magnetic Case is up to 37% off.

A case protects everything except the part you touch all day. The ESR UltraFit Armorite Pro Screen Protector covers the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max, and the name is worth unpacking. Armorite is ESR’s line of toughened screen protectors, and the Pro version is made with Accessory Glass by Corning™. Corning has made the durable glass in Apple products since the very first iPhone, so in non-tech speak, this is glass from a trustworthy name rather than generic tempered glass.

Sources indicate that why it matters: ESR notes the protector delivers 10x the impact absorption of generic protectors, and Corning’s lab testing indicates up to 2x better scratch performance and up to 25% less scratch visibility for its Accessory Glass. When you drop your iPhone or toss it in a pocket with your keys, the protector takes the hit instead of your screen. An anti-reflective coating reduces light reflection to just 2.3% while maintaining 94% optical transmittance, resulting in less glare outside and truer color. Edge-to-edge coverage leaves no gaps for dust to collect.

Industry observers note that installation is the part most people dread on a brand-new iPhone, and ESR’s UltraFit tray handles it in two steps. Pull the tab, and the tray’s design clears dust and pushes out air bubbles as the glass goes down. Long gone are the days when you needed “professional installation” for a screen protector to look great.

Black Friday deal: The ESR UltraFit Armorite Pro Screen Protector is 15% off.

Holiday travel usually means one open outlet, an iPhone, a laptop, an e-reader, etc., that all need power, and cables left at home. The ESR Xtend 45W Retractable Charger builds the cable in. It has a braided cable that extends to 3.1 feet and fully retracts into the charger, and ESR rates it for 20,000 pulls and 10,000 bends. An extra USB-C port lets a second device charge simultaneously. 9to5Mac’s Michael Burkhardt went hands-on with the Xtend 45W earlier this month and mentioned it’s an excellent iPhone fast charger on the go.

Sources indicate that it’s rated at 45 watts and delivers up to 60 watts of dynamic power, enough to fast-charge phones and laptops, and it works with iPhone Duo, iPhone 15 through 18, and Android phones like Galaxy and Pixel. It supports PD 3.2 AVS, which in plain English means the charger and your device talk to each other, and the charger fine-tunes the power it sends to exactly what that device asks for. ESR says it can charge an iPhone 18 Pro or Pro Max to 50% in about 15 minutes. It’s also TÜV-certified, meaning an independent testing organization has verified its safety features.

Black Friday deal: The ESR Xtend 45W Retractable Charger is up to 32% off from November 20 through December 1.

For the student or anyone who does real work on an iPad, the ESR Shift Keyboard Case makes for an incredible gift. The Bluetooth keyboard attaches magnetically and comes off when you don’t need it, so you can type an essay at a desk, then pull the keyboard away to watch something on the couch or sketch with the iPad flat on a table.

ESR built the Shift around five modes designed to make your iPad even more versatile. Productivity mode lets you detach the keyboard and type over Bluetooth, so the iPad can sit on a desk while the keyboard sits on your lap. Landscape mode adjusts from 20 to 75 degrees for typing and watching, Portrait mode holds 70 degrees for reading, browsing in Safari, or making a FaceTime call, and Drawing mode drops to a stable 20 degrees for sketching and editing with your Apple Pencil. Hands-On mode lets you hold the iPad like a regular tablet. An iPad is a laptop one minute and a tablet the next, and the Shift is designed to keep up with all of your iPad use cases.

Industry observers note that for a student, that means taking notes in class with the keyboard attached, then detaching it to annotate a PDF or review flashcards on the couch. For someone who travels for work, it means answering email on a tray table, then pulling the keyboard off to watch a movie on the flight home. One case covers both, and the keyboard pairs and reconnects easily when you snap it back on.

Industry observers note that the trackpad is fully clickable and supports all the multi-touch gestures you already use on your iPad. Apple Pencil gets a home too. ESR’s Dual Smart Pencil Storage uses a magnetic holder and an elastic sleeve, so your Pencil stays with your iPad instead of rolling around the bottom of your bag. Its Air Guard corners protect your iPad when it’s stowed away.

The ESR Shift Keyboard Case comes in versions for iPad Pro 11-inch and 13-inch (M4 and M5), iPad Air 11-inch and 13-inch (including the fresh M4 models), and iPad (A16), so whichever iPad you’re trying to take to the next level of productivity, there’s a Shift that fits it.

Black Friday deal: The ESR Shift Keyboard Case is up to 25% off, depending on your iPad model.

Have you ever dropped your AirPods case and watched the earbuds go flying? With the Cyber FlickLock, you won’t have to worry about that. We’ve covered FlickLock in MagSafe Monday before, but let’s recap it.

Recent findings suggest that when the internal latch is engaged, the magnets line up to attract each other and hold the lid shut with maximum force, adding a second layer of security. Slide the button, and the magnets shift to repel each other, so the lid pops open with one hand. ESR indicates the slide mechanism has been tested over 20,000 times.

It has been revealed that the result is that your AirPods stay in the case if you drop it. Both cases also have 260g of magnetic strength, so they snap onto MagSafe chargers, Apple Watch chargers, and MagSafe batteries if you need to charge your AirPods. Again, it’s extremely strong, but extremely easy to unlock with one hand.

Recent findings suggest that the ESR Cyber FlickLock Magnetic Case is extremely durable and has a clip hook, so you can hang your AirPods on a backpack while hiking or cycling. The ESR Pulse FlickLock Magnetic Case brings the same lock in a range of vibrant colors with a carrying lanyard, so you can wear your AirPods on your wrist or attach them to a bag. Both cases come in versions for AirPods Pro 3, AirPods Pro 2 and 1, and AirPods 5 and 4. No matter which AirPods you or your loved one have, this is the case everyone will love.

Black Friday deal: The ESR Cyber FlickLock and Pulse FlickLock Magnetic Cases are both 20% off.

The ESR Equinox Watch Band is a quick pick for anyone who works out in the morning while tracking progress with Apple Watch, then heads to the office. A pin-and-fold lock keeps it secure, and it’s made from HNBR, a durable, skin-friendly synthetic rubber that resists water and tearing, with ventilation cutouts for all-day comfort. It fits 44mm, 45mm, 46mm, and 49mm models across Apple Watch Ultra 1 through 4, Series 4 through 12, and SE 1 through 3, and it comes in several colors to match your outfit or your mood that day.

Black Friday deal: The ESR Equinox Watch Band is 20% off.

Industry observers note that the best gifts are the ones that get used every day, and accessories are the part of the Apple experience people live with the most. A case that props up a foldable, a screen protector made with Corning glass, a charger with a built-in cable, and an AirPods case that stays closed even when dropped check all the boxes. ESR truly makes something for everyone and is one of the most trusted names in the Apple accessories ecosystem.

According to recent reports, ESR built its Black Friday lineup around the whole Apple ecosystem, from the new iPhone Duo to iPad, AirPods, and even a great Apple Watch band, with premium materials and versatile designs that are durable, functional, and great-looking. ESR’s Black Friday and Cyber Monday deals run on Amazon from November 19 through November 30 (the Xtend 45W runs through December 1), with discounts of up to 37%!

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that the last time Sam Rockwell worked with Martin McDonagh, he ended up winning an Academy Award for his performance in Three Billboards Outside Ebbing, Missouri, having previously worked with McDonagh on Seven Psychopaths. There were another nine Oscar nominations for McDonagh's work four years ago when he reunited Colin Farrell and Brendan Gleeson for The Banshees of Inisherin, and this year, it's the turn of Rockwell and John Malkovich to play two men whose relationship is explored through McDonagh's own distinctive brand of dark comedy. Unfortunately, if you've been planning to see the movie over Thanksgiving weekend, it's about to become considerably more difficult to find a theater showing it.

According to the latest theater count figures from The Numbers, McDonagh's Wild Horse Nine has officially lost 1,000 theaters heading into its fourth weekend of release, reducing its domestic theatrical footprint by exactly 50%. Having opened in 1,100 theaters on November 6, the movie expanded to 2,175 locations in its second weekend, but it will now be playing in 100 fewer theaters than it was on opening day.

According to recent reports, wild Horse Nine is alos nearing the $20 million milestone, having made $18.31 million domestically to date, with $2.46 million of that coming last weekend, when its grosses fell by 46%. The movie was averaging $1,231 per theater over the weekend, although that figure dropped to just $192 on Monday. With Thanksgiving bringing a particularly competitive weekend for theaters, McDonagh's movie has now lost more than 54% of its locations since the second weekend of its release.

McDonagh takes us to Chile in 1973, where two CIA agents are sent to Easter Island shortly before the military coup. For Malkovich's Chris, who's spending an increasing amount of time contemplating his own mortality, there's quite a bit of history between himself and Rockwell's Lee to reckon with, and things become rather more complicated for the two men when Chris befriends a pair of students on the island.

Written and directed by McDonagh, the movie features Malkovich (Con Air) as Chris Carlisle, Rockwell (Moon) as Lee Chesterfield, Steve Buscemi (Boardwalk Empire) as MJ, Mariana di Girolamo (Ema) as Monica, Ailín Salas (The German Doctor) as Alicia, Tom Waits (Seven Psychopaths) as Jim, and Parker Posey (The White Lotus) as Marge.

According to recent reports, wild Horse Nine is currently playing in theaters. Stay tuned to Collider for all the latest box office news and updates.

  • It has been revealed that additionally, IndieWire has declared that the incoming awards ceremony will be hosted by writer and comedian Demi Adejuyigbe, whose latest special “Demi Adejuyigbe Is Going to Do 1 (One) Backflip” is now available to stream on Dropout.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that indieWire, the definitive outlet for creative independence in film and TV, announced on Wednesday, November 25 the final additions to the lineup for the Winter 2026 edition of our IndieWire Honors event, featuring our largest lineup yet of film honorees. Curated and selected by IndieWire’s editorial team, IndieWire Honors is a celebration of the filmmakers, actors, and artisans key to crafting some of the most exciting cinematic works this year.

According to recent reports, the newly unveiled honorees include “The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth” star Yahya Abdul-Mateen II and costume designer Trish Summerville, who will be receiving the Spotlight Award. They join previously announced honorees John Turturro, Monica Barbaro, Andrew Garfield, Ike Barinholtz, Yura Borisov, James Gray, Adam Driver, Beth de Araújo, Mason Reeves, Gemma Chan, Ruth Madeley, David Greaves, Javier Ambrossi, Javier Calvo, Jeon Do-yeon, Anthony Ippolito, James Ortiz, Neal Scanlan, Mag Sarnowska, Paul Lambert, and Travis Knight. Related Stories Cult Hit ‘Hundreds of Beavers’ Returns to Theaters for Big Christmas Expansion Cinematographer Caleb Deschanel on Finding the Right Techniques For ‘The Right Stuff’.

It has been revealed that additionally, IndieWire has declared that the incoming awards ceremony will be hosted by writer and comedian Demi Adejuyigbe, whose latest special “Demi Adejuyigbe Is Going to Do 1 (One) Backflip” is now available to stream on Dropout. Previous IndieWire Honors emcees include Emmy winner Alex Edelman, Emmy nominee Robby Hoffman, multi-hyphenate Dewayne Perkins, and lauded comedians Vinny Thomas and Atsuko Okatsuka.

IndieWire Honors will take place on Thursday, December 3 in Los Angeles, starting with an intimate cocktail reception and awards ceremony. IndieWire will also begin rolling out exclusive editorial content, including honoree profiles, on Friday, November 27 through the lead-up to the awards night. Throughout the ceremony, into the next day, IndieWire will publish photos and exclusive social content from the event as well.

“It’s thrilling to be able to recognize the artists behind so many of this year’s most exciting and compelling films,” remarked Brent Lang, IndieWire’s editor-in-chief. “They dazzled us with their talent, inspired us with their willingness to take risks, and left an indelible mark on cinema. We are excited to celebrate their accomplishments.”.

“It’s exciting to celebrate such an eclectic group of film talent for this year’s IndieWire Honors,” said James Israel, IndieWire’s SVP and Publisher. “We are also pleased to continue to celebrate top craft artisans in entertainment.”.

The Winter 2026 IndieWire Honors honorees are:.

The fact that he is known for being a frequent collaborator of both Spike Lee and the Coen brothers conveys just how expansive an actor Turturro is. The Brooklyn native is quintessentially New York, as most recently proven in Sony Pictures Classics’ acclaimed Sundance premiere “The Only Living Pickpocket in New York,” written and directed by Noah Segan. Yet, a filmmaker can still drop the performer into the corporate dystopia of sci-fi series “Severance,” or have him go on a Southern odyssey in “O Brother, Where Art Thou?,” and he just as well hits it out of the park.

With nearly five decades of film work under his belt, starting with an uncredited role in “Raging Bull,” Turturro manages to be one of the few veteran actors who continues to best himself year after year.

Industry observers note that the pair of Madrid-based directors colloquially known as Los Javis are not shy about cluing the audience in on the shoulders upon which they stand on. They cast Penélope Cruz and Lola Dueñas, two muses of auteur Pedro Almodóvar, as the most important women within their epic adaptation of an unfinished play by Federico García Lorca, another one of Spain’s queer artist forefathers. That reverence is balanced by the confidence in their own eye for new talent, weaving together three different timelines led by three relative unknowns, including most notably, indie musician Guitarricadelafuente, who also contributed the poignant original song “La Nieve” to the project.

Made outside the Hollywood system and chosen to represent Spain in the Best International Feature Oscar race, the Netflix release “La Bola Negra” is a film of immense scale. If viewers knew nothing of the director duo before seeing the film, they come away with a crash course in everything they are about. Considering how they won both the Best Director Award at Cannes, and the coveted People’s Choice Award at TIFF, it seems to be an experience most cinephiles enjoy.

“Tallgrass” is the code word that unlocks what makes the creative collaboration between “Paper Tiger” writer-director James Gray and star Adam Driver such a feat. Though the Neon release, which premiered at Cannes, is their first time ever working together, the filmmaker imbues the two-time Oscar nominee with such a specific vision of what it feels like to realize one’s time has gone by. Though the film is another deeply personal work in the oeuvre of the Queens-born auteur, Driver adds a more broad portrait of a figure wrapped up in crime, slowly feeling the overwhelming situation constrict and constrict.

According to recent reports, “Josephine” was not made to be an easy watch, but boasts the rare feat of winning both the Grand Jury Prize and Audience Award at the Sundance Film Festival. Written and directed by Araújo, and starring Gemma Chan and Mason Reeves as mother and daughter, the drama is a bold exploration of how little control parents have over their children being confronted by certain horrors in life that there’s no guarantee of avoiding.

An early release for latest distributor Sumerian Pictures, “Josephine” has only felt more necessary as the year has gone on, and news stories like the Cornell rape case have come to the forefront. It is a conversation piece about a subject many wish to evade, that puts forth the effort to reach meaningful discourse.

According to recent reports, the most bold artistic choice in “Artificial,” the latest film from prolific director Luca Guadagnino, is to not proffer any romance in becoming one of the Promethean figures. The repeated refrain of “Feel the AGI” rings as a benevolent threat by the time the two hours and 20 minutes of the Neon release are over. Garfield, Borisov, Barbaro, and Barinholtz, all four playing key figures in the genesis of OpenAI, play incredibly off of each other as tech titans forcing a smile as they convince their audience artificial technology is inevitable. Join or die. Their joint efforts to invoke a common sense of humanity would be funny if the reality of the situation weren’t so uncanny.

In a recent development, re-teaming with her “Secret Sunshine” director Lee Chang-dong almost 20 years later, the “Possible Love” star is unmissable as a woman caught in a class divide between her blue collar, out-of-work husband, and the couple that hosts them as a means to interview them for a documentary. It is a role that she mentioned uses “the whole entirety of her body” to push back against the weight of capitalism. The Netflix film chosen to represent South Korea in the Best International Feature category at the 2027 Oscars offers a feast of ideas, with Jeon’s layered turn as Mi-ok alone being enough fodder for many conversations to come.

All sorts of biopics enter theaters each year, but few task their leads with the difficult job of playing someone still actively in the public eye. In Peter Farrelly’s “I Play Rocky,” from Amazon MGM Studios, newcomer Ippolito deftly captures the distinctive look and sound of a young and hungry Sylvester Stallone. But what is more impressive than that form of transformation is how the 27-year-old actor captures the spirit of the unlikely star and scribe of the 1977 Best Picture winner. How some of his best moments come when he himself plays Rocky is a meta element we are still unpacking, but add it to the overwhelming evidence that Ippolito is one to watch.

There is a standout moment in Oscar winner Siân Heder’s “Being Heumann” in which Madeley, as trailblazing disability rights activist Judy Heumann, asks a well-meaning congressman what he means by calling her “inspiring.” “Inspired to do what?,” she indicates. It is a moment that clarifies that the film about Heumann leading the successful protest to get the government to sign Section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act is not standard fare about a woman in a wheelchair overcoming odds, but a film about her refusing to let those odds overcome her.

It has been revealed that madeley embodies a fight against circumstances that applies to more than just the disability community. May casting directors take notice of the limitless potential she offers as part of any type of ensemble.

According to recent reports, as the President and CEO of Laika Studios, Knight has spent over 20 years educating audiences on the artform of stop-motion animation. And still, in his latest film “Wildwood,” a fantasy epic taking place in the forests outside Portland, Oregon, Knight directs scenes that seem inexplicable. It is hard enough to animate one bird flying, using that technique, yet the Fathom Entertainment release sees whole flocks fly off toward a war between species. The film’s commentary on parents and children is as heartrending as the craft behind how the film was made is genuinely inspiring to filmmakers of all types.

In a recent development, talk about legacy. Decades after his father, noted documentarian William Greaves, hosted a party for the surviving members of the Harlem Renaissance, “Once Upon a Time in Harlem” co-directed finished the film, one of the gems of Sundance 2026. To listen to Black luminaries from the ‘20s speak about how their work has endured into the ‘70s, with the dramatic irony of watching the film through a modern lens, is a singular cinematic experience. In a year where there is so much conversation around what pushes the documentary artform forward, the Neon release delivers both necessary context and innovation.

There is humor in having puppetry, one of the world’s oldest artforms, at the center of a conversation around innovation, but come on. Ortiz’s performance as Rocky in “Project Hail Mary,” supported by the work of visual effects team leaders Scanlan, Lambert, and Sarnowska, made us fall in love with a spidery alien rock that has no mouth or face. Puppetry’s forebearers would have still found that to be an insurmountable challenge. Hence, why the artist behind the fan favorite character opposite Ryan Gosling in the Amazon MGM Studios blockbuster deserves their flowers for helping viewers go beyond their earthly imaginations.

Though the latest film from director David Fincher and screenwriter Quentin Tarantino furthers the mis-adventures of Cliff Booth, the role that earned star Brad Pitt an Oscar, the Netflix film has an identity all its own. The work of costume designer Trish Summerville and actor Yahya Abdul-Mateen II are two elements that put that into focus, really easing the audience into the jump forward to 1977, where the silks flowed, and fur dripped off new screen icons akin to the latter’s Rodrick “Hot Rod” Harrison. This go-round allows viewers to have an appreciation for more than just Hollywood, but the greater Los Angeles area, and all the distinct styles it brought in that pivotal ‘70s moment.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A posh, Philippine country club’s colonial secrets are exposed in Rafael Manuel’s evocatively creepy, grimly funny, and austerely constructed social satire, “Filipiñana,” set outside Manila.

Writer/director Rafael Manuel’s film, which won a World Cinema special jury award at the 2026 Sundance Film Festival, also stands a chance at being his country’s first representative on a Best International Feature Film Oscar shortlist. While the Philippines was among the eight countries that submitted during the category’s inaugural year in 1956 (with Lamberto V. Avellana’s “Child of Sorrow”) along with France, Italy, and others, it’s never been nominated or shortlisted. Related Stories IndieWire Honors Film Celebration to Fête John Turturro, the ‘Artificial’ Cast, Los Javis, and More Cult Hit ‘Hundreds of Beavers’ Returns to Theaters for Substantial Christmas Expansion.

Executive-produced by Manuel’s former mentor Jia Zhangke, “Filipiñana” follows a tee girl who discovers something is off (and downright sinister) about the club’s administration, specifically president Dr. Palanca (Teroy Guzman). She’s played by Jorrybell Agoto, who, at just 32 years old, died earlier in November after a short battle with lymphoma.

Recent findings suggest that indieWire’s interview with filmmaker Rafael Manuel took place a week before the news, though he shared in a later statement, “The tragedy of this loss cannot be put into words. The world has just lost one of its brightest stars. We have just lost a great friend. But our thoughts and prayers go out especially to Jorybell’s family, who have just lost a loving ate [the Filipino word for older sister] and a devoted daughter.”.

An elegaic air, too, hangs over the film in retrospect and even before Agoto’s passing, as “Filipiñana” dwells in ghosts of the Philippines’ imperial past and Spanish occupation.

Sources indicate that “No one explains it to you beforehand,” director Manuel told IndieWire of touring with his first feature for nearly a year. (We spoke over Zoom while he smoked a cigarette in his Amsterdam apartment.) “What I’m starting to realize is the biggest difference between short and feature is that with short festival, it’s kind of the end goal. When you premiere at your festival, you’re so happy, and it’s done; it’s like people get to see it finally. But with a feature film, it’s just the beginning, and no one explained this to me.”.

Manuel joins the ranks of Lav Diaz, Brillante Mendoza, the late Lino Brocka, and many others to represent the Philippines at the Academy Awards — a concept, he remarked, that was never really on his radar.

“When we were coming up with this film and the genesis of the film, you don’t really think about an Oscars race,” noted Manuel. “You just think about making the best film you can. And especially coming from Southeast Asia, access to the American market, even getting a U.S. theatrical release, it’s not something that’s very common. Usually, your usual route is via the European arthouse market. So it’s been really surprising and in the best way possible, seeing how well received the film is in the States, in North America, and in the Anglo world in general.”.

The process was a “very challenging one,” he said, as the Philippines is taking the Oscar push very seriously from a governmental perspective. “And to be the first film that’s seriously backed by the government means a lot to us,” he said, especially for a film that’s critical of government and social hierarchy.

And there are hat tips not only to Jacques Tati, but also to Wes Anderson and Michael Haneke, at least in reviews, in terms of the movie’s flattened remove from violence and its dryly observational approach where everything in the frame is meticulously arranged.

In a recent development, “I get why people are saying Michael Haneke and Wes Anderson,” he said. “I mean, Jacques Tati, obviously, he’s a really substantial influence for me, but for example, with Haneke, I feel like we tackle violence very differently from how Haneke tackles violence. And I think with Wes Anderson, I see it because of the colors, because of the symmetrical framing and all of that, but I think this is very much a satire of that. And so, yes, we use a lot of Western codes and Western aesthetics in the film, but because it’s a film that deals with Western influence in the Orient, it was a film that deals with colonization. So the form and the aesthetic of the film is very much part of the satire. It’s the form.”.

He added, “It’s a polarizing film. I think it’s either you love it or you hate it, and I think that’s the same whether you’re in the West or in the Philippines.”.

The distribution of world cinema in the Philippines also helps to explain the divided palate for “Filipiñana,” as audiences have very little exposure to arthouse cinema from the outside world.

“In the Philippines, distribution of world cinema, it’s almost nonexistent. In Metro Manila, we have basically one or two arthouse cinemas, independent cinemas. The rest of the cinemas are all in shopping malls, and all they play are local rom-coms or Marvel movies,” he noted. But issues in the West of audience fatigue over shopworn, recycled I.P. and familiar material also apply in the Philippines.

Industry observers note that “It’s been a hot topic lately in the Philippines and consumers and audiences complaining about formulaic Filipino filmmaking. They’re tired of the formulaic rom-coms. But then the thing is that in the Philippines, I would say 90 percent of people have never seen a Lav Diaz film, even maybe 99 percent of people haven’t seen a Lav Diaz film,” Manuel stated of the slow cinema master behind last year’s submission, the Gael García Bernal-starring “Magellan,” which also dealt in the Philippines’ colonized history. (Diaz and Manuel share producers, including Bianca Balbuena and Bradley Liew, though they’ve never actually met.).

“Filipiñana” marks a break from tradition in terms of its Westernized style — and chatter has been flying on Letterboxd over the film since the Sundance premiere. (“I look through Letterboxd sometimes. Well, I used to, I stopped. And then the unhealthy thing with Letterboxd, for me especially, is that I’ll skip all the good comments and I’ll just read all the bad comments,” he said.).

Sources indicate that “When you’re faced with something different with arthouse cinema, like Filipino arthouse cinema, when Filipino audiences are faced with Filipino arthouse cinema, and you get some violent reactions, then it begs the question, ‘When you’re complaining about being tired of formulaic Filipino filmmaking, what exactly do you mean, and what exactly is it that you want?’ Do you just want Hollywood films but with brown faces in them? Because I don’t think that’s the answer either.”.

“Filipiñana” is now streaming on Kino Film Collection.

She is a historian by training and a bilingual reader, moving between English and Spanish literature. Beatriz began her career as a technology writer at a startup in the UK. Almost a decade later, journalism has taken her to five cities across three continents and into business reporting, cultural criticism, and live TV commentary. She joined Collider in 2026. Beatriz has a passion for travelling and loves keeping an eye on the books headed to the screen. One of her favorite pastimes is critiquing the historical accuracy of period movies. She also once volunteered for the Charles Dickens Museum. Beatriz also has a core belief that a book is always better than the movie, but she has been happy to have been proven wrong in a couple of occasions.

When she isn’t reading, Beatriz is watching musicals, stage managing Shakespeare plays with a local theater group or doing historical research. She enjoys tracing family trees for her history and genealogy TikTok, creating databases for historical analysis and sifting through 17th-century stories for the novel she is currently in the process of writing.

Agatha Christie did not write true crime. Instead, her talent was imagining complex and compelling puzzles surrounding a murder. Several of them were inspired by experiences from her own life, such as working as a nurse during WWI or traveling through the Middle East, accompanying her archeologist second husband to excavation sites. But not even the Queen of Crime could avoid the coverage of real crimes in newspapers and media. Although the stories and characters are always her own, some of Christie's most famous murder mysteries take inspiration from real-life cases.

It has been revealed that many real crimes and criminals are explicitly mentioned in Agatha Christie's novels and short stories. "Remember the long-continued successes of Jack the Ripper," Hercule Poirot tells Captain Arthur Hastings in the 1936 novel The ABC Murders. It is often believed the story of the Victorian serial killer inspired the plot of the book. Christie also held a deep fascination for the 1892 Lizzie Borden case, and the rhyme inspired by it is recited in After the Funeral. Other times, Christie did more than just borrow the general idea of a crime, and incorporated specific details related to a murder for her stories. Here are some of the most fascinating cases.

Recent findings suggest that in 1916, during World War I, Agatha Christie was working in a hospital dispensary and was bored. Christie decided to use this time to write a detective novel. "Since I was surrounded by poisons, perhaps it was natural that death by poisoning should be the method I selected," Christie herself wrote in her autobiography. Inspired by the detective book tradition, she created her own iconic investigator. He would be Belgian, like many of the refugees she was interacting with. His name would be Hercule Poirot.

The Mysterious Affair at Styles was inspired by not one but two real murder cases. The fictional death of wealthy Emily Inglethorp at her Essex country house, Styles Court, has many parallels to that of Frances Garnett Orme. The 49-year-old spiritualist was found dead from poison in her locked room in the Savoy Hotel in Mussoorie, India, in 1911. Orme's companion was the main suspect. The book also echoes the story of William Palmer, an English doctor convicted in 1856 of poisoning his friend, John Cook, with strychnine, the same poison Agatha Christie uses in the book. It was suspected that Palmer had also killed several members of his family, including four of his children. In addition to the murder method, Agatha Christie's novel also includes several key details from the Palmer case, such as coffee left in a hallway, an inquest at the village inn and a pharmacist who sold the poison thinking it would be used to kill a dog.

Billie Carleton was a British musical comedy actress in WWI London. By 18, she was a star. Four years later, and days after the end of the war, Carleton was found dead of an apparent drug overdose. The night before, she had attended the Victory Ball at the Royal Albert Hall dressed in a scandalous semi-transparent dress designed by her friend Reggie de Veulle. An investigation found De Veulle had provided Carleton with the substances and revealed he had been part of a secret underground London cocaine trafficking ring. He was sentenced to eight months in prison.

Agatha Christie's The Affair at the Victory Ball, one of the first Hercule Poirot short stories, takes readers to the inside of British high society. It is set during this luxurious celebration of the end of the war, which a group of people attended dressed in the costumes of the Italian commedia dell’arte. During the ball, Lord Cronshaw, dressed as Harlequin, is stabbed to death. The morning after the ball, his fiancée, actress Coco Courtnay, is found dead in her bed from a cocaine overdose. Christie never remarked the story was based on Billie Carleton’s death, but the details speak for themselves.

According to recent reports, on the evening of 31 January 1910, Cora Crippen, an extravagant music hall singer, disappeared from her London home. Her husband, the quiet American homeopath Hawley Harvey Crippen, claimed she had left him and moved to the U.S. Soon after, his mistress, Ethel Le Neve, moved into his house and began wearing Mrs Crippen's clothes and jewelry. When the case caught the police's attention, Dr. Crippen and Le Neve fled on a ship to Canada, with Le Neve disguised as a boy. However, the ship's captain recognized the pair and notified his superiors using wireless telegraphy. It was the first time this technology was used to track a criminal. In their absence, the police had searched the home and found human remains. Police officers then jumped onto a faster ship and chased the doctor and his mistress. They were arrested, and Dr. Crippen was found guilty of the murder. Le Neve was acquitted and later changed her name to distance herself from the case.

The story of the Crippen murder made international headlines, and even caught Agatha Christie's eye. She borrowed many details from the crime for her witty novel Mrs. McGinty's Dead, in which James Bentley is convicted of killing the elderly Mrs. McGinty. Hercule Poirot is asked to take on the case. The trail leads him to a newspaper clipping Mrs. McGinty kept that profiles women connected to notorious murder cases. One of them is Eva Kane, the mistress in the fictional "Craig case". Like Le Neve, Kane was found not guilty of the murder of her lover's wife. In the book, Kane changes her name and leaves the country. Her story is the key to the case.

It has been revealed that the Mousetrap still holds the record for the longest-running play in the world. The production, which first opened in 1952, is the same that can be seen today in London's West End. It is based on a radio play written by Agatha Christie as a birthday present for Queen Mary, titled Three Blind Mice. Christie then expanded the plot into a short story, but she requested that it not be published until the play had closed. Since The Mousetrap is still running, this has not happened yet in the UK, although the story has been published in the U.S.

In a recent development, both The Mousetrap and Three Blind Mice are based on the same case, the tragic death of 12-year-old Dennis O'Neill in 1945. Little Dennis and his younger brother, Terence (Terry) O'Neill, aged 9, were placed in foster care and sent to live with Reginald and Esther Gough on a remote English farm. Under their care, the children were beaten and barely fed. Less than a year later, Dennis died after being struck on the chest and beaten. The couple was charged with manslaughter and neglect in a grueling case made worse when young Terry was asked to act as a witness in the couple's trial. Terry's testimony angered the whole country and helped bring about the Children Act of 1948. The case became a clear inspiration for Agatha Christie's story, in which three fictional foster care children are sent to live in Longridge Farm, where one of them dies. Years later, one of their siblings takes revenge.

Industry observers note that toni Collette and Kit Harington are shooting a newly introduced Miss Marple and 20th Century has several more Christies in development, so the drawing room is busier than it has been in decades. Here is which of them you are, and the case for yours being the best.

Order, method, and a quiet confidence that you are the cleverest person present. Poirot is a retired Belgian police officer who solves murders by sitting still and thinking, and who is vain enough to make the reveal a performance every single time.

People tell you things because they cannot imagine you being a threat. Marple solves murders by comparing everybody to somebody she once knew in St Mary Mead, which sounds like a joke until you notice it works every time, because human beings are not as original as they think.

According to recent reports, you have far too many ideas and roughly a fifth of them are excellent. Ariadne Oliver is a successful crime novelist who is sick of her famous foreign detective and keeps saying so, which is Christie writing about Christie and getting away with it completely.

Recent findings suggest that you are steady, decent and the reason the difficult genius has anybody at all. Hastings narrates the early Poirot novels, misses most of the clues, and is the only character in the books that Poirot is unambiguously fond of, which tells you what he is really for.

The second Poirot story Agatha Christie wrote takes the detective to France. When he and Captain Hastings arrive, they are met with the news that the man they came to see, Paul Renauld, has died. His widow, Eloise Renauld, claims a group of masked men broke into her villa in the middle of the night, tied her up to the bed, and dragged her husband to the golf course, where they stabbed him to death. The investigation takes a turn when a second body is discovered, killed in a nearly identical way.

In a recent development, the setup of Murder on the Links follows that of one of France's most notorious murder trials. In May 1908, Marguerite Steinheil was found gagged and bound to a bed. Like Mrs. Renauld, Marguerite claimed she was attacked by intruders who killed her mother and husband, the painter Adolphe Steinheil. Marguerite was already infamous in Paris. Years before, she had been the mistress of French President Félix Faure, who had died in her arms after suffering a stroke. Marguerite tried to frame several people for the murder of her family members, but she was found out. It was widely believed that she herself had staged the intrusion to murder her husband. With no proof to back the accusation, a French jury acquitted Marguerite Stenheil in 1909 after an extremely sensationalistic trial.

Just as with a good murder-mystery, a list can take a turn. In this case, it is worth highlighting The Pale Horse as the only Agatha Christie book that inspired a crime, helped solve another, and saved several lives. In the novel, Mrs Davis gives her last confession to Father Gorman along with a list of names. Shortly after, the priest is murdered, and the people on the list begin dying from what seem to be natural causes.

At the heart of this book is a poison. It is made from an odorless heavy metal called thallium, which, if ingested in small doses, can cause symptoms such as hair loss and gastrointestinal distress that doctors routinely misdiagnose. The poison is said to have inspired Graham Young, known as "The Teacup Poisoner". In 1972, Young was accused of lacing his coworkers' tea and coffee with thallium and antimony, killing two colleagues. Some accounts say Young was caught thanks to a doctor who had read Agatha Christie's novel and became suspicious. Thallium was also the method used by George Trepal to poison his neighbors, the Carr family, killing Peggy Carr. An undercover detective who had been in Trepal's home recalled seeing a copy of The Pale Horse.

Recent findings suggest that agatha Christie's book also saved lives. In 1975, more than a decade after the novel was published, Christie received a letter from a reader in South America who had noticed a friend suffering from unexplained hair loss and pain. The reader remembered the plot of The Pale Horse and alerted the woman's physicians, who confirmed she had suffered thallium poisoning. Two years later, a one-year-old Qatari girl was flown to London. She was in a coma caused by an illness no doctors could diagnose. It was Marsha Maitland, a nurse in the hospital who had been reading The Pale Horse, who suggested thallium poisoning. The test came back positive, allowing doctors to find the treatment that saved the toddler's life.

It has been revealed that one child was kidnapped. Six people died as a direct consequence. This is the tragic arc at the heart of what is perhaps Agatha Christie's most famous novel, Murder on the Orient Express. In the book, Hercule Poirot is tasked with investigating the murder of American businessman Samuel Ratchett aboard the luxurious Orient Express. All the suspects in the murder are staying inside the same train, trapped in Yugoslavia in the middle of a snowstorm. Poirot soon finds that the murder is connected to an older tragedy: the kidnapping and murder of little Daisy Armstrong. The conclusion to the story is what makes it so compelling. It is tragic and simply brilliant.

It has been revealed that in the book, Agatha Christie aims to give a sense of justice to a real-life tragic crime. In 1932, 20-month-old Charles Lindbergh Jr, was taken from his crib in his New Jersey home. He was the son of the most famous aviator in the world, whose name he shared. The authors of the crime requested a $50,000 ransom. The parents paid. Soon after, the baby's body was found in the woods near the house. Weeks later, a young maid, Violet Sharpe, killed herself after being questioned by the police as a suspect. The crime was so famous it led to the passing of the Federal Kidnapping Act (the "Little Lindbergh Law"). Agatha Christie's fictional Armstrong case reproduces the Lindbergh case almost point for point. Except, of course, real crimes are rarely clear-cut. In 1934, a carpenter named Bruno Richard Hauptmann was arrested for the crime. Hauptmann was executed in 1936, although his guilt continues to be called into question even today.

Now, over six decades on from its inception, Star Trek has returned an iconic character as part of its 60th anniversary celebrations, and as of 24 November, you can hear all about Captain Janeway's perilous journey home in one brand-fresh release which will be a must-buy for the Star Trek fans in your life.

Despite the Star Wars universe being home to many iconic characters, there is no denying that Captain Kathryn Janeway is definitely one of them. Serving as the main character in the television series Star Trek: Voyager, she was the captain of the Starfleet starship USS Voyager and had to navigate the trials and tribulations of being lost in the Delta Quadrant on the other side of the galaxy. Portrayed by Kate Mulgrew, the actor has returned to bring life to the role once more in Star Trek Timelines, a fresh hardcover book from DK that features 336-pages of the entire fictional universe we have fallen in love with over the past 60 years.

Not only that, but Mulgrew has provided a foreword detailing how the franchise, and more specifically, Star Trek: Voyager, had an impact on her life, and it is lovely to see such an iconic actor and character being showcased during this celebratory time.

According to recent reports, star Trek Timelines retails at $60, so it is quite the investment, but readers will discover a recap of Star Trek's universe, including the various television highlights which have aired over the years, as well as all the other media it has popped up in. Not only that, but the book aims to share information on the Star Trek universe as a whole; all the way from the Major Bang that created the universe to the many significant moments that have made the fictional universe as successful as it is. As such, it will feature some of the most beloved entries, such as The Original Series, The Next Generation, Deep Space Nine, Voyager, and Enterprise, as well as more recent television shows like Discovery, Strange New Worlds, and Starfleet Academy.

With the Star Trek universe being set, well, across the universe, Star Trek Timelines has a lot to cover, but you will be pleased to hear that it will also delve into various alternate timelines, such as the iconic Mirror Universe, and even Voyager's unforgettable "Year of Hell" storyline that I am sure none of us have forgotten. With this being one of Captain Janeway's most memorable storylines, it was obvious that it needed to be included, especially with Mulgrew endorsing the book herself.

And then you have a rigger and a facial artist, all of these artists.”.

He went on to explain how that research process produced character-defining details that they would not have discovered any other way.

Sources indicate that netflix’s The Hunting Wives is one of the streamer's most addictive series: a soapy, raunchy romp that is delightfully unhinged from start to finish. Grounded in the sizzling chemistry between stars Malin Akerman and Brittany Snow, the show is steamy, sexy, and wildly entertaining, the sort of unashamed guilty pleasure TV that was made for the “just one more episode” binge model.

Industry observers note that based on the novel of the same name by bestselling author May Cobb, the series exploded in popularity following its debut last summer, racking up streaming minutes and TikTok edits while thrilling viewers with its nonstop plot twists. The story revolves around a group of wealthy Texas housewives who sport designer fashions and are all heavily armed. They’re at the center of everything in their small conservative town of Maple Brook, Texas, whether it's passing judgment from the pews at church, throwing back margaritas at a local honky tonk, or having ill-advised affairs.

These women are messy with a capital M, and that’s before they find themselves at the center of a murder investigation. Here's a quick recap of everything you need to remember about The Hunting Wives’ twisty first season before Season 2 premieres.

The series follows Tesla-driving, East Coast liberal transplant Sophie O’Neill (Snow), who moves to Maple Brook with her family for a fresh start after a devastating personal trauma. Her husband Graham (Evan Jonigkeit) lands a job with Jed Banks (Dermot Mulroney), a wealthy oil businessman who is being courted to run for governor. Sophie hits it off immediately with his wife, Margo (Akerman), bonding over prescription drugs and anxiety in a fundraiser bathroom.

Sources indicate that drawn into the lavish world of the Texas elite, Sophie rapidly learns that things are much more complicated (and salacious) than they initially appear. Margo’s essentially open marriage means that she’s not only sexually involved with her BFF Callie (Jaime Ray Newman), but she’s also secretly having an affair with her other BFF Jill’s (Katie Lowes) teenage son, Brad (George Ferrier). (Anything goes in Texas!) And when Brad’s high school girlfriend Abby (Madison Wolfe) turns up dead after a night of drinking and partying at Margo’s forest cabin — the same night Sophie’s gun goes missing — everyone’s a suspect, including Sophie herself.

Industry observers note that abby’s murder is the primary narrative drive of The Hunting Wives' first season, pushing Margo and Sophie closer together as they scramble to cover up their night of blackout-drunk escapades with a pair of high school boys. Along the way, the two ultimately give in to the attraction that’s been simmering between them since the series’ first episode and become intimate, not only sharing steamy hook-ups, but building a real emotional bond.

It has been revealed that unfortunately, all of that is shattered when Sophie realizes that Margo actually killed Abby. The teen found out that Margo not only had an affair with Brad, but had gotten pregnant and had an abortion. Abby's threats to expose Margo's secrets led to Margo shooting her with Sophie’s gun. Margo ultimately frames Brad’s mother, Jill, for the crime, leading to a standoff in the Thompson home that results in several other deaths, including Abby’s mother, Starr (Chrissy Metz), and Jill herself. (It is easier for the police to blame a dead woman, after all.).

In 1985 these four put their names on one record and called it Highwayman, and the title track went straight to number one on the country chart. Here is which of them you are, what it claims about you, and the case for yours being the best of the four.

Recent findings suggest that nothing gets to you and you have no prepares to stop. Willie left Nashville for Texas, made a sparse concept album the label thought was unfinished, and it turned out to be the record that proved the whole outlaw idea worked.

Sources indicate that you carry weight and people feel it when you walk in. Cash wore black on purpose, played prisons when nobody else would, and spent a career siding with whoever the room had decided to look down on.

Nobody tells you how to do your job. Waylon forced RCA to let him pick his own songs, his own band and his own producer, which simply was not done in Nashville, and every artist who came after him benefited from it.

In a recent development, you have had about four lives and you are not finished. Kristofferson was a Rhodes Scholar and an army helicopter pilot before he took a job sweeping floors at a Nashville studio so somebody might eventually read his songs.

Although Jill’s death — and the fact that the police now believe she's responsible for Abby's murder — results in Sophie being released from prison, it’s far from the end of her problems. Margo tells her volatile brother Kyle (Michael Aaron Milligan), who has a substance abuse problem and has frequent run-ins with the law, that her friend/ex/situationship knows the truth about what she did.

In a recent development, after a lifetime of playing the protective big brother, Kyle takes things into his own hands, running Sophie off a deserted road and trying to intimidate her. Terrified, Sophie runs Kyle over with her car before dragging his body to a nearby quarry to hide the evidence. In the season’s final moments, Sophie answers a call from Kyle’s phone — it’s Margo, asking if he “took care” of Sophie.

In a recent development, if The Hunting Wives’ first season is anything to go by, we can expect even bigger, wilder swings in Season 2. Both Margo and Sophie may technically still be free, but they also have literal bodies in their closets, and in a town as small as Maple Brook, it seems unlikely that those secrets will stay buried forever.

It’s also unlikely that the two women will stay at odds for too long. After all, their relationship is the emotional engine that propels the series, and things feel very unfinished between them. Sure, Sophie knows the truth about Abby Jackson’s death, but now that she’s a murderer herself, it’s basically impossible for her to go to the police. And while Margo’s presently in the dark about Kyle’s fate, even if/when she finds out, would she even be able to tell anyone, given Sophie’s knowledge of her own crimes? (We won’t talk about what’s going to happen when Margo realizes Kyle’s dead at her girlfriend’s hand, er, wheel...) But whatever happens, Season 2 is guaranteed to be a wild ride in more ways than one.

The Hunting Wives Season 2 premieres November 26 on Netflix.

It’ll offer two, larger display sizes: 6.4-inch and 7-inch. This largely comes from the bezel reduction.

I wish they prioritized the Telephoto camera more. I need that (whether it be on an Air or a Duo) way more than an Ultrawide.

If you’re holding out for iPhone 18 Pro, this “iPhone 20” is definitely the phone to wait out for.

Recent findings suggest that lastly, Apple will release a successor to its just-announced iPhone Duo next fall. Of course, you can expect next-generation Apple Silicon with the A21 Pro chip next year, but there aren’t many other substantial changes expected. Apple may bring proper Face ID to the outer display, an improvement from the recently-announced face unlock, but it’s unclear whether this feature will make the engineering cutoff date.

Tech Report: ‘All of a Sudden’: Why Does an 11-Minute Scene Centered on a Whiteboard Lecture Work So Well Onscreen?

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (981 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Indiewire

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, it is an unorthodox sequence.
  • Recent findings suggest that while a guest on this week’s Filmmaker Toolkit Podcast, Hamaguchi acknowledged the whiteboard is not what we generally consider to be cinematic, but then again neither is the three-hour-and-17-minute film about two women who form a powerful bond by talking about life, their life’s work, and the ever so sexy topic of eldercare for dementia patients.
  • And yet “All of a Sudden” blew away the world’s toughest critics at Cannes.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, it is an unorthodox sequence. In the middle of “All of a Sudden,” Mari (Tao Okamoto) pulls out a whiteboard and markers to diagram the principles of nature vs. capitalism for her new friend Marie-Lou (Virginie Efira). The scene lasts 11 minutes and digs into material you would expect in a university seminar, not the latest cinematic achievement from the Oscar-winning director of “Drive My Car,” Ryūsuke Hamaguchi.

Recent findings suggest that while a guest on this week’s Filmmaker Toolkit Podcast, Hamaguchi acknowledged the whiteboard is not what we generally consider to be cinematic, but then again neither is the three-hour-and-17-minute film about two women who form a powerful bond by talking about life, their life’s work, and the ever so sexy topic of eldercare for dementia patients. Related Stories Watch ‘The Sheep Detectives’ VFX Supervisor Break Down the ‘Sheep-Isms’ That Made His Characters Stand Out ‘Filipiñana’ Could Be the Philippines’ First-Ever Oscar-Shortlisted Feature — Even as the Film Was Dealt an Unexpected Tragedy.

And yet “All of a Sudden” blew away the world’s toughest critics at Cannes. Now, its distributor, Neon, heads into this weekend’s holiday theatrical release believing it has a legit shot at winning over the more commercially oriented Oscar voters — and becoming one of the (increasingly common) foreign-language Best Picture nominations. Neon similarly released “Sentimental Value” and “The Secret Agent” to Best Picture nominations the year before.

The whiteboard scene is not an extraneous aside, but a critical turning point in the women’s relationship. We asked the film’s writer/director why it not only works, but was deemed vital to the film.

“In trying to answer why this somehow works, I think there’s a few layers to it,” said Hamaguchi while on IndieWire’s Filmmaker Toolkit podcast. “And one maybe is because it really is something that is far removed from what is generally considered as cinematic. Perhaps because of that, it brings about a certain suspense, where you wonder, ‘OK, what is this for? What is this actually going to do?’ And there’s a certain sense of wondering that happens.”.

The scene comes a little over an hour into the film. Neither woman wants their magical evening to end. Mari follows Marie-Lou to her job as director of a nursing home, where she struggles to implement her passion project, “Huminitude,” a patient-centered care method based on touch and eye contact, which Mari sees in action. What prompts Mari’s whiteboard seminar is an attempt to help her newly introduced companion put into perspective the resistance she faces in implementing Huminitude and open the door to problem-solving.

In a recent development, “I think the second part [of why the scene works] really comes down to the efforts of the actors that are performing this scene,” noted Hamaguchi of Okamoto and Efira, who shared the Best Actress Prize at Cannes. “For Tao, I think it was an incredibly difficult scene to perform because first of all she really needed to understand all of the concepts that she was describing here and to really understand everything intellectually. And so in her preparation she did read a lot of the relevant books to really understand what she is talking about.”.

Industry observers note that hamaguchi believes the key to his dialogue-driven film is not necessarily how the words are spoken, but the performance of the listening and how the words are received. In Efira’s whiteboard scene, we see a shift from determined frustration to open enthusiasm that changes the direction of the film itself.

“The attitude of listening that Virginie portrays in this moment, I think, is very key and really supports this scene,” said Hamaguchi. “She’s not uninterested in what is going on, but in fact she feels that this is something that she should really be exploring together and she’s there and very much present. And I think this attitude of interest and curiosity really starts to work on the audience as well. And so in that sense I think ultimately this scene really works because of the actors’ performances.”.

Recent findings suggest that one topic that comes up in most post-screening Q&As is that both actresses were not working in the native language. Hamaguchi himself had to work with an interpreter to direct his leads. This is not the first time Hamaguchi has worked this way. On the podcast, he said that, in his experience directing the play inside “Drive My Car,” the language barrier was less of a hindrance and could even aid actors in listening to one another, as shown in the whiteboard scene.

“I felt that, in fact, this kind of difficulty that exists can in fact provide an environment for even more heightened concentration than you might have if you were speaking the same language,” said Hamaguchi. “ I think that actually when you can actually hear a lot and get a lot of information from somebody’s voice, you can, in fact, precisely feel just how concentrated the person is when they’re saying something by listening to their voice.”.

Asked if any of his collaborators or producers ever questioned the whiteboard scene after reading the script, Hamaguchi stated no, and speculated why: “Because it’s so unusual, I think people understood that this is something that I really wanted to do.”.

“There were some questions around, ‘This section feels a little long. Is there anything we can do about that?’” recalled Hamaguchi, adding that he made a concerted effort to cut his four-hour script to a three-hour, 16-minute running time.

“For me, I was ultimately trying to bring in the shortest version that I felt was accurate for this moment. But ultimately, there is this understanding that this moment is a very important turning point within the film, and so I believe that the producers also understood this.”.

“All of a Sudden” is now playing in select theaters.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that most people are probably waiting until Jan. 1 to start getting in shape, whether they want to start fresh or absolve themselves of their perceived holiday indulgences. Every year, people start the latest year by joining a gym crowded with others newly resolved to get in shape, paying full price for the privilege of waiting in a long line to use the squat rack. This year, try something different: Start your gym membership during Black Friday.

According to recent reports, the week of Black Friday can deliver you a good discount on a gym membership, an empty gym, and a built-in two-month runway to turn a generic resolution into a real habit. While you're comparing deals on upcoming tech, headphones, or smart home devices, here’s why you should also take a few minutes to scout out the gyms near you.

This week is as good a time to save of a gym membership as a fresh air fryer. Here are just a few examples of the offers out there right now:.

Orangetheory and F45 have various free-month and prize-entry promotions for upcoming Black Friday sign-ups, and similar studios for Pilates, yoga, and strength training have discounted multi-month and annual packages.

Independent gyms, university rec centers, and local studios often run their own versions, from a free month tacked onto a longer commitment to waived joining fees.

Sources indicate that deals vary a lot by location, so call or stop by the clubs near you and ask what's available. Then remember to always read the fine print before you sign:.

Look at the price after the promotion ends, not just the first month's rate.

Ask about fees, including joining, annual, and access fees.

Try before you buy. Many gyms offer a free trial pass. It might make sense to first visit at the time of day you'd actually go.

Recent findings suggest that be honest about distance. The best gym is the one you'll actually walk into, so pick one that's close to home or work.

In a recent development, gyms also run sales around New Year's, so a good Black Friday offer isn't the only deal you'll see. Even still, the savings aren't the only reason to go now.

December is reliably the quietest stretch of the gym year: People are busy with holiday travel and work deadlines, and many tell themselves they'll "start fresh in January." That means open benches, free treadmills, and staff who have time to show you how a machine works.

That's a gift for any gym-goer, but especially if you're fresh. Learning your way around a gym is much less intimidating when it's empty. You can figure out the equipment, make your mistakes in peace, and build a routine before the January crowds arrive. Plus, this time of year is a perfect window to set and achieve a winnable goal.

From Black Friday to Newly introduced Year's Day is about five weeks. By the time the January rush hits its peak and settles into its usual patterns, you could be eight weeks into a new routine. And as my colleague Beth Skwarecki explains, you really can get a lot stronger in 24 workouts. Beginners tend to see the fastest gains of their lifting lives in the first couple of months.

Sources indicate that prefer running? I know I do, and luckily, a couch-to-5K initiative works the same way. Most programs run about nine weeks and build you up gradually from short run-walk intervals. Start the week after Black Friday and you'll be running for a solid stretch by early January, and you'll be well on your way to 30 minutes at a stretch by the end of the month. By the time your New Year's resolution friends are just starting, you'll already be a few runs in.

According to recent reports, this is also the season when many workplaces and health plans wrap up their open enrollment periods, which makes it a smart time to check what wellness perks you already have. Before you pay full price for anything, look into:.

Workplace wellness programs, which sometimes offer gym reimbursements, discounted memberships or fitness stipends.

Health insurance perks, since some plans include gym memberships or discounts.

Recent findings suggest that HSA and FSA rules, where general gym memberships usually don't qualify, but some medically recommended programs may. Also check any year-end deadlines for money you'd otherwise lose.

Corporate and employer discounts, which many large gyms offer on top of regular promotions.

Stack a workplace benefit on top of a holiday sale, and your cost per workout can drop considerably—well before New Year's resolution time arrives.

According to recent reports, netflix's 6-part political conspiracy thriller delivers a masterclass in psychological suspense, with gripping twists, dangerous secrets, and deep themes of betrayal. Starring Richard Madden of Game of Thrones fame, this Netflix limited series is one of the easiest demonstrates on the platform to start and finish in just one weekend, sporting a total runtime of roughly 6 hours and 7 minutes across six masterfully crafted episodes. The series is a phenomenal showcase of building tension from its very first episode, led by a morally conflicted protagonist.

Bodyguard remains one of Netflix's best political thriller miniseries of all time, delivering relentless psychological suspense across a tight 6-part story that is full of well-executed plot twists. The 2-time Emmy-nominated series earned a 93% Rotten Tomatoes score and is still an elite quick binge option 8 years after its premiere, featuring outstanding performances, dazzling action sequences, and fantastic character development. Bodyguard follows a war veteran and police officer named David Budd (Madden) who is assigned to protect a controversial yet high-ranking government official he disagrees with politically.

Bodyguard begins with a compelling high-stakes situation, forcing David to respond to a potentially catastrophic situation after he suspects a suicide bomber on a train heading for London. Aboard the train with his children, David must rely on his quick thinking and his advanced training methods to neutralize the threat, all while protecting his family at the same time. All this happens within the first 20 or so minutes of Bodyguard, setting up the rest of the unfolding action that includes even more threats of violence against the politician David is assigned to protect, Julia Montague, played by Keeley Hawes.

Before David and Julia ever meet in the series, Julia already has a target on her back for signing a upcoming bill into law that increases the government's ability to monitor digital communications between citizens, which is met with public outrage. This establishes the narrative engine that sustains the tension built within the first episode throughout the 6-part series, with the threat of retaliation and violence present at any given moment. Beyond the physical threats, David is diagnosed with PTSD, which greatly influences his behavior and ability to make decisions. This, along with his differing political views from Julia, creates psychological suspense beneath the surface-level violence.

Sources indicate that david's complicated psychological profile and complex history with trauma make him a fascinating protagonist in Bodyguard, as he can often be quite unpredictable for someone who is entrusted to protect the life of a high-ranking political figure. That said, plot developments after the first few episodes of Bodyguard would be confusing for any character, as larger conspiracies begin to reveal themselves and it becomes increasingly difficult for David to determine who he can trust. Because of these unique psychological elements, Bodyguard elevates itself beyond a standard political conspiracy thriller on Netflix, allowing it to exist in an elite category of its own.

Sources indicate that madden delivers one of his career best roles as David Budd, bringing all the complexities of the David Budd character to life in convincing and compelling ways. Most critics highlight Madden's performance as the greatest part of the 6-part Netflix series and one of the key reasons why it's so binge-worthy from start to finish. Variety writes of Bodyguard, "Both juicy in its delving into character psychology and rippingly ready to tear up its playbook as it goes, it's a six-episode ride that demands, and rewards, a quick binge.".

It has been revealed that netflix has a great new slate of streaming releases that are worth checking out this holiday weekend, including Black Doves season 2, The Hunting Wives season 2, and The Trials of Karen Read. However, if you're looking for a phenomenally suspenseful show that's guaranteed not to disappoint, Bodyguard is about as good as it gets as far as 6-part political thrillers go on Netflix.

Ferrell co-created the series in which he plays a former top golfer who is now trying to return to the tour. And while it figured to be a tentpole series for Netflix, one that carried possibly the most expensive budget for a comedy series on Netflix and reunited Ferrell with his “SNL” co-star Molly Shannon and co-creator Harper Steele, it didn’t connect with critics or audiences.

“The Hawk” spent just three weeks on Netflix’s Top 10 when it debuted back in July, topping out at #2 in its second week on Netflix with just 6.2 million views. Ferrell’s vulgar, loudly-dressed golfer with a personalized visor and significant mess of bleached blonde hair played a lot like some of Ferrell’s other string of sports comedies throughout the years. But even our critic was perplexed by the series’ tone that makes it sometimes play like a “bizarre addiction drama.” Related Stories Where Are Rick Dalton and Sharon Tate in ‘The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth’? ‘The Mosquito Bowl’ Review: ‘Friday Night Lights’ Meets ‘Five Came Back’ in Peter Berg’s Formulaic Netflix Movie About a World War II Football Game.

Steele, in a recent appearance on “Late Night with Seth Meyers,” tipped her hand a little that the show was likely ending when she let slip that, “I was working on a short-lived but probably the best show ever, ‘The Hawk.’”.

Industry observers note that the cancellation comes in the wake of a changing of the guard at Netflix, with Peter Rice taking over for veteran creative chief Bela Bajaria. Our critic also recently wrote about the challenges Netflix is facing right now in getting audiences to discover fresh series in the ways they used to.

But at the same time, Netflix has already renewed a couple of other comedy series that even premiered after “The Hawk” later this year, including “Nobody Wants This,” “A Different World,” “Tires,” “Significant Mistakes,” and “The Four Seasons.” Netflix is also still working with Ferrell’s Gloria Sanchez Productions on three new series, “All the Rage,” “Prep,” and another scripted series from Nikki Glaser.
