📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that with three Emmy wins for his role as Jesse Pinkman, Aaron Paul confirmed his pop culture icon status by starring in Breaking Bad. Even though Vince Gilligan initially intended to kill Jesse off, Paul’s inherent likability created the glue that held the AMC drama together. The actor earned his accolades as the traumatized meth cook who was just another victim of Walter White’s (Bryan Cranston). As iconic and dark as the role was, however, Paul followed up Breaking Bad with something even more harrowing.

Sources indicate that after the conclusion of Breaking Bad, Paul starred in the Hulu series The Path. The show was set in an entirely different world than his previous one, but no less serious. Paul portrayed the role of Eddie Lane, an acolyte of the fictional Meyerist movement. The Path views this movement non-judgmentally, as the series is portrayed from the perspective of those in the cult. At its core, Meyerism is a self-help philosophy that draws on many real-life cults. Paul’s character is a heavily indoctrinated believer, along with his wife, Sarah (Michelle Monaghan), who grew up in the movement.

Sources indicate that only after going to a retreat does Eddie question his faith in Meyerism. As a convert, Eddie’s relationship with the so-called movement is shaken, but Sarah is much more stringent in her beliefs. This conflict leads to a dark character arc for Eddie, which rivals his role in Breaking Bad. A decade after its 2016 premiere, the 36-episode drama remains one of Paul’s more overlooked television performances.

Cults have been a source of fascination for a long time, but viewers won’t catch the actors saying such a thing about Meyerism. Michelle Monaghan, Aaron Paul, and Hugh Dancy, who plays a ranking official, Cal, were so immersed in the series' culture that they were reluctant to label the movement a cult.

Sources indicate that “I could never call it a cult,” Dancy told E! News. “We are a movement. I think that’s relevant and that’s, in a way, the core of the show.” The far more interesting way to portray the series is to create it from the perspective of its acolytes and how insidious this type of thinking is. As Dancy says, no one in a cult thinks that they’re in a cult.

These ideas are prominent in many real-life movements, whether they are legally acknowledged as a cult or just a church. Regardless, Paul’s role in the series gets so close to reality that it can sometimes be uncomfortable. While on ayahuasca, Eddie receives a vision that leads him to believe there is no “Light,” a core tenet of Meyerism. His doubts lead to friction in the movement and eventually separation.

Industry observers note that called “deniers” in The Path, people who separate from these types of churches or movements are shunned by the community and often separated from their families. The Path shows what happens behind closed doors and the violence used as punishment. Ambition is also at the center of Meyerism as Cal becomes adversarial with Eddie. Cal is poised to become the next leader of Meyerism and has always been in love with Sarah. Considering Eddie’s controversial views, he is an easy target for Cal.

In a recent development, the Path is mostly disturbing because it shows the ramifications of boutique beliefs such as these. Though there are characters who want to dismantle such a system, Eddie goes through a harrowing character arc that doesn’t tie everything up in a bow. At least Jesse escapes his torment in a powerful Breaking Bad performance. The Path is even more morally ambiguous and questions everything the viewers have seen.

In a recent development, all 36 episodes across three seasons of The Path remain available to stream on Hulu in the U.S. as of November 2026.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Industry observers note that earlier this month, IndieWire surveyed the programming at independent movie theaters across the United States on Election Night.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

One of the great things about going to the movies by yourself is that, technically speaking, you’re not alone. Even if you’re the only person in the auditorium, somebody thought about what you might like to watch, put it on the calendar, and made sure there was a place for you to sit.

That’s something worth being grateful for this Thanksgiving.

Industry observers note that earlier this month, IndieWire surveyed the programming at independent movie theaters across the United States on Election Night. Continuing that exercise over Thanksgiving weekend reveals another delightful cross-section of American film culture — albeit with considerably more cannibalism. Related Stories ‘All of a Sudden’: Why Does an 11-Minute Scene Centered on a Whiteboard Lecture Work So Well Onscreen? Watch ‘The Sheep Detectives’ VFX Supervisor Break Down the ‘Sheep-Isms’ That Made His Characters Stand Out.

At the Music Box Theatre in Chicago, where audiences have spent more than two decades celebrating Thanksgiving by singing along to “The Sound of Music,” moviegoers can also catch Ruggero Deodato’s “Cannibal Holocaust” late Friday night. It’s hard to imagine the Von Trapps sticking around for that one, but there’s something lovely about a neighborhood institution accommodating both crowds.

Industry observers note that in Seattle, the Beacon is observing its own Thanksgiving tradition with “Blood Rage,” the gloriously ridiculous slasher that made cranberry sauce an enduring point of reference for a certain subset of horror fans. For a somewhat more realistic depiction of the horrors of going home for Thanksgiving, SALA Event Center in Los Alamos, Latest Mexico, is showing Jodie Foster’s “Home for the Holidays.”.

According to recent reports, in Cambridge, Massachusetts, the Brattle Theatre is celebrating Black Friday with a double feature of “Chopping Mall” and “Night of the Comet.” If you’d rather watch people die in a shopping mall than go to one yourself, that’s certainly an economical alternative. Meanwhile, Minneapolis’ Trylon Cinema is spending the biggest shopping weekend of the year celebrating the work of documentary filmmaker Barbara Kopple, screening her Oscar-winning “Harlan County, U.S.A.” and “American Dream” as part of a series dedicated to class struggle.

In a recent development, thanksgiving also marks the 50th anniversary of the Band’s legendary farewell concert, held at San Francisco’s Winterland Ballroom in 1976. At Film Streams in Omaha, Nebraska, audiences can spend Friday morning watching Martin Scorsese’s “The Last Waltz.” That half a century later, people are still getting together to experience a concert most of them weren’t alive to attend speaks to one of the more miraculous things movies can do.

And in Portland, Oregon, stop-motion animation studio LAIKA is expressing its gratitude to its hometown audience by offering free screenings of “Wildwood“ on Sunday at theaters across the area, including the historic Hollywood Theatre. Considering how many thousands of hours of human labor go into making a stop-motion animated feature, there’s something especially sweet about giving people whose real home served as the setting a chance to enjoy the outcome together.

Of course, what Americans celebrate on Thanksgiving — and whether they celebrate it at all — varies considerably. On Wednesday, California Indian Nations College is presenting a free screening of “People of the West,” a documentary series examining the history of California’s Indigenous peoples from Indigenous perspectives, in Palm Desert. At the historic Raymond Theatre in Raymond, Washington, a free Saturday screening of a documentary about the Qwayat Canoe Society’s journey to Nisqually offers an opportunity to learn more about a living Indigenous tradition.

Recent findings suggest that and for anyone navigating a particularly painful holiday season, a film festival in Magnolia, Texas, is making a different kind of space. Presented by the nonprofit My Grief Angels, Grief Fest is hosting an in-person community screening on Black Friday, with films also available to watch virtually throughout Thanksgiving weekend. Dedicated to exploring loss and healing through cinema, the festival recognizes just how complicated an invitation to celebrate can be.

Recent findings suggest that there are innumerable ways to spend a long weekend like this, and movies aren’t a substitute for the people we wish we could spend it with. But the wonderful thing about indie exhibition is just how much of it depends on random people thinking about other random people. Someone has to remember that a certain movie exists. Then someone else has to think it might mean something to you. And finally a different person has to care enough to bring it all together.

Industry observers note that whether you’re somebody who spends every Thanksgiving with the same people or a cinephile whose traditions are still taking shape, consider making a little time for your local movie theater this weekend. Thank the person who takes your ticket, and tell the programmer when you love something they booked. Maybe even invite that friend you’ve been meaning to catch up with.

It has been revealed that there are so many extraordinary works of art to see in this lifetime and never quite enough time to see them all. How lucky we are to get to watch some of them together.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Despite welcoming many reimaginings since it first premiered in 1978, Battlestar Galactica fans have been waiting a while to see what is next from the beloved sci-fi franchise.

Recent findings suggest that after all, it was in 2010 that the prequel series, Caprica, premiered, and before that, the series that ran from 2004 to 2009 gave us a reimagining of the original television show. However, with a legion of fans still dedicated to the story which takes us to a group of planets known as the Twelve Colonies as we follow the exploits of the survivors who engage in an ongoing war with the Cylons, 2027 is the year when it is set to make a major return.

In a recent development, unfortunately, back in 2024, Peacock broke fan's hearts when it announced that it would be scrapping its planned Battlestar Galactica reboot. Despite being in development for five years and announced back in 2019, the project, created by Mr. Robot's Sam Esmail, was rumored to follow the same vein as the 2004 reboot, but was reportedly canceled due to high production costs, creative friction, and a tighter streaming market.

However, it is not all bad news as Battlestar Galactica is expected to return in the new year thanks to one of the franchise's most beloved entries.

This is all courtesy of Battlestar Galactica: The Board Game as it is set to make an official comeback after almost two decades. Earlier this year, Ghost Galaxy revealed a new licensing agreement with Universal and Fantasy Flight Games and, as such, an updated edition of the beloved tabletop classic will begin a crowdfunding campaign in early 2027.

According to recent reports, for those who missed out on its original iteration, Battlestar Galactica: The Board Game first introduced in 2008 courtesy of Fantasy Flight Games. Created by Corey Konieczka, it swiftly became one of the most successful hidden-traitor games on the market, which makes it all the more exciting that it is set to return, and with a modern twist.

The original game is based on the 2004 reboot and will allow players to head to the Galactica in an attempt to secure humanity's dwindling resources, all whilst surviving Cylon attacks and various events which could see your ship damaged, or even destroyed. However, what made Battlestar Galactica: The Board Game all the more exciting is that it allowed some players to secretly be Cylons with the aim of sabotaging the other players.

The board game experience was so successful that it welcomed multiple expansions, including Pegasus, Exodus, and Daybreak, and even though it eventually stopped being created, secondhand copies of Battlestar Galactica: The Board Game soon became highly sought-after collectibles.

According to recent reports, whilst we do not yet know the specifics of the upcoming crowdfunding campaign, we do know that the updated Battlestar Galactica: The Board Game will feature an updated design, but what this will look like remains to be seen. Nevertheless, if you were a fan of the original experience, or just so happen to be a Battlestar Galactica fan who is eager for a return to the sci-fi world, make sure to keep up-to-date with this exciting fresh project.

12 Things to Do on Christmas If You Don’t Celebrate

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1037 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that in a way, the Christmas season is more fun if you don’t celebrate it.
  • According to recent reports, you can’t go wrong with some moo shu pork and a trip to the multiplex.
  • If Chinese food isn’t your thing, look at restaurants serving any non-European cuisine—Greek places, Japanese places, and Mediterranean places are usually open, as are plenty of Italian restaurants and steakhouses.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that in a way, the Christmas season is more fun if you don’t celebrate it. You get to enjoy all the brightly colored lights your neighbors put up, but you don’t have to put up your own. You don’t have to do any duty-shopping. There's no pressure. But Christmas Day itself leaves you in a mostly shuttered world that feels like there’s nothing going on. Fortunately, there are options to make Dec. 25 a fun day off, regardless of your observances.

According to recent reports, you can’t go wrong with some moo shu pork and a trip to the multiplex. Chinese restaurants and movie theaters traditionally stay open on Christmas Day for those who don't celebrate, and they’re often filled with fellow Christmas refugees. Check Google for the hours of your local Chinese restaurant and give them a call to make a reservation. If you’re more adventurous and you’re in a city large enough to have a Chinatown (or a whatever-town), just head straight there on Christmas and see what happens—that’s how the best days usually start.

If Chinese food isn’t your thing, look at restaurants serving any non-European cuisine—Greek places, Japanese places, and Mediterranean places are usually open, as are plenty of Italian restaurants and steakhouses. Just make sure you check first. Lots of chain restaurants are open on Christmas Day too, including Applebee's, McDonald’s, Benihana, and more. You can even get Christmas breakfast at your local IHOP. But not every location of every outlet follows the same hours.

Recent findings suggest that as for movies, most chain multiplex theaters are open on Dec. 25, and theaters are usually pretty full. The movies attract both people who don't celebrate Christmas and people who do, but want to get away from their families for a couple hours, so make sure and reserve a seat beforehand. Consider hitting up an out-of-the-way spot or that theater with the table service and cushy recliners to make it feel like more of an occasion.

In a recent development, most people going to the movies on Christmas Day aren’t there for Christmas movies, so interesting “secular” movies are often slated for release on the 25th. This year's Christmas is unusually packed with interesting fresh movies, including family flick Jumani: Open World, a Robert Eggers horror movie called Werwulf, and the crowd pleasing football story Mr. Irrelevant, so you have serious options.

Chinese restaurants and movie theaters aren’t the only establishments open on Christmas. Here are some other options:.

Go skiing or snowboarding: Most mountains are open on Christmas, and the lift lines are blissfully empty. There's no better way of celebrating a winter-based holiday than on a wide-open mountain.

Visit a skating rink: Speaking of winter sports, ice skating rinks are generally open on Christmas too.

Pretend to be a tourist: Tourist attractions are often open on Christmas, especially in larger cities. This includes places like Madame Tussaud’s and Ripley’s Believe It or Not, as well as ziplines and Segway tours—so do that touristy thing you’ve never done before.

Get a room: If you’ve got some spare cash and have nothing better to do, get a room at a hotel. Hotels don’t usually close on Christmas, and they typically offer plenty of amenities, so take advantage of the pool at the Holiday Inn or the spa at the Four Seasons, depending on your lifestyle.

Hiking and biking: Hiking trails and parks are open on Christmas if you want to get outdoors. If you’re into biking, hit the trails or hit the streets: Traffic is minimal on Christmas, so it’s a great time to put in some serious roadwork.

Volunteer: Not having anything to do on Christmas isn’t the biggest life problem, especially compared to people who have nowhere to go and nothing to eat. So use Christmas to help people and actually deliver on that whole “good will towards men” thing. Check your local Craigslist for volunteering opportunities.

Sources indicate that use Christmas as a catch-up day: This is strictly for type-A people, but if everyone is out of town and no one is going to call you, why not spend the day catching up on neglected chores or personal projects? You can spend at least part of your day knocking a few things off your to-do list and the rest of the time relaxing. That way you’ll get a break and still feel accomplished.

Just sleep all day: Type-B personalities like me see a day free of obligations and other people as a golden opportunity to do as little as is humanly possible, a day to fully commit to sloth.

It has been revealed that spend time with friends and family at home: Not celebrating Christmas doesn’t mean you can’t spend the day with family and/or friends. Get together with your loved ones, play games, watch a movie, cook together, talk, or whatever else you all enjoy. You don’t have to go out to have fun, so don’t rule out staying in with people you care about.

According to recent reports, shopping: This is at the bottom of the list because it’s iffy. Drug stores and convenience stores like 711 are usually open on the 25th. Grocery chains like Kroger’s and Trader Joe’s usually aren’t. Your local shopping mall or retail district might be open, but probably won't be, so check ahead.

Because so many places are closed on Christmas Day, you should proposal ahead (unless you like spontaneity and are OK with the possibility of disappointment) by:.

Making a list of the places you want to go.

Calling nearby locations to confirm they’ll be open, as not every chain follows corporate holiday hour recommendations.

Making reservations at any restaurant(s) you plan to visit.

Putting together a basic timeline of the day, accounting for travel time, so you don’t lose any reservations, miss a movie, or arrive after the store closes.

Sources indicate that the most vital advice here is to do something intentional on Christmas, even if it's sleeping in, so the day doesn't feel depressing or empty. So hit the slopes, suck down some dim sum, or keep your couch from floating away, but be sure you make Christmas your own.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Hannah covers horror, sci-fi, and games at Collider, where she writes news and features, reviews upcoming releases, and interviews the people who make them. She’s helping build out Collider’s gaming coverage, with Pokémon as one of her specialties. If she isn’t writing about a monster, she’s probably watching one on a tape from her VHS collection.

It has been revealed that of all the things Sophie O’Neil (Brittany Snow) could have packed for her first night out in East Texas, the one that might have spared her a great deal of trouble was a sanitary pad. When a stranger asks her for one in the bathroom at an NRA fundraiser, Sophie offers a tampon, the stranger declines, and the two discover something they can agree on in Sophie’s purse. By the time they’ve each taken a Xanax, Sophie has made her first friend in Maple Brook. She’s also about to discover that the woman who just got half undressed in front of her is the wife of her husband’s boss.

Sources indicate that there are any number of places The Hunting Wives could have introduced Margo Banks (Malin Åkerman), including the stage where she joins her oil tycoon husband, Jed (Dermot Mulroney), as he floats the idea of running for governor. Having Sophie meet her in the bathroom first is considerably more fun. Everybody else at the party sees a prospective first lady of Texas. Sophie gets to spend the rest of the evening looking at that woman and thinking about what the two of them just did. Anybody who spent eight seasons of Desperate Housewives waiting for organization to arrive at Bree Van de Kamp’s house at the worst possible moment should feel right at home. Adapted by Rebecca Cutter from May Cobb’s novel, The Hunting Wives has an eight-episode first season on Netflix and a second arriving on Thanksgiving Day, November 26. That gives you a perfectly respectable excuse to spend the long weekend with the Banks family, provided you’re prepared to explain what’s happening on the television when a relative wanders in.

According to recent reports, john Dutton would understand Jed Banks just fine. One man made his name in Montana cattle country and the other made his in Texas oil, but both have spent enough time being the most crucial man in the room to figure they might as well be governor. What gives The Hunting Wives its own angle on familiar Yellowstone territory is where it sends Sophie once Jed finishes talking. Margo wants to know what she thought of his speech. Imagine being upcoming in town, having exactly one professional connection through your husband, and discovering that his boss’s wife would like a little constructive criticism.

It has been revealed that A look around Margo’s friend group explains how much is riding on her liking the answer. Callie (Jaime Ray Newman) is married to the sheriff. Jill (Katie Lowes) is the pastor’s wife, and her son Brad (George Ferrier) is the local basketball star. Between them, these women have Sunday morning, Friday night, and any trouble you might get into in between pretty well covered. Most jealous friends have to settle for scrolling back to the beginning of your Instagram. When Callie catches on to Margo’s interest in Sophie, she has the resources of the sheriff’s office at her disposal.

Jill, meanwhile, can be perfectly sweet to Brad’s girlfriend, Abby (Madison Wolfe), while making it clear she thinks her son could do better. Lowes gets at something wonderfully aggravating about a mother who has promoted herself to the third person in a teenage relationship. You can imagine how Jill would describe the encounter to Brad afterward, and how ridiculous Abby would sound trying to explain what his mother did wrong. That’s where the Wisteria Lane resemblance runs deepest. Half the pleasure of watching these women misbehave comes from knowing whose side the neighbors would take if anybody complained.

Sources indicate that snow is funny in the early going because Sophie seems to share the audience’s judgment about everything happening around her, right up until Margo asks if she’d like to come along. There’s a lovely bit of cowardice in how long Sophie can pass off her interest as good manners. Going to the fundraiser was Graham’s idea, after all. Dinner with the Bankses could conceivably fall under the heading of supporting her husband’s career. Buying a pistol and leaving it at Margo’s place because Graham wouldn’t approve takes a little more explaining.

Åkerman makes Margo’s attention feel as good as Sophie thinks it does, even when we have an excellent view of the woman who was getting that attention yesterday. Early on, Margo offers Sophie a ride home from a bar, leaving a visibly disappointed Callie behind. You could spend the whole ride anticipating what might happen between the two women in the car, or you could spend it dying to get back to the bar to hear what Callie has to say. Even the woman who didn’t get invited along has a scene you want to see.

There is, of course, a murder to solve. The Hunting Wives opens with a girl running for her life before taking us back three weeks, and what makes those eight episodes go down so easily is how often you can forget about the shooting altogether. Jed and Margo have Sophie and Graham over for dinner, the hosts have rather different ideas about what’s on offer than their guests do, and suddenly the most pressing question in East Texas is how on earth these people are going to face each other at work on Monday.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

“I’m not one of those people that try to act like I don’t want the thing. I want the thing. I’m excited about the thing,” said recent Academy Award nominee Danielle Brooks. “I know how much it has impacted little Dani when I’ve watched Oprah Winfrey or Whoopi Goldberg or Viola Davis or Halle Berry receive [Oscars], and listened even to the speeches now, [from Emmy winners] Niecy Nash-Betts and Sheryl Lee Ralph. They push you to continue to work hard.”.

In a recent development, though her 2023 role in “The Color Purple” cemented the Grammy winner’s status as a performer who has at the very least been nominated for each letter of EGOT, the real reward the recognition among her peers has brought is the opportunity to executive produce and star in projects like the Walter Thompson-Hernandez film “If I Go Will They Miss Me,” which premiered at Sundance 2026 to rave reviews. “Yes, I have the desire to be receiving awards one day,” said Brooks, “but at the end of the day, I get to do that with my work. I get to do that with stories like ‘If I Go,’ where my goal is for people to feel seen.” Related Stories What Are Local Movie Theaters Showing for Thanksgiving 2026? ‘All of a Sudden’: Why Does an 11-Minute Scene Centered on a Whiteboard Lecture Work So Well Onscreen?

The coming-of-age drama set in Watts, California sees the actress play a mother named Lozita doing her best to hold her family together while there’s inscrutable tension between her partner, recently released from prison, and their imaginative 12-year-old son. “I started out in theater, so to me, it’s never been about a paycheck,” joked Brooks. “It’s always been about the story and what you’re putting out into the world. And so, when I watched [Thompson-Hernandez’s] short, I was like, ‘Yo, this is different. I ain’t never seen nothing like this.’ And it was captivating just the way he was shooting it.”.

Expanding on what drew her to the project, which came to her during her time bouncing between Los Angeles awards press for “The Color Purple,” and the Fresh Zealand set of “A Minecraft Movie,” Brooks said “They handed me the script and it was really the conversation, sitting down with Walter, his passion for his community, hearing about the real Lozita who had unfortunately passed away from cancer two years prior, hearing about the Compton Cowboys, just getting to talk to him about relationships between kids and their parents and the complications that it can bring.”.

According to recent reports, she stated, “I like the balance. I got to have a little comedy, but I got to do some drama and it does my heart well.” While “Minecraft” brought her “laughs all day with Jack Black and Jason Momoa,” “If I Go” brought Brooks “purpose.” “I’m excited that we get to share stories like this where people are really dealing with their personal complications and healing and all of that stuff,” she said.

Having screened the film in Los Angeles the night before, Brooks remarked “You can feel the energy of everyone feeling super represented and feeling a sense of ownership. It’s cool hearing the audience be like, ‘Yeah, yeah,’ When you talk about the planes passing by, or the story about the fuel engines falling on elementary schools. People remember and know that to be a part of what has happened in LA, and the fabric of LA.”.

According to recent reports, one job that was foundational to how she approaches projects like “If I Go” happens to be Brooks’ breakout role as Taystee on “Orange Is the Fresh Black.” Coming out of the prestigious Julliard School, her mind was more so on “how am I going to make my money for the subway and pay for my college tuition and how am I going to pay for this PB&J sandwich?,” when she booked the role on the series for the then-nascent streaming service Netflix. “I didn’t know what I was stepping into at the time. ‘Orange’ was looked at as a webseries, so nobody knew what this was about to be. But once we got into the work, I was like, ‘Oh, this is deeper than that.’ I remember talking to people who’ve been incarcerated, and I remember even doing a clothing drive for women who have just come out of prison so that they could have clothes for job interviews and stuff like that. We were really invested in the community and giving back,” said Brooks.

Recent findings suggest that “We had that as a group, as storytellers, but then individually, I was watching my co-stars have a point of view, have something to say. And so, I [was] just learning that being an artist is also a form of activism,” she said. “That was one of the beginning seeds planted in my head once I was in the industry, because I’ve always known that what we do is about service, that’s number one. But I hadn’t experienced that on this level.”.

Since then, Brooks’ goal has been to tell at least one story a year that incorporates a bit of activism, and with “If I Go,” the actress and producer has been more active than ever. “I’ve deemed us the little engine that could, because I really believe that we can take this far. My goal is that we just get as many eyeballs on it as we can. But the truth of the matter is nothing moves like money does. And that’s what I’ve learned is you’ve got to get really creative and strategic about how you can push a movie into the face of the people when you don’t have the money.”.

According to recent reports, “If I Go Will They Miss Me,” distributed by Rich Spirit, has truly been an indie success story, making over $1 million at the box office from the humblest of beginnings. As Brooks noted, that haul has been hard fought, with her, Thompson-Hernandez, and her co-star J. Alphonse Nicholson touring as much of the country as they can to screen the film, and even abroad. “I’m going to Africa this week, I got invited, but then I learned there’s a film festival in Africa. So, I’m like, ‘Can we take the film to Africa?’ And they remarked, ‘Yes.’ So now, the film’s going to be in the festival there,” said the actress.

According to recent reports, she continued, “It’s even in the form of fashion. People pay attention to what you’re wearing and then they’re like, ‘Why you got that on? Oh! She had a premiere.’ Boom. It’s insane how many tricks I have been working to get people to pay attention to this film that is worth paying attention to.”.

One of the more beautiful aspects of this “If I Go” experience has been the way in which her community has shown up for her and the film. Snoop Dogg and Ava DuVernay have Instagrammed about it, while Helen Hunt and André Holland have even hosted talk backs for the film. But in terms of creativity, one marketing strategy takes the cake. “Issa Rae, even at her restaurant, she did a menu dedicated to ‘If I Go’ where it was a discount, 15 percent off or something if you bought a ticket,” she said. “People understand the importance of this,” said Brooks. “If the film wasn’t good, I wouldn’t be doing all this.”.

On the awards front, the challenge is still getting the film in front of the steak eaters who still make up a good chunk of the awards body, and maybe do not immediately think they identify with the material. “The Academy is working really hard to change that narrative by who is allowed to vote. The voting party is shifting, but that’s what I’m experiencing right now,” said Brooks.

According to recent reports, but regular filmgoers have a role in getting smaller, truly independent films awards recognition too. “The general audience plays a huge part because the culture tells the voters where to look, what is vital,” said the actress. “The people, we have a voice in this too. I think we make it very clear what we want to see, but it’s a weird cycle.” Studio films have a budget for billboards, commercials, advertisements, and more. “When you are a small independent film, you have to be that substantial machine on your own to get it out there. And that’s a lot of work, and that’s a lot of time, and that’s a lot of smarts,” said Brooks. “You’ve got to have a lot of faith and hope too. You’ve just got to believe that what you’ve created is strong. And I do know that we all do, myself, J. Alphonse, Walter, MACRO, Rich Spirit, we believe in this film wholeheartedly.”.

“Movies like these are worth telling, and I think they do reach who they need to reach, and they do lock in with the world on a larger scale when they’re supposed to,” stated Brooks, reflecting on the fruitful journey “If I Go” has already had so far. “This is the thing I’m most proud of in my whole career because just the fact that people are having conversations, hard conversations with their loved ones, and they’re finding ways to heal.”.

“If I Go Will They Miss Me” is now available to rent on all platforms.

Industry observers note that prime Video's new 8-part sci-fi thriller delivers a masterclass in cyberpunk worldbuilding, bringing an iconic, breathtaking dystopian future to life. Released in full on Wednesday, November 25, this brand new series is one of the best new binges on Prime Video this weekend and is expected to be one of the most-watched indicates across all streaming platforms in the coming days. With its striking visual style and rich production design based on a brilliant sci-fi franchise, there is no better new series to watch right now with remarkable worldbuilding.

Blade Runner 2099 just arrived with all 8 episodes on Prime Video this Wednesday, November 25. While early reviews are mostly, but not unanimously, positive, earning a Rotten Tomatoes score of 68%, the series' greatest achievement is its rich setting that evolves the original dystopian cyberpunk feel and lore from the original Blade Runner film. Set 50 years after the events of Blade Runner 2049, which is widely considered one of the top sci-fi sequels ever made, Blade Runner 2099 delivers a masterclass in expanding a beloved classic story world.

Sources indicate that while both Blade Runner and Blade Runner 2049 established a legendary dystopian world that presents a not-so-distant Los Angeles full of tall skyscrapers, neon lights, and a perpetually unsettling atmosphere, Blade Runner 2099 takes these elements one step further by placing the megacity under Replicant control. After humankind lost a major war to the Replicants, the city's framework and power dynamics have fundamentally changed, adding a fascinating newly introduced thematic layer to the already ominous dystopian landscape. This also takes the initial cyberpunk design of the franchise's LA setting one step further, leaning more heavily into urban decay contrasted by advanced tech.

It has been revealed that with Replicants in control of Los Angeles in Blade Runner 2099, humans have devolved into being second-class citizens, and the distinct visual style of LA has also undergone massive changes to align with this extreme power shift. Unlike the Blade Runner films, 2099 features a new signature aesthetic, replacing the dark and rainy weather system with oppressive light and heat, which completely alters the visual identity of the franchise. The 50-year time jump between 2049 and 2099 also introduces new societal customs and technological abilities that demonstrate the Replicants' rise to power, adding even more worldbuilding elements to an already well-established sci-fi universe.

Apart from the Replicants taking over Los Angeles in Prime Video's new Blade Runner series, the most revolutionary change in 2099 is how the series views oppression, power, and justice, which builds on the franchise's legacy of dystopian storytelling. Rather than having humans continue to determine the quality of life over Replicants, the Replicants now wield the authority to categorize humans, which is a direct reversal of the pre-existing core theme in the previous two Blade Runner installments.

2099 could have easily maintained this essential factor in the upcoming Prime Video series, but flipping its core moral question on its head is a testament to the franchise's willingness to broaden its own horizons while still holding firmly to its dystopian roots. Hunter Schafer's Cora, a human protagonist and fugitive, experiences similar forms of oppression and social discrimination that Replicants had suffered for multiple decades, while Michelle Yeoh's Replicant character, Olwen, confronts her own conflict with mortality and her life's value as an AI entity.

Although not all critics have praised Blade Runner 2099 as a whole, most contend that the worldbuilding and franchise expansion are some of its strongest and most appealing qualities. IndieWire writes, "Blade Runner 2099 may not be as exquisite as its predecessors (and it won’t likely win over audiences who aren’t already fans), but it nails the franchise’s aura — and builds one awesome world." Additionally, Empire Magazine notes, "It may sometimes lose narrative momentum but this is world-building par excellence, high on atmosphere, spectacle and food for thought." Ultimately, Blade Runner 2099 may be flawed, but it's a masterclass in crafting an immersive sci-fi world.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Industry observers note that if you just want to sit back and relax as your character drives around Leonida in GTA 6, you should try the auto-drive mode.
  • Your character is going to commit a lot of crimes in GTA 6.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, you can have a ton of fun in GTA 6 even if you only follow the core gameplay loop of running around, stealing cars, and completing missions and side quests. However, if you take a minute to learn a few hidden controls, I think you'll enjoy the game even more. These are fairly simple controls that let you hide from the cops, trash talk other drivers, or flip the bird when you're feeling like annoying NPCs. These are 10 of the best hidden GTA 6 controls that'll help you unlock an entirely new side of the game.

Industry observers note that if you just want to sit back and relax as your character drives around Leonida in GTA 6, you should try the auto-drive mode. It's a relaxing way to enjoy the streets without having to worry about following traffic rules. To enable it, you need to get in a vehicle and add a waypoint on the map. This serves as your character's destination, so if you want a longer drive, be sure to drop the waypoint far, far away. Next, hold the down arrow on the D-Pad, and press the Option button. This enables cinematic mode. Then, hold the Circle button to enable auto-drive.

Your character is going to commit a lot of crimes in GTA 6. When this happens, you attract heat, and soon enough, cops will begin chasing you. Switching cars is a great way to reduce the amount of attention you get from law enforcement, but you can still be identified by your face or clothing. Until you can reach a safe spot to swap outfits, maintain a low profile by ducking while driving. Hold the Circle button while driving to duck.

It has been revealed that EA's Road Rash was among the first racing games I played as a child, and I remember how much fun it was to kick your rivals while speeding through the game's various courses. You can have a taste of that in GTA 6 too. Press the Square button while you're riding a bike, and your character will kick anyone who's near you. If you do this in a car, it opens the door, and hits people around the car. To annoy other drivers, press R3, and your character will direct some trash talk towards NPCs.

Hold Circle to lean back against walls, or to sit on the beach. To rest on a ledge, you can hold L3. This lets you take a moment to soak in beautiful views in the game, or lounge around as you listen to NPC conversations. Paying attention to those conversations can lead to some fun side quests, and sometimes give you a tip or two for quick money or other rewards.

If you really want to rile people up in GTA 6, you can flip the bird. This works only when your character is unarmed. Hold L2, focus on a person, then press R1. Actions have consequences in GTA 6, so be prepared to fight NPCs when you do this.

It has been revealed that when you're being chased by cops, enemies, or angry NPCs, you can use a quick shortcut to look back without turning the camera around. Just hold R3 to look behind you.

According to recent reports, while driving, press Circle to toggle headlights (and switch to high beams). This is particularly useful when you're offroading at night. You can also hold left arrow on the D-Pad, and move the right stick up to access other vehicle controls like hazard lights, opening or closing windows, etc., in case you want to add to the realism.

Stealing emergency vehicles in GTA 6 is risky, but the reward is totally worth it. Not only do you find stashes of weapons, gear, and money in some of these vehicles, but you also have access to sirens that help you clear traffic off your path. If you steal an ambulance or a cop car, hold L3, and move the left stick up to go through different siren tones. Press L3 and the left stick up to enable the siren.

GTA 6 is a third-person game, but it has a first-person mode that partially works. It is useful for looking at smaller objects around your character, such as posters, small signs, or to look for clues in and around a house. (Yes, I am talking about Mandy's creepy house and bad vibes.) Hold L2 + hit R3 to switch to first-person mode. Sadly, you can't move when you do this, but you can look around. Try it in Mandy's property to observe a few nasty surprises.

When you sprint towards a car, press the X button to slide across the hood. This is much faster and smoother than running around parked cars or jumping over them. It also looks cool, which is reason enough to try this feature.

#120036. 9 Books From the 2010s That Are Officially Classics Today

9 Books From the 2010s That Are Officially Classics Today

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1697 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Collider

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It's a text that has stood the test of time for at least a few years and has proven to be substantially influential and widely celebrated over time.
  • In a recent development, of course, artistic appreciation is and always will be an almost entirely subjective matter, but looking back at the biggest classics from the 2010s, it's almost undeniable that they still hold the elements that make up a classic book: historical relevance, cultural impact, and artistic merit without equal.
  • According to recent reports, no conversation about 2010s literature could possibly be complete without getting into non-fiction, which was absolutely massive (both commercially and culturally) throughout the whole decade.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

What makes a book a classic? It's a text that has stood the test of time for at least a few years and has proven to be substantially influential and widely celebrated over time. It's a text that attained cultural and artistic relevance and maintains it as the years pass; it's historically relevant, universally significant, and worthy of being counted among history's "greats." Thankfully for those who love modern literature, there are a handful of 2010s books that are officially classics today.

In a recent development, of course, artistic appreciation is and always will be an almost entirely subjective matter, but looking back at the biggest classics from the 2010s, it's almost undeniable that they still hold the elements that make up a classic book: historical relevance, cultural impact, and artistic merit without equal. From non-fiction masterpieces like The Warmth of Other Suns to speculative fiction cornerstones like The Way of Kings, these are books that definitely live up to the hype.

According to recent reports, no conversation about 2010s literature could possibly be complete without getting into non-fiction, which was absolutely massive (both commercially and culturally) throughout the whole decade. The biggest masterpiece that the genre produced was Isabel Wilkerson's The Warmth of Other Suns, which traces the decades-long Great Migration of nearly six million Black Americans fleeing the Jim Crow South for Northern and Western cities between the 1910s and 1970s.

It has been revealed that it took Wilkerson 15 years of extensive research to complete The Warmth of Other Suns, and the result ended up being one of the best American book masterpieces of the 21st century. It's a towering work of non-fiction art that reads like a sweeping novel, anchoring its research in the deeply personal biographies of three real individuals. It was modern classics like this that sparked the non-fiction boom of the 2010s.

According to recent reports, before it became one of the best Irish TV series of the 21st century, Normal People was a romance drama novel by Sally Rooney. A massive bestseller and winner of several awards, it's one of the most perfectly written books of the 21st century, about two young Irish teenagers from vastly different social backgrounds who navigate an intense, on-and-off romantic bond from high school through university.

The coming-of-age genre produced several great romance novels over the course of the 2010s, but it's hard to point to one that had more of a substantial pop-cultural impact than Rooney's sophomore novel. Normal People captures the emotional, social, and economic anxieties of the millennial generation through a story of such profound thematic and emotional power that just about anyone should be able to appreciate it, no matter their age.

According to recent reports, in Madeline Miller's Circe, an overlooked nymph banished to a remote island masters witchcraft and carves out her own destiny amid gods and mortal heroes. It's an unforgettable retelling of the story of one of Greek mythology's most iconic characters (mostly framed as a reimagining of Homer's Odyssey), and it's absolutely worth reading even for people who don't typically have much interest in mythology-inspired fantasy books.

The 2010s gave us several fantasy books that are perfect masterpieces, but few quite as exceptional or popular as Circe. Miller took a character that had long been seen as a villainous seductress and flipped the narrative altogether, exploring Circe's interiority in a way far too complex to catalog the book as one of those typical "misunderstood villain" narratives that plagued the 2010s. The prose is beautiful, the character writing is powerful, and the book was so popular that it sparked a whole new wave of feminist mythological retellings.

According to recent reports, far and away one of the best books of the 2010s, the Nigerian novel Americanah came as part of a major boom in popularity and cultural relevance that African literature saw throughout the 2010s. It follows two young Nigerian lovers, whose paths diverge across the United States and the United Kingdom as they're forced to navigate race, class, and cultural identity abroad before they can reunite in a changed Nigeria.

Books about the immigrant and diasporic experiences became far more prevalent and popular during the 2010s, and few masterpieces demonstrate the quality of such writing better than Americanah. Written with a perfect balance between razor-sharp wit and sweeping narrative scope, it's a brilliant redefinition of traditional immigrant stories and one of the most sincere love stories that 2010s literature ever told. If there's any African novel that's today an official classic, it's surely this one.

According to recent reports, the subgenres of high, epic, and heroic fantasy have also delivered many an incredible masterpiece throughout the 21st century so far, and the 2010s were certainly no exception. The decade saw the bulk of the output of Brandon Sanderson, who has quickly become one of the most prolific speculative fiction authors at the moment working. Case in point: The Way of Kings, about a brutal war of vengeance on a storm-ravaged world where ancient magic is fading.

Recent findings suggest that far and away one of Sanderson's best books, this first chapter in The Stormlight Archive is arguably also the author's novel that is most worthy of being considered a modern classic. Tremendously vast in scope, ambitious in plotting and worldbuilding, and emotionally resonant in its psychologically profound character work, The Stormlight Archive is undeniable evidence of the unmatched power of epic high fantasy.

Industry observers note that four worlds and four completely different ideas of what a good life looks like. This is where you belong, what it would ask of you, and what you would get back in return.

It has been revealed that you belong somewhere old enough that the mountains have names and somebody can still tell you who gave them. Middle-earth is for people who think the right thing is worth doing even when it will not be finished in their lifetime.

You want the sea, a crew, and absolutely nobody telling you where you are allowed to go. The Grand Line is the world for people whose main ambition in life is finding out what is over there.

It has been revealed that you would rather be feared and useful than liked and useless. The Continent is a world where the monsters are the straightforward part of the job and the people are where it all gets complicated.

You want the myths to be real and loose in the actual world, and you want to find out at about thirteen that you were never anywhere near as ordinary as everybody kept telling you.

Further proof of how ingrained in the mainstream books about marginalized experiences became throughout the 2010s is the success of author and journalist Min Jin Lee's epic historical fiction novel Pachinko, which just so happens to be one of many great books recommended by Barack Obama. In it, a young Korean woman pregnant by a married man marries a gentle minister and moves to Japan, sparking a four-generation saga of survival and resilience.

Sources indicate that before Pachinko, few readers outside East Asia knew about the Zainichi, ethnic Koreans living in Japan during and after Japanese colonial rule who were subjected to systemic discrimination for generations. But far from just serving as a learning experience, reading Pachinko is also a journey elevated by the incredible moral complexity and psychological depth with which Min Jin Lee writes.

Back in 1992, Donna Tartt wrote The Secret History, easily one of the best and most impactful debut novels of the '90s. The reception for her second novel, 2002's The Little Friend, was significantly more mixed. Nine years later came her third novel, the Pulitzer-winning The Goldfinch, and it may just be Tartt's magnum opus. In it, a teenage boy steals a priceless painting as he navigates the grief of surviving a terrorist bombing that killed his mother.

Sources indicate that it's one of the best books published since 2010, an absolute masterclass in modern Dickensian storytelling that, at nearly 800 pages in length, somehow manages to not have a single page of fluff or wasted space. Combining energetic thriller plotting with profound meditations on loss, obsession, and the redemptive power of art, Tartt delivered one of the defining masterpieces of 21st-century English-language literature.

N. K. Jemisin's Broken Earth trilogy made history by becoming the first book trilogy ever to have each installment win the Hugo Award for Best Novel in consecutive years. But as great as books two and three are, this is one of those book series that peaked with their first entry: The Fifth Season, a science fantasy masterpiece about a mother journeying across an apocalyptic supercontinent to rescue her kidnapped daughter as the world tears itself apart around her.

In a recent development, speculative fiction delivered so many of the 2010s' greatest masterpieces that it deserves immense amounts of credit, and there is arguably no speculative fiction book from the decade more fit to be called a modern classic than The Fifth Season. Boldly experimental and daring in its structure and creative elements (including some chapters written in the second person), it's a visceral allegory of oppression that has somehow only gotten timelier and more potent with age.

Upon publication in 2012, Gillian Flynn's Gone Girl revolutionized modern thriller writing, reshaping both publishing trends and narrative tropes across the domestic thriller subgenre in particular. In it, after Nick Dunne's wife vanishes on their fifth wedding anniversary, mounting evidence and a media circus turn him into the primary suspect in the investigation. The narrative that comes from such a premise makes for the single biggest, most official modern classic of the 2010s.

Recent findings suggest that one of those mystery books that are a masterclass in prose, Gone Girl is not only an enrapturing thriller baked into layers upon layers of suspense and subtext, but also an intelligent dissection of modern marriage and media sensationalism. It's cool, tense, timely, subversive, and it pushed a latest wave of domestic noir fiction whose influence can still be felt to this day. If there's any modern classic from the 2010s that's an absolute must-read, it's this one.

AI May Be Scanning Your Private Signal Chats

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • If you use Signal, it's likely you care at least a little bit about keeping your communication private so only you and those you're chatting with can see your message threads.
  • It has been revealed that in a recent blog post, Signal president Meredith Whitaker outlined the potential threat AI assistants like Siri and Gemini pose to the platform's promise of privacy.
  • It has been revealed that signal has already blocked screenshot capabilities for Microsoft's Recall AI, which by default was able to take and store screen grabs of Signal messages on Windows 11.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

If you use Signal, it's likely you care at least a little bit about keeping your communication private so only you and those you're chatting with can see your message threads. Signal's end-to-end encryption keeps prying eyes out, but if you use agentic AI on your device, your chats may not be as locked down as you think.

It has been revealed that in a recent blog post, Signal president Meredith Whitaker outlined the potential threat AI assistants like Siri and Gemini pose to the platform's promise of privacy. Systems-level capabilities like Gemini Intelligence (on Android) and Siri AI's Onscreen Awareness (on iOS and macOS) scan your screen and may be able to capture data from Signal conversations in the process, which can then be used to perform tasks. Not only does this potentially expose your information, but that of other conversation participants as well. Whitaker notes that this leaves privacy protections outside of Signal's control because the platform cannot easily restrict AI access to the app.

It has been revealed that signal has already blocked screenshot capabilities for Microsoft's Recall AI, which by default was able to take and store screen grabs of Signal messages on Windows 11. While Signal cannot guarantee that AI won't have access to your data, there are a few protections now available for those on iOS and Android as well.

According to recent reports, the main workaround in Signal for now is to restrict screenshots and screen recordings inside the app, though this does not prevent AI agents from potentially grabbing content from other parts of your device. According to Signal's support documents, these protections will now be enabled by default on iOS 27 and Android with the latest versions of the Signal app.

Users on iOS 27 can confirm or manually disable screenshot protection via Settings > Privacy > Block Siri AI. The compromise with this setting is that it also blocks you from taking screenshots of Signal conversations in the app and App Switcher, though you can disable it temporarily for 10 minutes if needed. On Android, Signal automatically engages the "Screen security" setting when it detects an AI agent attempting to access the screen. This, too, blocks screenshots inside the app and can be disabled via Settings > Privacy > App security > Screen security. Signal cannot block screenshots on macOS 27. However, users can add Signal to their Excluded Apps list via System Settings > Siri, which at least limits proactive access to conversations by Siri AI.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Five major tech outages in quick succession earlier this month led to speculation that they were connected, with some inevitably believing them to be AI-related.
  • That wasn’t the case, but the US Director of National Intelligence is one of a number of experts warning that we should expect AI-powered outages in the near future ….
  • In a recent development, earlier this month saw five tech outages, one after the other.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Five major tech outages in quick succession earlier this month led to speculation that they were connected, with some inevitably believing them to be AI-related.

That wasn’t the case, but the US Director of National Intelligence is one of a number of experts warning that we should expect AI-powered outages in the near future ….

In a recent development, earlier this month saw five tech outages, one after the other. A widespread Microsoft 365 outage occurred when two unrelated challenges coincided. The next day saw a nationwide ground stop of US air traffic due to a communication problem affecting all air traffic control centers. A few days later, a bug in a Chase bank system saw disruption not only to the bank itself, but also other banks where Chase was a party to a transaction. Many Apple services went offline later the same week, with retail stores also affected. Finally, United Airlines had its own widespread IT outage that grounded a significant number of flights.

Each had their own unrelated causes, with the White House stating that rumors of an AI-facilitated systemic attack by a hostile state were false.

In a recent development, however, Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton has warned that we should expect future tech outages as a result of attacks facilitated by AI-discovered vulnerabilities. CNBC reports him issuing the warning on CNN’s State of the Union.

The American people should be prepared for a great deal of investment in upgrading our systems; they should be prepared for investment in cybersecurity, and they should be prepared that any time there is a step change in technology, a step change in both compute and applications, there will be bumps in the road.

You prepare by knowing that systems are going to be upgraded; they may be interrupted for a period of time and that companies and government are dealing with this on the front foot.

We already saw an example of this last month when a vulnerability discovered in PHP saw a significant number of websites being taken offline.

Microsoft President Brad Smith says it isn’t just a question of bad actors exploiting vulnerabilities discovered by AI, but companies rushing to patch these may inadvertently cause systems to fail, as Newsweek reports.

What AI did earlier this year was basically make it much easier for people to find vulnerabilities in code, and then you can either use that knowledge to patch the code, or if you’re a bad actor, you can use that knowledge to try to hack into systems.

Especially when you have older infrastructure, especially when you’re trying to patch at such a pace, especially when you have to go so fast that you can’t take as much time to test what you’re changing in the code, you do increase the risk of something going wrong.

Major IT failures look set to be a routine event in the coming weeks and months.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that all five episodes of Steven Spielberg's Apple TV sci-fi series are a testament to how not to reboot a franchise after it's lain dormant for 35 years.
  • But he's also had a hand in plenty of other projects, too, particularly when it comes to serving as an executive producer for sci-fi found on TV.
  • That show is Amazing Stories, a fantasy sci-fi anthology series that was originally released from 1985 to 1987.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that all five episodes of Steven Spielberg's Apple TV sci-fi series are a testament to how not to reboot a franchise after it's lain dormant for 35 years. Spielberg is best known for his movies, the filmmaker being a powerhouse of cinema whose decades of work have defined movies in both the 20th and 21st centuries. From the heartfelt, sci-fi story of E.T. the Extra-Terrrestrial to the tense yet thematically potent tale of Jurassic Park, Spielberg has made his mark on movies, especially in the sci-fi genre.

But he's also had a hand in plenty of other projects, too, particularly when it comes to serving as an executive producer for sci-fi found on TV. The underwater sci-fi show SeaQuest DSV is one such example, taking place in an aquatic, sea-focused future. Some more contemporary works of his include the alien invasion-focused Falling Skies, alongside the TV adaptation for Stephen King's Under the Dome. His sci-fi TV series have become integral parts of media history. One such series that he helped create and reboot is no exception.

That show is Amazing Stories, a fantasy sci-fi anthology series that was originally released from 1985 to 1987. Across the series' 45-episode run, each upcoming installment would feature a story combining elements of fantasy or horror, crafting a tale much in the same vein as The Twilight Zone in terms of presentation and content. Spielberg created and executive produced the show, while directing some episodes. although the original series ended in the '80s, the show had a short-lived, five-episode run on Apple TV in 2020 — which didn't go according to strategy.

Apple TV's reboot of Amazing Stories saw Spielberg back as an executive producer for the show, which lasted five episodes of roughly an hour each, as opposed to the half-hour runtimes of the original series' episodes. Each episode focused on a different sci-fi adventure, not necessarily in the vein of horror. This includes an episode starring the late Robert Forster in his final onscreen role, a posthumous release after his death in 2019. However, despite the admirable attempt, the show didn't stick the same landing as its predecessor.

Recent findings suggest that according to reviews for Amazing Stories, the 2020 rendition of the show scored a 41% on Rotten Tomatoes from 34 critics. Audiences didn't fare much better, dropping it a 52% based on over 100 ratings. According to critics, the show doesn't feel like it evolved for modern times, offering a strong attempt at bringing the series to a modern audience that doesn't stick the landing. In particular, there was criticism toward the show's lack of originality, alongside messy writing that causes some stories to feel nonsensical.

What makes the Amazing Stories reboot all the more disappointing is that Jordan Peele's attempt at remaking The Twilight Zone served as a much better reinvention of episodic sci-fi anthology series. While the reboot wasn't perfect, it took risks in modernizing the series that eventually aided in it being a more memorable experience. This included both remixes of classic episodes from the original, alongside fully original terrors that would only work in the present day. Nostalgia wasn't the only factor, with the series also utilizing originality.

It has been revealed that the overarching attempt The Twilight Zone made with its continuation far outshone that of Amazing Stories, which goes to show how the Apple TV series unfortunately fumbled what could have been a memorable modern comeback. While some episodes stand on their own, such as Forster's, it's ultimately nothing like the classic that Spielberg created back in the '80s. It proves that, despite an attempt, the show just couldn't make its way to the modern age.

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Lifehacker ↗ Open Full Page

Two Budget Smartwatches That Make Perfect Gifts

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1461 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, if you or someone on your shopping list wants a new smartwatch, you have plenty of options to choose from.
  • There are two smartwatches on the market that aren't just cheaper than the competition, they're not even in the same ballpark.
  • Contrary to what you might expect, Amazfit has no ties to Amazon—other than that you can buy these watches from the latter.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, if you or someone on your shopping list wants a new smartwatch, you have plenty of options to choose from. The problem is, a lot of them can be quite pricey. Apple's cheapest smartwatch, the SE 3, starts at $249, and its other selections only skyrocket from there. On the flip side, the risk in picking a smartwatch that's too inexpensive is that the manufacturer likely made a series of sacrifices to get the price that low. At a certain point, the tradeoff just isn't worth it.

Luckily, you do have options. There are two smartwatches on the market that aren't just cheaper than the competition, they're not even in the same ballpark. And while you shouldn't expect the same capabilities as you would on flagship wearables, these devices are perfectly usable, both as fitness trackers and smartwatches—all while spending well below $100 a pop. CNET put both smartwatches through their paces to make these determinations, so you know whichever model you get, you won't be picking up a wearable paperweight.

Contrary to what you might expect, Amazfit has no ties to Amazon—other than that you can buy these watches from the latter. Amazfit is its own company, and produces a wide selection of smartwatch options. The Bip 6 happens to be the company's latest budget smartwatch, with an MSRP of just $79.99. In most cases, a price that low would be a red flag for a smartwatch, but not in the Bip 6's case.

Recent findings suggest that the Amazfit Bip 6 holds its own against other flagship smartwatches. That's true on a surface level: This watch looks your average smartwatch, rather than a cheap imitation. In fact, at first glance, I'd bet most people would assume the Bip 6 is actually an Apple Watch. It has a rounded square design with a large 1.97-inch display with a resolution of 390 by 450 pixels (though there's no Always-On display). This isn't a cheap display, either: Amazfit put an AMOLED screen on the watch, which looks great indoors—though CNET Labs struggled to see the screen in direct sunlight.

Where the Bip 6 really shines, however, is with fitness tracking. This watch supports GPS, which makes tracking outdoor runs possible without a smartphone. CNET Labs found that it takes about 10 seconds to find a GPS signal, but once it connects, you're set. While running, the Bip 6 reliably tracks your heart rate. CNET Labs compared its sensor to the Polar chest strap HR monitor and found it on par, though, like other smartwatches, the Bip 6 is slower at detecting heart rate spikes. You'll get data like cadence and stride while tracking runs, and strength training and muscle groups while working out indoors. For example, CNET Labs found that it correctly identified arm muscle exercises while testing the watch during a pilates session.

You also get some health and wellness features, too. The Bip 6 can measure heart rate variations, body temperature changes, sleep stages, and even your breathing quality. Its One Tap Measuring mode supports a single reading for heart rate, SpO2 (blood oxygen saturation), stress, and breathing rate, and it supports cycle tracking—though CNET specifies it can't track skin temperature like other smartwatches and health trackers. There's an optional subscription that provides AI coaching tools and looks out for health conditions like sleep apnea and insomnia. While health and wellness tracking is solid, note that CNET Labs found Amazfit's app, Zepp, to be confusing, since it simply displays your data without much context or explanation.

For an $80 smartwatch, the Bip 6 has an excellent battery life. CNET Labs found that the watch could be pushed to its limits—multiple workouts using GPS, heart rate tracking, keeping the display on during workouts—and still run for eight days before needing a charge. In fact, reviewer Vanessa Hand Orellana speculates you could push the Bip 6 to Amazfit's two-week battery life claim by limiting some of the most intensive settings and features. The only downside here is that there is no fast charging, so it will take about two hours to get back to 100%. But if you're only charging the watch once every week or two, that isn't much of a burden. There's also no charger in the box, so you'll need to use a separate USB-C cable.

Industry observers note that as a smartwatch, the Bip 6 can be a mixed bag. CNET found that the UI was clunky and sluggish, and the OS requires some user intervention before it's as usable as a standard Apple Watch or Galaxy Watch. While the watch has a voice assistant, Flow, CNET found it to be borderline unusable. However, CNET says Android users can reply to texts with a keyboard or dictation without needing the assistant. iPhone users can't do the same by default, but by downloading a third-party app, they can jerry-rig the watch to send and receive texts.

According to recent reports, based on CNET Labs' testing, the Amazfit Bip 6 is one of the best budget smartwatches you can buy. For $80, you get a reliable workout tracker that looks like most standard watches on the market. And while you're making some sacrifices at this price point, they're largely worth it for $80.

Industry observers note that while the Amazfit is a good choice for both iPhone and Android customers, the Galaxy Fit 3 might be the best choice for Samsung users. This isn't an option for iPhone users, and while it works with all Android devices, you get some Samsung-specific perks if you have a Galaxy phone.

The Galaxy Fit 3 is even cheaper than the Amazfit Bip 6: This watch is only $60, which makes it among the cheapest smartwatches you can buy. Now, this doesn't look like your average smartwatch. Samsung opted for a fitness tracker-like design, with a long 1.6-inch (40mm) AMOLED display. But for a fitness tracker/smartwatch hybrid, it's a solid look.

In CNET's testing, one of the Galaxy Fit 3's biggest strengths is its battery life—though it pales in comparison to the Bip 6. When pushed to its limits, the Fit 3 can run three days in between charges, though Samsung claims you can get it up to 13 days with the right settings. While the Amazfit has it beat, the Fit 3 might sound like a dream compared to other smartwatches, even from Samsung. Unlike the Bip 6, the Fit 3 supports fast charging. You can fill the watch up completely in just over an hour.

Sources indicate that CNET did find that the "smart" elements of this wearable were a bit lacking, however. The Fit 3 doesn't support voice dictation or mobile payments like other watches do, and unless you have a Galaxy phone, you won't be able to access the camera remote or sync your alarms. And while the Amazfit Bip 6's "Flow" is hardly reliable, the Fit 3 doesn't have an assistant at all. You can see incoming calls and decline (but not answer) them, and you can send prewritten responses to text messages, but not initiate them. Still, CNET found that Samsung added the essentials: You have an alarm, calculator, weather app, camera remote, and, of course, the Samsung Health app. (What kind of health tracker would this be without it?).

According to recent reports, CNET found that the Fit 3 is a reliable fitness tracker, particularly for $60. You can track over 100 different workouts, and the watch automatically logs exercises like runs, walks, rowing, and elliptical sessions—if you enable auto-tracking, that is. It also supports swimming with its IP68 water resistance rating. CNET Labs found that the heart rate tracking was "generally accurate" when compared to the Polar chest strap, though its slower with registering heart rate spikes. Interestingly, the heart rate tracker was a bit delayed in testing, but once CNET reviewed the data in the health app, the data had corrected to be largely accurate. You also get high and low heart rate alerts, though no ECG app. (The $249 Apple Watch SE 3 also omits this feature.).

In a recent development, in CNET's testing, the sleep tracker on the Fit 3 was useful, if not entirely accurate. The watch can detect your sleep stages and look out for snoring using your Galaxy phone's mic. Like other health trackers, you get a sleep score, but CNET found it a bit inaccurate, since it rated a six and a half hour sleep session "Excellent" (91/100).

Still, the Fit 3 is really the only other smartwatch option at this price point that people should seriously consider. Until another organization drops a product around this MSRP, you have two solid choices in the Amazfit Bip 6 and Galaxy Fit 3.

CEO John Ternus has reportedly been pushing Craig Federighi for faster software development, with specific mention of “moving beyond necessary improvements to Siri,” which seems likely to mean agentic capabilities.

Last week also saw a since-deleted Apple job listing detailing aims for autonomous AI agents.

We’ve already seen some of the ways in which this can go wrong, and we recently outlined three significant risks. Wired reports that banks are now responding to these by either blocking AI agents or warning customers that using them can be dangerous.

Wells Fargo even goes as far as using capitals in its latest terms, stating that it will not be responsible for the consequences.

Your use of any AI Agent is AT YOUR OWN RISK.

We can likely expect similar pushback in sectors like online shopping as companies fear high returns costs and other consequences from mistakes by AI agents.

Personally, I don’t give any AI agents access to any of my banking or other financial services, considering the risks to be too high. I don’t see my position changing any time soon.
